Fisher Price makes multiple versions of these swings. They have diff themes and colors with diff prices. As a buyer you find yourself looking through the different themes and wondering what the differences are. I purchased the Snugabunny and the Snugapuppy to compare first hand since the reviews are all over the place.
First off, Fisher Price swings have a grinding motor noise issues, (after reading this review, Google, "Fisher Price Swing Noise.")
Having a baby, I learned that the point of a swing is to find one with some power, to get a sway going, yes they are just babies but you will find that an aggressive smooth swing will calm a baby down opposed to a low power sway without good range. They want to rock.
Snugapuppy- The motor has a limiter with high friction so that the gears and motors don't grind as loud on start up. So imagine being in a race car, you hit the gas and the breaks are always on so you don't peel out you creep out slowly. But you always hear the rubbing of the breaks, constant friction sound, like a bike tire with the brake applied, that type of rubbing noise that sounds like friction. This swing rubbing noise is constant and never stops. This is not recommended.
The result of the Snugapuppy motor restrictor is the swing range now is not as strong limiting the side to side range, it has less throw and is weaker. The Snuapuppy avoids the Fisher Price motor grinding with this restrictor applied, but now you hear the constant rub of the motor during the entire rocking session. So this solves the startup of the loud grinding motor in the Snugabunny but leaves you with constant rubbing noise with less power and less range, boo. This Snugapuppy swing is being throttled back so the swing will not sway back and forth as well with this model.
Now the other Snugabunny has nice power and good sway because it does not have the motor limiter. So now when you hit the gas, it squeals out for 30 secs which will wake your sleeping baby. But it does not have the rubbing sound once it gets up to speed, but it has clicking and popping sounds from side to side which is bearable for the baby. However, if a parent wants to sleep with the swing in the room at night, this clicking will drive you mad. We do not sleep near this swing, but the baby can tolerate the clicking and popping noise, just not the initial loud grinding and stripping motor start up sounds.

First of all, I wanted to mention that my review may only apply to a specific car application and configuration. My case was mounting the seat in rear facing configuration at the back seat of a sport sedan. However, I didn't notice any issues like that with Graco or Chicco.
The most critical issue, something that in my opinion should warrant a recall, is that after installation, the corners of the child seat base came to a contact with red release buttons of the LATCH clamps. The corners of the base appear to be at an exact width that the LATCH positions are in my car. Upon tightening the strap and pushing lightly down on the seat, the corner of the base pressed the release button and the seat decoupled. It is extremely scary scenario to me. I have an engineering degree and I've thoroughly reviewed the manuals of the car seat and the car. I saw no fault on my side but I did notice something I haven't seen in other car seat manuals. This one actually says that Britax recommends using anchors in addition to LATCH. I am wondering whether Britax is aware of this design issue.

Second issue I've with this car seat is that there is not enough of angle adjustment (3 positions only). When the seat is facing rear it was completely upright in my case, which was probably caused by the deep seats my sport sedan has. I'd need to place something underneath the base to change that angle, like a rolled up towel. Moreover, the straps are actually attached to a reinforcement rail that goes quite high up around the seat. So when you tighten the seat, the forces generated by this lever move the seat even more straight up. Bad design.

Finally, the seat has a safety feature in its base that is a honeycomb structure meant to collapse under downward force during an accident. The problem is that because of where the straps are mounted (around the reinforcement rail) I managed to collapse this structure by tightening the LATCH straps. Again, the lever generated force pushing the seat angle up and seat base area around LATCH down, collapsing the structure.
If you have that seat, I'd carefully inspect whether the base can press on the LATCH release buttons. Overall, I'd not recommend it to anyone.

If you choose to buy this, buyer beware.

UPDATE: Amazon promptly sent me a new machine and this one also started leaking out of the base after a week. The interesting thing is that with the second machine, I was actually adding less water to the metal plate than was recommended (about 85mL instead of the 100mL recommended in the instructions). I did this so there would be absolutely no chance of the water spilling over the edge of the metal plate. Despite this care, the machine worked perfectly for a week, then started leaking everywhere from the bottom. As far as I'm concerned, this is a cheaply and poorly made product.

UPDATE #2: Less than 20 days after receiving the replacement, the sterilizer died in the middle of a cycle. This is a piece of junk. If you choose to purchase they, please keep the box. Thank goodness Amazon is a good retailer and offers free returns no questions asked. It's back to the Avent for us...

In the end, we went through five (yes FIVE) Wabi machines and they each broke in under a few months. The cause appears to be a very low vent that is too close to the plate, no matter how little water you put into the machine. I suspect that somehow water is getting splashed or blown into the vent area and into the electronics area when the machine is in operation. I tried stacking the equipment differently to prevent this from happening but it didn't seem to help. Eventually what would happen to each machine was either it would trip our ground fault outlet or the machine just wouldn't turn on. See my separate review for Baby Brezza, which so far is holding up longer than any of our five Wabi machines.

I can't begin to guess how or why this many people rave about the product. If I had to guess, a lot of the online articles raving about this product are paid plugs by the company and like other reviewers mentioned attributable to a free extra camera thrown in by the seller in exchange for a review. Here's why I think it is WAY overrated.

MAJOR CONS
(1) No VOX/voice-activation or "eco/smart" modes. Beats me why this isn't a standard. Yes, there's an "audio-only" mode. But that is worthless. We have white noise in the baby nursery. So good luck sleeping with a constant audio stream of white noise even if you use that mode. At the very least, you would expect that even the audio-only mode would only turn on when it detects a noise. But nope. Too much to ask for from such a pricey unit!

(2) Extremely finicky buttons: the parent unit has a power button on the top that is SO sensitive to touch that you can't possibly grip this screen in one hand without turning the unit on or off. Poor design

(3) Who the f*** cares about interchangeable lenses really? You guys want to monitor a baby that's sleeping or film a nat geo video? I don't get this meaningless hype over inter-changeable lenses.

(4) No time display on the screen. Nitpicky- but you have no idea how useful it is to display the time along with temp on the screen. Imagine waking up middle of the night and looking at the monitor with no idea what time it is. I mean there's so much screen real estate- add a clock! Again, too much to ask for from a 180$ unit?

(5) Range: This is subjective, your mileage may vary. But this monitor had worse range than a $40 unit I had purchased from amazon before. Seriously. way overrated.

PROS:
(1) Screen size. Loved it. That's it.

CONCLUSION; Save your $$$ get something way cheaper that is actually utilitarian. Don't buy into the hype.

The description says "free from interference from cordless phones, microwaves, game controllers, and even Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices." THIS IS QUITE DECEIVING. I am not sure if the interference is only on the 2.4GHz range or if all of our devices were N and we were on the 5GHz maybe we would be ok??? I don't see what Lorex says what frequency it operates on??

Anyways, we bought this product before the baby came and so our return date has since past. The description claiming free from interference from wifi networks is not true and if you have a home network i would stay away from this product. Even if you have an "n/g" router and all your devices are "n" as soon as you may add one device that is "g" the whole things drops to "g" which is where there is definitely interference.

[[VIDEOID:ef0f1cba0b15a5d0cd109ec9b64eea1e]] I am taking the time to write this review hoping others don’t find themselves in this same situation. I bought this seat so that I wouldn’t have to buy a booster when the time came. My daughter just outgrew this in harness mode so I switched to booster mode. That is where my trouble began. Most boosters have a loop (closed on bottom and overlapping on top) to hold the belt (the seat belt guide). This seat has a belt guide with an open bottom. When you put the seatbelt on, it slides right out of the bottom of the belt guide making it impossible to use in booster mode. I contacted Britax with my complaint hoping in the last two years they had made changes to this design flaw. They blamed my suv. So I tried it in my husbands suv with the same issue then tried it in my mothers car and my fathers truck. All the same issue. Unusable. There might be some that are lucky to enough for this to work in booster mode with their car but it’s definitely an issue. I joined a car seat board and was told it’s a known issue. There are two long protrusions on the left and right side of the tray that should click-in to slots on the chair. Trouble is ,my tray is actually wider than than the slots on the chair, so I have to pull the hard plastic to the left and right by an inch in order for the protrusions to even line-up. I could return and try my luck with another Peg Perego but with baby due in a few weeks, I just want to be DONE with the set-up. Total headache. I'm going back to the drawing board and will just pick a different brand that doesn't have these manufacture errors in the reviews.

Don’t believe the label “flushable”. It’s just a clever marketing trick. The only product that you can safely flush is toilet paper; even paper towels are not safe to flush. Manufacturers can make any claims because there is currently no oversight or certification.

Consumer report tested these claims on flushable wipes. The verdict is “not safe for severs and septic systems”. (See “Are Flushable Wipes Flushable?” by ConsumerReports)

“personal wipes are creating putrid sewage clogs that are costing Canadian ratepayers at least $250 million a year.” (See “'Flushable' wipes clogging Canadian sewers, waste-water officials say" by CBCnews Canada)

“Strong chemicals needed to process bamboo”. (See “Bamboo textiles no more 'natural' than rayon” by CBCnews Canada)

“Bamboo fabric is not biodegradable” (See “Bamboozled? Bamboo Fabric Far From Eco-Friendly, Says FTC” by treehugger)

So if you decide to use this product, just toss it in the garbage bin.

The Baby Brezza bottle washer is a great product! What a luxury to have a little appliance to wash the bottles, pacifiers, and other items. This is the only bottle washer I have ever used. Until the Baby Brezza I have just handwashed or put all baby items in my dishwasher, this product is convenient, because with a baby time is so precious. Here's my review as a mom of a 24 month old.
This product is somewhat large and needs to be set up next to your sink for the drain hose (see photos). Setup of the Baby Brezza is straightforward, but my first time using it I had to follow the manual meticulously to do each step correctly. For example, bottles(depending on the size) have to be positioned correctly for use. You will need liquid dishwashing detergent, which I had to go buy, because I use the pods in my dishwasher. I had difficulty locating the place to put the dishwashing liquid, but finally found it. I washed Nuk Active Sippy cups and a Munchkin sippy cup in it for my first wash (see photo). In the future I will use for pacifiers, all sippy cups, and even stemware. The device has 3 cycles: wash only(40minutes), wash+dry(105minutes), and wash+sterilize+dry(120minutes). There are additional options like sterilize only which takes 20 minutes. And a dry only option. When the machine is in a cleaning cycle it lights up inside with blue LED lights that looks futuristic. It did get a bit loud a certain times throughout the wash, nothing too bad and similar to a dishwasher.
Overall, this is a fabulous luxury baby item that I would have loved back in my Dr Brown's bottle days! Now with my 24 month old I may wash his sippy cups on occasion and use it for his pacifiers, but it would have gotten the most use in our son's first 14 months. The product is pricey, if you can afford it, it's a wonderful item to give you more time with baby!

Alright...so I finally took this out for a stroll today through our County Fair. I've had a jogging stroller since my daughter was a newborn...she's now 2 1/2, but she sadly outgrew it so we needed something. This is what I learned about this stroller in the hour we were at the fair.
1. I was completely spoiled by my jogging stroller!!!! I had a difficult time pushing the Kolcraft through the sand & unevenness of the terrain...including trying to get over the bumps from the all the midway electrical cords. There were a few times I had to back up & realign the front wheels because I felt that had I pushed any more they would have bent & broken.
2. It's incredibly light compared to my old stroller & folds up easily.
3. I'm going to address the backrest because I know LOTS of people have complained about it & it was a HUGE concern to me while reading reviews. While it's not as sturdy as my old stroller, it's not as flimsy as a lot of reviews have stated. There is also a strap that allows you to tighten it, which helps considerably.
4. It's a lot more narrow & shorter than my jogging stroller.
5. The canopy is a good size. It does extend kind of low & I'm not sure if it hinders my daughters view or if it's just her curious nature, but she was playing with it a lot.
Now, with all that said...I do realize that it is a step down from the jogging stroller, BUT is a step up from the tradition umbrella stroller. And I also know...or maybe hope is a better word, that my daughter won't need this for much longer! It serves our purpose...it gets us out of the house, while keeping her safely contained. So for the most part I am happy with it. BUT there is a nagging voice in the back of my head wondering what the Summer 3D Lite is like.

I wanted to like this. My mom insisted I have a video monitor for my son as he starts to become more mobile. We have been using an Angelcare audio monitor that is pretty simple - worked well, but obviously can't see the kiddo.

Setup of the Infant Optics was easy. Popped out of the box and on in no time. Charging was fast and painless. I wanted to just try it first, so I can't speak as to how well it attaches to the wall. We placed it on my son's changing table for the trial run. I set it up around 3:15 today and it was packaged back in its box by 7:30 tonight.

One huge problem I have with it is that the audio isn't voice activated. It isn't even an option, which seems crazy for such an expensive monitor. Both cheaper audio monitors I've owned have at least the option for VOX. My son needs a white noise machine to sleep and we live on a busy road. I don't want to hear his white noise buzzing in my ear on my nightstand all night. I don't need to hear every little breathing noise he makes. I don't want to hear the motorcycles from my window AND his monitor. I just need to hear him if he cries out. The description made reference to some white noise eliminating feature, but it apparently wasn't enough on my unit. Even at the lowest volume setting, I could hear the white noise in the background and every little whimper he made. It was annoying and I missed my completely silent/turned off audio monitor VOX feature. But, I was willing to give it a few nights to see how it affected my sleep. Maybe I'd get over it.

But then there was the deal breaker. I was using my computer next to the monitor and noticed the signal bars moving all over the place every time I clicked on a link while online. The signal was "lost" and one point and it made a loud beeping noise until signal returned. I put the antennae up and thought nothing of it. I left the monitor on my nightstand and went about my evening. Not long after, I started heating up my dinner in the microwave in the next room and I heard the beeping again. I went to the monitor and the signal bars were going all over the place. Up, then down, then no bars, then BEEEEEEP, then some bars, then lots of bars, then no bars, BEEEEEP. I gave it about 5 beeps before I unplugged it, packed it back up, and turned on my Angelcare.

Loud beeping noises next to my head because random electric things are causing it to lose signal? Ain't no(mommy) got time for that.

We bought this almost a year ago for our daughter, who is now 13 months. The number one selling point at the time was the reclining seat, which made it possible for her sit with us at the table before she could eat table food. The second selling point was the amount of space it would take up once it was folded.

The recline is awesome, but that's about it. In order to fold up the chair and keep it folded there's a cheap snap button on one side that keeps the legs up. Ours broke within 3 months, so now when we fold it up and accidentally bump it the legs come crashing down and it really hurts when it hits us. Our solution has been to keep the legs fully extended at all times, which means it's taking up just as much space as any other high chair. The other problem with keeping the legs down is that the legs protrude much farther than the chair, so it's very easy to trip over them. While this doesn't seem like a big problem and it would seem that one would become accustomed to the leg protrusion, you don't because it's so awkward. We are constantly tripping over the legs and my husband's father bruised his toes on them while visiting over the holidays and just about everyone else tripped on them too.

My next problem is with the tray table. It comes with an insert that you can snap into place for easier cleaning or so they say. The main problem with the insert is that it doesn't lie flat so our daughter was constantly pulling it up, which would knock everything onto the floor. Our solution was to remove it and not use it at all. We're currently having to wash the whole tray 3 times a day just like every other high chair.

Last but not least is the ease of cleaning the seat. It's not easy.... it's made out of some strange fabric and the only way to clean it is to throw it in the washing machine. That means when our daughter gets food on the seat and it stains it pretty much has to stay there until the end of the day when there's enough time between feedings to wash it. I'm so annoyed with this chair that I'm currently shopping for a replacement. I would absolutely not recommend this high chair, because you're paying a premium price just to be able to recline the seat, which honestly isn't useful once your child is ready to eat since at that time they need to be upright.

UPDATE: Looks were misleading. The mattress frame that came with our crib doesn't lay flat. It either tilts to one side or the other. At first I assumed it was because I was inverting the frame to make it sit higher, but I just flipped the frame today and it STILL doesn't lay flat. At first, it wasn't a big deal, I just manually leveled the frame myself. However, now that my son is heavier (16 pounds) and rolling over constantly, he's starting to tilt the mattress himself and face plant into the bars. Since it is WELL past any return date, we are stuck either drilling wider holes to compensate or getting another crib. NOT HAPPY. I also do not feel this pine wood is sturdy enough to withstand an enthusiastic toddler... it wobbles. If you were thinking of side-carring your crib, forget it. WIthout the fourth side, it feels like it will snap any second.

This is a beautiful, sturdy, solid wood crib, and it looks just lovely. The wood is a nice, light color, and there was no chemical off-gassing smell at all! Only a slight wood and oil smell. Putting it together was quick and easy, although the pieces weren't labeled, so I had to do some "educated guessing" on which parts were which. It was fairly easy, once I set out the parts. I really liked the way the bolts came prepackaged, so there was no question about which to use. The two, top side rails had a slight chip at their narrowest tips, but I think that's inevitable when shipping such soft wood. The mattress is useless; you will need a real one. For the price, I wasn't expecting a real mattress anyway. I'm only docking one star because I'm not too happy with the spring bottom. It attaches to the wooden crib via these weird metal arms. As another reviewer noted, the only way to get the crib set up at it's highest (newborn) level is to invert these metal swing-arms. So the crib is basically balanced on these 4, angled arms. (Maybe they don't want you setting the crib that high, but many of the manufacturer's pics show it that way, so I think those holes should be drilled). At any rate, that's still not my biggest gripe. The latch design on this gate is needlessly terrible. First and most importantly, it does not automatically latch when you swing it shut - it just bounces right back open again. To latch shut, you have to manually lift up the handle, close it, and push the latch back down while pulling back the gray spring lock to ensure that it actually latches shut. We've had it up for about 6 hours and the puppy has already slipped through twice because someone forgot to turn around and latch it behind them right away. Given how many gates there are on the market that latch automatically, there is just no excuse for this.
As others have mentioned, you also have to choose between sturdiness and functionality - tighten past a certain point and the gate is stuck in the closed position and cannot be opened. I can easily see a determined toddler or overly enthusiastic dog pushing this down because you can't tighten it enough to withstand their efforts.
And finally, WHY can't it open in either direction! Actually I know why - it is due to the same poor design that allows it to become stuck shut when you tighten it too much.

I've now had a chance to "live" with these V Tech units a short time now.  I decided to replace my audio only, decade old "Safety 1st" baby monitor that I bought at a yard sale for $5.  I wanted something new that was modern.  Didn't need a camera to monitor my utility room.  So I bought the V Tech DM111, expecting a lot from this manufacturer.  What a disappointment.  It not only doesn't hear much above a shout, but you can't turn the receiver loud enough to hear anything.  It hears the telephone great.  The phone is located 3 inches away from the transmitter.  Can't hear the water heater start and heat that is only 2 feet away.  Or the water softener go through it's cycles which is 4 feet away.  Of the freezer come on.  Nor the window air conditioner.  Nor water in the shower when it's running.  The "Safety 1st" baby monitor hears all these items.  Plus I can turn the "Safety 1st" receiver volume up loud enough to hear even the slightest sound.  My Wife has bone on bone hip joints and is subject to falling.  Should she fall, I'd never hear her unless I should happen to hear her scream through the walls.  Fortunately I don't have a baby.  Unless the child picked up the transmitter and yelled into it, I doubt you could hear it elsewhere in the house.  One receiver is located about 22 feet from the transmitter.  Another receiver is located about 40 feet from the same transmitter.  So you're thinking maybe I have a bad unit.  Sorry.  The two V Tech DM111 units act the same.  Also another V Tech DM111-2 (two receivers) does the same.  And moving the units around solves nothing.  Wish I could purchase an additional "Safety 1st" device.  I consider these V Tech units just about worthless---for my purposes.  Keeping an ear out to listen to older adults does not work either.  If your baby doesn't raise the roof when it cries, forget it.  And should it quietly start to choke, you won't hear a thing.  I expected a LOT MORE from V Tech.  BIG mistake.  You've been warned.  Good luck.

Let me start by saying I am normally a big fan of Chicco products. I used the Chicco Bravo travel system (with Keyfit 30 car seat) for my baby when he was a newborn, and it was first rate. I'm still using the stroller from that system, but I wanted something lighter and easier to maneuver now that my little guy is a bit older. I am also using the Nextfit Zip convertible car seat, which is outstanding on every level, probably the best in its class.

The Liteway stroller has a few bafflingly bad design choices, and I know that Chicco knows better, having made other far superior products. So I am writing this review in the hopes that someone on their staff will take note and make improvements for the next iteration.

The worst offender here is the straps. The harness is of the "put the puzzle together" variety, which is HORRIBLE. Having to fit the pieces together while trying to prevent a writhing, pissed-off toddler from escaping and running into the street adds completely unnecessary stress to the already taxing lives we moms lead. There is no conceivable advantage to having this type of harness. And, to add insult to injury, the pieces don't click together well, and the plastic loop that you have to fit the longer piece into (with the teeth that clicks into the crotch strap) is inexplicably open on one end, so it sometimes pops out multiple times before you can get it snapped in place. Terrible, terrible, terrible design. There is no excuse for something like this on what is supposed to be a high end product from a top class company. The straps are a total deal breaker for me.

The stroller is also about 5 lbs too heavy to call itself "lite". It's only a few pounds lighter than the behemoth stroller from the travel system, so it's not really that easy to carry. And they only give a flimsy cloth handle on the side for carrying, instead of the much more useful shoulder strap you see on other strollers in this class.

The two-step folding process isn't particularly smooth or easy, and half the time you have to bend down and manually push the latching mechanism into place or else the thing will pop back open again. Again, this is an unnecessary extra step to have to take when you are trying to also wrangle a toddler.

There is also no conceivable reason why this was constructed to have a 40lb weight limit. Other strollers in this class have much higher weight limits and are not heavier or bulkier as a result. So there's no excuse for it to have such a limited useful life.

Finally, the flimsy cloth hood is really sub-par. It should be a nice UV-treated nylon with a peek-through window or mesh, like they have on the travel system.

It's too bad that this product has so many major flaws, because there's alot about it that they got right. The seating area is nicely padded, and seems more comfortable than other strollers of this type. Overall the thing feels sturdy and well made, and it handles nicely. I also appreciate the fact that the seat bed lies completely flat, which is a nice feature even for an older baby like mine. He's now almost 17 mos and he still likes to lie down and relax. It's also really nice-looking, like all the other Chicco products, and the cupholder is a particularly handy size. All it needs to be perfect are a one-click harness system, one-step folding mechanism, a better hood, and to lose 5lbs.

Chicco usually makes fantastic products, but in my opinion they made some unacceptably poor design choices on this stroller, so I hope they come out with a revised version that is more thoughtfully crafted with ease of use in mind.

As someone who lost a child to a furniture tip-over (yes it happens, in fact tip overs send a child to the ER every 45 minutes!), I test anchors frequently. With so many on the market it's hard to tell which one is the best. This one is not it. It's a great idea, but like 99% of other anchors on the market, they are not tested for safety! My 155lb husband's weight was enough to break the steel cable with a straight line force before he even applied his full weight. You may think that's crazy, my kid doesn't weigh that much, but it's about physics, not just weight.

In order to prevent a tip-over, the anchor has to hold the weight of the furniture, whatever is in/on it, and the weight of a child climbing, hanging, or otherwise applying forces to the furniture to cause it to become unstable and tip. This often adds up to 100 pounds or more, depending on the furniture and the weight of the child and how they are using the dresser. The steel cable is great for luggage tags, but NOT safe for anchoring furniture. It's important to note anchors also have to be in solid wood, not drywall. All metal anchors are better than ones that contain plastic, but they also have to work. I recommend the Hangman furniture anchor or L brackets you can get at the hardware store with long screws instead of this style of anchor.

We have a hound dog that is pretty agile and has no trouble jumping over our normal gates, so I decided to try this "extra tall" gate. First, I should say the size is pretty good; it is certainly tall enough that I'm doubtful our dog would attempt the jump. But that is where the praise for this product ends. I don't often bash a product, but this gate was beyond terrible.

It installs similarly to a couple of DreamBaby gates we already have (which are very good, by the way). Only, it doesn't work. If tightened enough that it is firmly in place, the door will not open. It has to be loosened slightly to leave a large enough gap between the door and the gate's frame that the door can swing out. But when it is loosened just enough to allow the door to open, it simply falls down. Literally. My dog could knock this gate over by breathing on it.

Even if it worked, the quality is still pretty crummy. The door latch is not all that simple or quick to operate, and, unless I'm missing something, the latch allows the door to open in only one direction. The latch is plastic and feels cheap; I certainly would not expect it to stand up to continued, regular use. Even the metal gate is a bit suspect--the welds are sloppy (though not necessarily weak), and the gate feels lighter than it should (which could be a plus for some, but I worry that it indicates thin and insubstantial metal).

I'm going to send this back and try DreamBaby's tall gate. Update #2 (May 2020, 2.5 yrs of use): The monitor now will only work if plugged in. It no longer holds charge long enough to beep at us, which is concerning if the power were to go out (it would turn off silently). We're going to get a new monitor from a different company.

Update #1 (Fall 2019, 2 yrs of use): We've been using this monitor for almost two years, and for the last year, we've been having a lot of problems with the monitor and its rechargeable battery. It loses charge very quickly, and the monitor will immediately start beeping at us (low battery) after an entire night of it being charged. Sometimes, if I unplug and then reconnect the battery connection within the monitor, it fixes the problem, but often it does not. The battery is lithium-ion, which in my understanding, means that it shouldn't be allowed to stay at full capacity (plugged in) for a long time. However, it won't stay charged through the night while unplugged, so I have to keep it plugged in. Perhaps this is the reason we're having such a difficult time with the battery? Either way, it seems like a design flaw. The battery life should last through the night unplugged, or is a battery that won't be damaged from being plugged in all night. After having seen the baby monitor my sister uses, I know this one isn't the top of the line in battery life or in image quality/clarity on the monitor (much more pixelated than my sister's monitor).

Please also note that the add-on wide-angle lens (for when your baby is a toddler and you need to monitor the whole room) is pretty low quality as well. Read the reviews for that product so you're well informed about the ability to use this product long-term. I wish we had bought a baby monitor from a different company.

We received this as a gift from our registry. We thought this would be a terrific and convenient crib for our first child. We were sorely mistaken. The brass latches cannot be screwed in all the way; otherwise, they don't catch as intended. This weakens the structure already. Secondly, the bolts included do not thread securely into the side walls of the crib as shown in the instructions. Both washers were placed on the bolt as instructed and the correct bolt was threaded through the hole. Then when I brought the side wall up, labeled as section C in the instructions, the bolt simply slid right into the hole with no effort. This is unacceptable and shows very poor craftsmanship as it is literally impossible to secure the crib and is therefore unusable and deadly to an infant. How this passed QA is beyond me. Furthermore, there are screws included in the package that appear nowhere in the instructions, either by description/illustration or by what they're used for. Also the illustrations of the 5/8" screws do not match the actual screws included with the package. Somehow Fakespot rates this an A, which is very disappointing. For the sake of your sanity and your child's safety, stay far away from this product. Also, for those who blame age being the limiting factor of understanding the included instructions, I'm 30 and have worked in IT for over 10 years. I received this pump through insurance, and I figured that free is always good. I was an idiot. I started pumping when my daughter turned one month old. For the first month or so this pump worked well. I was able to get many ounces in a fairly short period of time. I was pumping about twice a day at that point (morning and night) to build up a stash. However, shortly before my maternity leave ended this pump started making a slightly weird noise in the motor and the suction didn't seem as good. Upon my return to work last month, this pump has been horrible. I pump three times a day at work and also in the morning and night (for a total of 5 sessions) and I'm lucky if I get three ounces total at each pumping session, at nearly 30 minutes a piece! Yes, I spend nearly two hours every single day using this machine, to get maybe 15 ounces total. At first I thought it was a supply issue and starting drowning myself in Fenugreek and Mother's Milk, but then realized that this pump is the issue. I've replaced all the tubing and valves but there's been no change. This pump sucks, but unfortunately not literally. Here's a breakdown of why:

Pros:
1. Free
2. Closed system means no worries about mold
3. Cheaper than the comparable alternatives

Cons:
1. Motor slowly dying after 3 months of use (only one month of heavy use). A common complaint from the reviews on here.
2. Loud- I'm embarrassed to pump at work.
3. Closed system in theory, but I commonly find milk up in the diaphragm, which means it can get into the tubing easy.
4. About twice a day I have to stop in the middle of a pumping session because the diaphragm won't fully expand. It's easily corrected by popping off the caps and repositioning them.
5. Milk constantly leaks from underneath flange. I have to hold a burp cloth underneath every single time I pump, and even then I end up with milk on my pants at times.
6. Nearly impossible to use hands-free. Because the flange is attached you either have to stretch out the opening of your bra to use hands free or just don't do hands free. Even if you stretch out the opening, the suction (even when it was brand new and functioning at its best) wasn't strong enough to keep the flanges properly in place.
7. Calling it a "double" electric is a joke. First off, read #5 above. Second off, the suction is so poor that trying to split the power between two makes it even more ineffective. Because of this I spend a large part of my work day pumping one side at a time.

I've read reviews that state that their customer service is awesome. I plan to call them soon to address my issues, but I guess because this pump is still technically "working", I'm lazy and am trying to procrastinate on the hassle of it. Regardless if their customer service is amazing, I'd still rate this one star because of serious design flaws and the fact that there's no acceptable excuse why this pump is failing so miserably in such a short period time.

WARNING: Do not buy these brackets unless you buy your own screws. While the brackets themselves are great, the screws are crap. You will need sheet metal screws (not wood) size #6 x 3/4" and #6 x 1-1/2” as exact replacements for what comes in the package.

STORY: I am a handywoman and have used these brackets before when they came in a box with some furniture I assembled for a client. They worked great, so I recommended them to another client for some furniture he and his wife had. Little did I know that recommendation would come back to haunt me.

I came out to install them and had nothing but problems with the crappy screws they provided. One after another snapped off while trying to drive them into the furniture and the wall studs. The metal was brittle so they simple sheared even with pre-drilling the holes. See the attached pictures showing the broken heads.

I called the company and explained to them what happened. In addition, I asked to get some kind of a credit to my client for their trouble because they had to pay me for my time regardless. Not only that I had to make a second trip out after purchasing some decent screws from Home Depot. I got zero cooperation for the effort except that they would replace them so my clients are out the money from two visits not to mention sheared screws in their furniture.

Now I have to spend time mailing back the screws for testing and there is nothing in it for me or my client other than hopefully it will eventually prevent someone else from getting “screwed” by this product. So much for good will towards clients when you produce a defective product.

Fine, this warning will be my pound of flesh.

I mean, if you plan on going through this gate carrying anything, or if you happen to be a slightly rounder person, this is going to be a problem. The opening is exactly 16 1/2". I did my research before buying the Summer Infant Day and Night monitor. It seems like many people opt for this monitor and it got mostly good reviews so I figured I would try it out.

At first, I did like the monitor. The picture is very clear, even at night. And the range is pretty good, I could go outside and still get a pretty good signal for video/audio.

Right away, I noticed something very STRANGE: I occasionally saw a different crib!! I tried the other channel, but the other channel's signal was not as good. Seeing the other baby's crib happened when the reception for my channel wasn't as good. I live in a townhome, but I know for a fact that there are no babies in cribs in my building or in the building next to me. It might be a building across the street?!

At first I thought I could live with that since otherwise it was a good monitor, but as I thought about it, I became more uncomfortable with the idea. Someone may occasionally be able to see my son. This is not safe at all. I don't want some random stranger being able to see my son's room, his routine, what he looks like, etc. Plus, at night I go into my son's room in a shirt and underwear.

If you don't mind other people being able to peep into your house, then this is a good monitor, otherwise, opt for a digital monitor that is more secure. We will be returning this one asap.

I wanted to love my Uno, because I really wanted the versatility that it offers, but it is a very disappointing product overall. I want to be very specific about the problems with the stroller, so bear with me on the length of the "bad"! :)

First, the good:

It can be used as a carriage/pram, a backward-facing stroller, forward-facing stroller or with your Peg Perego car seat. It also has an adjustable handle for users of different heights. It comes with a "boot" for providing a nice, warm place for baby in the winter. One-hand braking. Very cute pattern (Green Bubbles) that I constantly get compliments on. Nicely padded handle.

Now, the bad:

The biggest deal-breaker flaw for this product are the wheels. It has two stationary and two swivel. When used in the regular, forward-facing stroller position or with the infant car seat attached, the swivel wheels lock up on any smooth surface. They will roll over cement/gravel just fine, but inside a store or mall they are constantly locking up and the entire stroller jerks to a halt, waking the baby. You have to lean down on the handle and lift the front end off the ground a little in order to get it rolling again. It's a traction problem, not a wheel problem. The wheels spin freely when you lift them, it is just that they are made of sort of soft rubber and the wheels get stuck on smooth tile or linoleum flooring (like that which you find in most grocery stores, Target, etc.). The stationary wheels are just annoying because when you are using it in the carriage/pram position, it is hard to maneuver. Another flaw is that the one-hand brake design doesn't work all that well. You have to squeeze REALLY hard to engage it, but once engaged you can lock into place. However, the wheel will still move so you have to lock the second set of brakes manually in order to get it to be stationary. The five-point harness is also odd because the straps do not go through the seat back as in most other strollers, car seats, or high chairs. Instead it just hooks on to the seat behind the child. This is supposed to be great for toddlers because you can unhook it and they can have greater range of motion while still being securely fastened in, but it is horrible for little babies because the hook is right behind their head. The last very minor flaw is the cupholder. It is NOT a cupholder, but rather a slim water bottle holder.

Because of the issues I have had with the stroller, I don't use it at all. Unfortunately for me, I got it while I was still pregnant and was outside of the return period before it became clear that it is pretty much unusable for me (I only really need to use it when I am going shopping, and it won't work in department stores or grocery stores). Because it is a design flaw and nothing wrong with the stroller, there is nothing that Peg Perego can do for me either.

You're supposed to be able to use recline level 2 or 3 for a rear facing child. Level two is so upright that my child is constantly falling forward against his harness when he is sleeping. Level 3 is fine, but the seat is so large that the passenger seat in front must be moved very far forward to accommodate the giant size of the recline of this car seat.

Finally, the harness will not tighten or loosen without feeling like its getting pinched somewhere. Reading the 1 star reviews I am both happy and sad to read I am not the only one that has this issue. This seat does have one bonus, which is the fact that the back of the seat exposes the harness, so to get my child in the car, I have to manually pull the harness tight from the BACK of the seat, and then tighten the slack with the 'tail' at the bottom front of the seat.

The cup holders are molded from some kind of rubbery plastic, where the seam of the mold is still visible and little fringes of plastic spill out from the seam. It looks messy and cheap, and the cup holders are semi flexible, not rigid plastic.

I got the Graco Extend2Fit for my husbands car, and for only $19 more I got a far superior seat that looks and functions as it should.

At first, this video baby monitor was awesome. My wife and I would bring the monitor upstairs so that we could watch television for a little while before we went to bed, and we always ended up just watching our son over the monitor instead. The night vision was not bad for low-light, and when our son took daytime naps, the color picture was very good. The sound was good quality, and we liked that we could turn a few lullabyes on and off from upstairs. The range was also very good.

But.

When we went to visit some family about two and a half months after buying the monitor, we set it up and I realized about half an hour later that the picture looked as if it hadn't changed at all. I went to go check on my son (the room we were stayign in was on the other side of the house), and he was crying miserably. You'd never know by the picture frozen on the screen!

We tried repeatedly to use the monitor after that day, but it never worked well again. After reading several other reviews here, it seems as if the same thing happened to several other consumers. For well over $100, this unit should be working as well as it did at first for several years, not 75 days. We were (and remain) very disappointed with the product.

There's no way I'm going to have it on in baby's room--I don't want to bother her and if she doesn't sleep soundly, then neither will I.

Disclaimer: my ears hear high sounds much better than most everyone I know. There's a good chance you will plug your monitor in and not hear a thing. I REALLY wanted to like these. I’ve been cloth diapering for almost a year and currently have two in diapers full time. leaks happen. especially overnight. And these promised more absorption. A new hybrid special system. So I gave it a shot.

The diaper is like a plain shell with a little sling to hold the inserts. The sling means the inserts can be held in place without snaps (so you can theoretically use any insert) and they don’t move out of position while putting it on a wiggly booty. The sling isn’t attached in the middle to the cover and is fully water proof. That means the outer shell can remain ‘untouched’ if you change it soon enough. You would just wipe the sling and put in a new insert. That’s the great thing about plain covers and inserts. And since the sling keeps it in place you avoid the insert falling out of place while wrestling the diaper onto your kiddo. The sling also functions as a double gusset. Some people love double gussets- they prevent leaks and spray clean easily. I do not. They pinch my kiddos and when I spray them I get sprayed back (unpleasant considering what you spray off).

As for the actual inserts and covers: there are different fabric options FOR THE SHELL- the part that doesn’t touch baby skin. The inserts are pre-folds made mostly of polyester. Polyester is horrible! You really want cotton or bamboo- microfiber and polyester just don’t breathe and that’s a sensitive area. Plus polyester doesn’t absorb as much as other options (like hemp or bamboo infused microfiber) These do come with a booster pad and disposable boosters which help.
Then there’s the size issue. These diapers are not one size fits all with ways to adjust as baby grows. These diapers have sizes like traditional disposables. Thankfully the inserts have some overlap (the inserts I have are labeled 3/4 while the shells clearly say one or the other). These things are expensive. You need at least 14 diapers per kiddo and with this diapering system that’s 14 per kiddo, per size?!
The box says these diapers are fashionable, and the solid colors are nice. But generally speaking you don’t see the diapers and you can get all kinds of cool prints and patterns in any brand of cloth diaper.

These use a velcro closure instead of snaps. Velcro means you get a snugger fit. These have a special tab to fold them to when you wash so they don’t get stuck to each other and tangled up- a very nice touch. Velcro also wears out faster than snaps.

And with that we come to the ‘eco-friendly’ claim… Cloth diapers reduce landfill waste. They also add a lot more waste water and detergent use. This diaper system has disposable pads- claiming those pads use less plastic than a traditional disposable diaper and are more convenient while traveling… But it’s still waste? They’re wrapped in plastic? It’s supposedly less waste but you’re still buying something to throw away when you’ve invested (quite a bit) in things you can reuse… it just seems counterproductive. Plus if you want to reduce waste why would you design a system that promotes it in how you handle sizing?

All in all these are just disappointing. My kiddos have a rash now and I would not recommend.

We bought this to replace a single camera from a Summer model. We used it reliably for our first child from 3 months to 2 years 4 months. When we had our second child we wanted a monitor with two cameras. Here is a list of the things we liked and didn't like.

The video quality is really good.

The audio is irritating and the auto mute feature is unreliable. It is difficult to understand when the VOX is working and when it isn't.

The base and swivel features for the camera is clunky. We had to mount the 2nd camera on the wall to get a view on the crib. Our last Summer camera was so flexible we could wrap the wire around the corner of the crib and find a way to point it without putting screws in the wall.

The second camera paired easily enough and worked great. Then it stopped working. I even reconfigured my WiFi router to different channels in case that was causing interference - but to no avail. This is the entire reason we purchased this system, so if I cannot rely on the 2nd camera the whole system is useless to me.

If you have more than 1 camera and less than 4, you have to scroll through the unused camera channels to get back to the cameras that you are using. That is a dumb design - if the other channels are unused there should be a means to disable them. If one kid starts crying suddenly at 3 AM, I don't see how you can have to have the presence of mind to patiently scroll through channels until you get to the one you want... that's just ridiculous. I know that when I shoot out of bed in the middle of the night I'm rarely logical or patient.

It does feel light and flimsy, unlike the Summer Slim & Secure that we've had for >2 years.

Given the other reviews on here that cite interference problems (assuming that is what is causing my 2nd camera to fail the connection) it would seem that this product fails to do what it says it should do. I never had any problems with the Summer, but this is quite unsatisfactory.

Constant Ads (feels like daily)… the Nanit app that you use to view your camera is constantly serving ads - I’ve emailed the company and they’ve said there’s no way at all to disable them. They said they’d forward it to the design team in case they make a change in the future. It probably doesn’t annoy people as much as it does for me, but the problem doesn’t end at the constant ad serving, but there isn’t a way to close the ads (no visible “X” to close), and they pop up over the buttons to control the features of your app, microphone, or adding music). Essentially if you want to click one of those buttons, you have to click on the ad, and then “X” out of the ad once the page loads, and when you go back, then the ad disappears. Here are just a few, “Sign up for another yearly subscription… $_______”, “join this community”, “upgrade to Nanit insights”, “unlock sleep analytics with Nanit insights”… and on and on.

Camera quality is average. I’ve had multiple home security cameras over the years and the quality ranks to some cameras I had in 2012 (not great). The camera is about 5 feet above the crib and his face is still a little blurry. None of the security cameras I’ve purchased over the past 5 years (about 12 cameras) have a quality at this low of a level. They get blurry at about twice the distance.

If they could fix the camera quality I’d add another star. And if they could fix the ad serving, I’d add another star. But for the price (and if you buy a stand later which is about $150 for the stand only, no camera), this product can’t get to5 stars (my security cameras that have about twice the quality are around $100).

We had a Summer infant video monitor for our oldest daughter and then used it for our middle daughter. We would still be using it for our third daughter, but after 6 years it finally stopped working properly. We did not want to spend a great deal of money, so after many hours of reading reviews and looking at many video monitors we bought this one. I was very excited when we received it and it worked great for during the day, but things all changed at night. Our daughter sleeps with a white noise machine and the monitor picks that noise up, so it is very loud. We tried turning the VOX sensitivity down, the monitor would not turn on when she cried. We woke up to a screaming 4 month old who was soaked in her tears, which made me feel terrible. I noticed that the power light on the camera was shining right in her eyes, so we decided that she would sleep back in our room for the night. The next night we covered the power button with tape and left the camera on all night. The camera is very bright, so I had to turn it away from me while I was sleeping. Our daughter does not cry very loud, so it is very difficult to hear her over the white noise. When we did have the VOX on the camera turns on and off all the time because of the white noise. We are very disappointed, so we are sending it back. We need a camera that lets us sleep with our baby in another room and not have to worry about not hearing her or being kept awake because the monitor is so bright and loud. Let the research for another monitor begin!!

The app is very easy to use. I am not sure if other cameras allow you to move the camera from the app, but it is manual to move the camera. One thing I do not understand/like is when you are looking at the feed it is not as wide as it actually has the capability of showing you. I know this because I took a video, using the feature on the app, and I saw more of my son than I could through normal use. It is very odd to me and I wish I could see more. Perhaps there is some kind of user error?

I will update this after it has been longer than one day.

Update:
The latest software update makes the camera useless. Takes several minutes for the green dot to appear meaning I can view my child. It's always been a pain and hasn't gotten better. - The pail started rusting after 7-8 months.
- It is not convenient to open and close the lid with hand. Better to have a pail that can open with stepping on it.
- Due to its design, you get an assault on your senses every time you open the pail. The room fills with poo smell just within the second you open its lid, put diaper bag and close it back. There are other brands that figured out this problem by "trapping" the smell when you open the lid.

This is a great looking crib and designed well to go through different phases of your child's early years. It's sturdy and relatively easy to put together. It took my husband and I about an hour to put together, but make sure to pay close attention to the placement of the holes on each side of the crib in the directions.

The reason for the 2 star review? The crib calls for a standard crib mattress (roughly 27.5" W x 52"L), however the instructions included with the crib state "any mattress used in this crib must be at least 27 1/4 inches by 51 5/8 inches. Thinking the mattress would be the least of our worries, we went to a big box baby store and purchased a mattress listed as 52" L x 27.5" W x 6" H. When we got home, we placed the mattress in the crib, but lo and behold, there was about an inch and a half gap between the crib and the mattress, when the mattress was pushed to one side of the crib. I've read numerous reviews saying that the mattress should be a snug fit in the crib. Being a first time nervous mom, I was not okay with the gap and the idea of my soon to be born child getting her limbs stuck between the crib and the mattress. The mattress was nowhere near a snug fit (and crib bumpers are out of the question), so back to the store it went. We spoke to one of the sales people at the store and they mentioned that a lot of crib manufacturers who also manufacture mattresses, will make their cribs slightly larger (or smaller) than normal so you're forced to buy their mattress. I should've not ignored that little anecdote.

I searched high and low for a new, wider mattress, but the best I could find was one that claimed to be 28" wide. It was listed as 28" wide every site it was listed on, so I was convinced it was 28" wide. When it arrived, I placed it in the crib, and it turned out to be 27 1/4" wide. It was even worse than the first mattress. Thank goodness for free returns on Amazon, because that's going back.

The third and final mattress I tried, I bit the bullet and purchased the Babyletto Pure Core Air mattress. There weren't very many reviews on it online but I decided to try my luck one more time. When the mattress arrived, I unpacked it, and placed it in the crib, and guess what? It was a perfect fit. No gaps, no sliding around, no nothing.

It seems that others who've reviewed the crib here have had varying luck on mattresses fitting, but I was one of the unfortunate ones who got a dud - in terms of size. Thankfully the Babyletto mattress was a perfect fit, but I found it annoying that all other "standard" sized mattresses slid around.

UPDATE July 2018
We're still using this crib after three years, but now as a toddler bed. It continues to serve its intended purpose as a place for my child to sleep in. When my daughter was teething, she gnawed at the rails and did some damage to the paint. I contacted Babyletto directly for a touch up kit that is mentioned on their site was sent a standard white paint pen you can find on Amazon. I was expecting a better match in paint.

I've had this pump for a little over 7 months; I received mine through my insurance (didn't purchase from Amazon), but I own the freestyle model. From day 1, I experienced a loss of suction on the pump at least every other time I'd use it. The suction on this pump is so bad that I went out and purchased several spare replacement parts (tubing, valves, etc), hoping that this would solve the issue. It didn't. This device has really been a disappointment. Sometimes it works like it's supposed to and I have no issues, but at least 50% of the time, it doesn't. This can range from being a minor inconvenience during the day to becoming completely infuriating at 2am when you have to swap out a part to try and fix the problem. I wouldn't purchase another one of these pumps due to the inconsistency in suction.

The fact is, if you're doorframe isn't perfectly lined up, then this gate ends up being a lot more difficult to mount. Despite reading the instructions (and understanding them), grasping the handle and pressing the buttons just doesn't work well. The internal locking mechanism seems to lock or impact against itself, meaning that the handle ends up not going up or down when you want it to. This is the problem and why the gate is so difficult to use, at least when it's pressure mounted. With some fidgeting (and in my case, a lot of sitting and kneeling), you can get it mounted and it will stay put pretty well, but for a product that's billed as being easy to use, it's hard to recommend when that's a major selling point. Using the included mounting hardware might make this a much better product, but if you want to use it with the pressure mount method, you may want to explore other options.

I don't normally return used unit, but in this case i have to since it actually broke. i bought a Papablic ones instead. so here is my impression on this unit, compared to the highly rated papablic ones.

pro:
1. both unit are very large, the gourmia one, being rounded, is probably able to fit more than Papablic. it has 8 bottle vs 6. even though i only use two at a time (with pump attachments, so 4 pieces total), I see the larger volume will be advantageous.
2. rounded size means you don't have to care too much about lid orientation (papablic lids are directional)

con:
this is pretty serious ones
1. Leaking. the issue is with the design. the heating element is FLAT, meaning if you fill the water at the max capacity of the heater, when it boils, the water will leak through the seams. i don't mean you overfill so that water leak though the drying fan, i mean the seams.
2. seams: the heating element is pressed against the plastic, which create a seam. as the heating cycle goes, it can develop leak though the system. the leak was slow and isn't immediate, and could keep leaking even after the unit finishes the cycle. because it is slow and you cannot see it until you move the unit, it has ruined my wooden dressing table completely in the 2 weeks i used it. while i felt pretty salty since the table was thousand dollars and i have to replace the table top, this is a huge design flaw. compared to papablic where the heating element is surrounded by silicon seals, this unit's design is definitely flawed.
3. noise. the dryer fan is so loud that i cannot sleep when it is turned on, the papablic is much quieter.
4. control: the all digital control SUCKS. you can only choose the pre programmed interval. the sterilizer runs for 10 min (or until the water is boiled), and the drying function runs for 40, 50 or 60 minutes. there are two issues with it
a. when the water gets in (which mine unit did). the control malfunctioned. specifically, the drying function keep running all night and the count down simply dosn't work.
b. often times, you don't need to dry 40, 50 or 60 minutes. my use case only requires 15 to 20 min max. with papablic, you simply dial to set the amount of time, this one? you have to shut down the unit manually.

so with all that being said, i cannot recommend this unit over papablic. in fact, i would recommend against buying this unit.

I ordered Graco SnugRide for a baby shower present through a Target Gift Registry, processed through Amazon. It was shipped to me in the same thin single-ply cardboard box you buy it in stores. The box is very large and flimsy. It arrived with the box seriously dented on all sides, hardly worthy of presentation. But worse, when I opened it up, I found a 2 inch white stress line in the plastic, where apparently the beige plastic of the car seat (which seems fairly thin) was over stressed during shipping. The box had no padding inside whatsoever, the car set is simply wrapped in a plastic cover. I've done a lot of shipping, and I know you have to have 2 inches or more of padding on all sides, or double boxing, and a box this large should be double corrugated for strength.

It was convenient to be able to return the car set at a local Target store, but I was not refunded the shipping cost of $15, even though it was very clearly the faulty packaging by Amazon/Target that caused the unit to get damaged. I was also informed that Target does not carry the item in their stores, so it is only available through mail order. I'm going to try to find some other local seller.

The Super Saurus model in the Gift Registry that I ordered is apparently in the premium line of SnugRide car seats, having the "GracoPedic" foam padding for comfort (in addition to the EPS which is in all Snug Rides for safety). I wouldn't buy one of these without the GracoPedic foam. Baby should not be resting on the hard plastic (oh, well, maybe the plastic isn't that hard anyway). I think they should all come with the extra GracoPedic foam (though reportedly it doesn't hold up to washing), or at least it should be mentioned on the box. But it didn't mention the GracoPedic foam on the box, I only learned it from a review, and it is hard to tell otherwise.

For a top-rated product like this, I was not impressed by the thin plastic construction, which looks and feels cheap and flexible. more like a toy than a car safety device. And if you look at the 1-star reviews, these things can break in normal use, which I don't find reassuring. But I'm not sure what if anything is actually better than this from a safety perspective, as long as you replace it at the first sign of damage so it doesn't actually come apart in use.

I have super-sensitive skin that’s prone to eczema outbreaks, so I thought a product intended for babies with sensitive skin might be gentle enough for me. I was initially a bit surprised that this product is scented—I’m accustomed to products for sensitive skin being fragrance-free as well—but the scent is mild and doesn’t bother me.  My first impression of the lotion was relatively positive. As long as my skin was in decent condition to begin with (i.e., no significant eczema to speak of), this lotion seemed to do its job, moisturizing without problems.

Then came the day when my hands became bright red and painful within minutes of applying this product. A strange coincidence, I thought, since I had been using it without trouble for several days by that point. Maybe it was some sort of delayed reaction to the meal I’d eaten several hours before? I didn’t think much of it, though I did stop using the lotion for a while.  And then it happened again. My skin started to tingle and burn almost immediately after applying this lotion. This time, I was quick to take action; I immediately rushed to the sink and washed it off as much as possible. I put on my go-to Aveeno moisturizer instead, and the problem was greatly reduced.  So my conclusion is that this lotion isn’t really for super-sensitive skin. I can use it when my hands are in good shape, but it leads to a negative reaction when my skin is at its most sensitive. I’ll be sticking to my tried-and-true Aveeno in the future.

*The recline is impressive and easy to do, with a lever rather than the infinite recline straps that many strollers have.
*The basket is very spacious for an umbrella stroller.
* The straps are a generous size.

The cons:
* It is INCREDIBLY long when folded. I would not travel with this thing, if you paid me. It also doesn't have a standing fold. So its like travelling with skis.
*It is very uncomfortable to carry when folded. In part due to its' folded dimensions.
* The harness buckle comes apart into 5 separate pieces. It is very difficult to fasten with a still child. I'm imagining an episode of America's funniest home videos with this thing as a starring role.

My 3 year old daughter started waking at night months ago and would come in our room.  We tried to deal with this different ways and decided to try this cute clock.  My daughter was really upset at first because she wanted to still come in our room but quickly liked the cute bunny. And I liked that it plugged in so I new there wouldn't be batteries that died in the middle of the night. However, the set up on this is horrible!  I could set the clock time (which is so tiny and does not light up) but I could not set the wake time correctly. The bunny was always sleeping, which is preferred if it's going to be stuck in one of the positions, but it should wake up. I could not figure out how to do an AM setting, it was only displaying PM. With a combination of good parenting and this dimmer nightlight (her other nightlight was pretty bright) actually did get her to sleep through the night. But I've decided to return it and get the Onaroo instead.  The Onaroo was easy to set up and actually works. It has a bigger time display that lights up so now she can tell me what time it is.  The only downside to the Onaroo is that it is only battery operated. I thought since the night light turns off after a while (to save energy) it would be a problem, but my daughter didn't wake up scared during the night when it was dark. Overall, a night/day clock of any kind is a good option, but one that actually works is preferred.

In theory, the thermometer is great. Loved that there were 3 settings - forehead, ear, and room. I also like how if the temp is high it turns red with the reading, and the carry case that comes with it. But for how expensive it was, I expect it to be accurate! I understand that there is a difference between readings depending on where it is taken. But this was more than just that.

My 3 month old baby had her first fever today. She was fussy and her forehead was very warm. I took her forehead temp first and it read 99.8. Then her ear read much lower. Weird, I thought, so I tried forehead again. It was then within the normal range. The temperature kept changing from one minute to the next.

I called the pediatrician to make an appointment, and waited an hour until we had to leave. I decided to try the temp again before we left - her ear read 102.6 and her forehead was normal. At the pediatrician, her rectal temp was 101. I took the temp in the office and it read 100.5 ear, 99.9 forehead. This was the closest they had been to each other. She then got some Tylenol.

Back at home, when it came time for her next dose, I decided to try again to see. She felt less hot to the touch than before. Her forehead read 97 and her ear 95.5. 10 minutes later her ear was 96 and then a half hour later it was 97.6.

The only thing that seems to work is whether the temp is on the red or not, but otherwise it's completely useless and I am currently looking for another one. Very disappointing, what a waste of money.

The SNOO had pros and cons for our twin baby girls. We rented 2 when the girls were 2 months old (about a month adjusted age since they were born early) because we had heard great things. It didnt work as well for the girls as I hoped it would. It was not helpful in getting them down at bedtime or naptime, or when either baby was upset. In fact, due to reflux, we think the SNOO actually made them more upset when they woke from reflux because they would cry and the SNOO would respond by moving faster, which would get their reflux all riled up. Perfect if you want a milkshake, not great for calming a crying baby with reflux. Needless to say, we would just get up and comfort them anyway long before the machine "timed out" and said that baby needs you. We ended up co-sleeping at around 4 months and that was a better fit for us (we use all the safe co-sleeping guidelines that our doctor recommended and did alot of reasearch into the safety of co-sleeping beforehand). I do think a pro of the SNOO was that it may have helped them connect sleep cycles with the base level of white noise and base rocking, and we did see some longer stretches of sleep which was great! Pros and cons- but overall we sent it back after a couple months and I probably wouldn't recommend the product to friends. That being said, anything is worth a try that could help when you are sleep deprived!

Being a new mom, I don't have a ton of experience with baby items. I knew I wanted a bouncer/seat, but found most of the ones available to be too garish and obnoxious-looking. This product was in soft, aesthetically pleasing colors and seemed to be a good value as it would accommodate children up to 40 pounds. I didn't really care about the music or vibrations, so they were a bonus. I liked this item until I placed my baby in it. She slid right down, despite the harness (which is uncomfortable for her, by the way - why can't they pad those straps a little?). The newborn insert didn't really help in holding her in the right spot, and her head was pushed down onto her chest. She did not look happy. The other problem was that this "rocker" does not rock - at least not well. To get any kind of rocking motion, you have to push UP on the front edge of the seat, rather than down (this won't make much sense unless you can actually try it out for yourself). This is an issue because this can't really be powered by baby's kicks because the baby will just be pushing down on the rocker, not pulling it up. I don't know if this problem is caused by the two plastic pieces at the front of the rocker rails (perhaps a safety feature?) or if it is because the rails don't have enough of a curvature to generate enough motion. Either way, it is a stretch of the imagination to call this a rocker. It's basically a seat, and for the price, I'd like something a little beyond a seat.

After doing yet more research I realized that some bouncer chairs actually recline to lay almost flat, and I think that would be more appropriate for a newborn. I have now decided to go with the Bright Starts Cradling Bouncer and once I have had a chance to try that one out will post a review.

Thank goodness for Amazon's generous return policy on baby items!

I gave this monitor two stars because we did manage to use it for two years. But it was never a great monitor for two reasons: terrible battery life on the monitor unit and poor construction on the monitor unit. The monitor lasted about 6 months before we had to keep it constantly plugged in because the battery couldn't last an hour. It also was constantly plagued with what I'm guessing are shorts on the PCB and / or poor connections involving the power circuitry. It would constantly reboot itself at the slightest touch, a wiggle of the power cord, or setting it on the charging base and making that power connection. Luckily, the reboot cycle is pretty fast. But it got to the point where we could not touch it at all without the entire unit needing to reboot.

The only slight problem with the camera itself is that the LED interferes with the night vision when you try to use it aimed down low. So don't put it on a high shelf and expect it to look down at the crib.

It had some good functionality - loved the night vision, the camera's remote swivel, the good image quality when the monitor worked, relatively intelligent volume triggering when it detected a sound (but the low rumble of the nearby train tracks would trigger it every single time). We did not utilize multiple cameras or video recording to a SD card. The talk-through was handy, but the "lullabies" were tinny and harsh - more alarming than comforting.

We have finally had to replace it after 26 months because the random reboots have turned into random shutoffs. There is no power-off warning beep or alarm. We would not even know that it had stopped monitoring the toddler in the middle of the night, which was very alarming.

I don't understand all the positive reviews! Yes, it has a nice feature set, but the image quality is terrible, the video skips and lags, and screen is tiny. I'm very disappointed in the monitor and would definitely not recommend it.

We got this based on it boasting sound detection and being a great baby monitor. Unfortunately, it was completely inadequate and I returned it.

PROS
- Easy to set up
- Video quality was good, and there was little lag in the feed

CONS
- Sound detection setting said it would detect "baby crying." We could not set it off, not matter what. Yelling, crying, banging, etc. Nothing set off the alarm at any sensitivity, except for random noises after we set it up.
- Audio won't stay on overnight. I figured I'd try it without an alarm and use it as a mostly audio monitor with video for our 3-year-old. I'd wake in the morning to find the audio had muted itself overnight and our daughter was already awake, who knows how long. Good thing she didn't actually need our help!

If you just want to watch a room with video, then this seemed like a reliable camera with good video quality. If you need to be alerted when something makes noise, it's completely unreliable. I'd even go so far as to say it's irresponsible to advertise that you can wake someone to a baby's cry and then fail entirely.

In my 20s, I developed early-onset rosacea and I've always had super sensitive skin that reacts to problematic ingredients in a BAD way. Most recently, I noticed a sunburn-like rash on my nose that looked like very dry skin. I was using a moisturizer from Whole Foods for at least a year and realize it was this lotion that had been consistently used so I needed a replacement that would both sooth my dry skin and not irritate my rosacea further. I noticed this lotion on the shelf in the store and was intrigued because it contains all natural ingredients - including chamomile which soothes redness. It does not contain anything I know I'm allergic to - such as gluten or corn. It was a decent price (less than $8 for a bottle) so I decided to give it a go. I started using it last night and I can usually tell within 24-48 hours whether my skin will react to it and I haven't had a single problem so far. My skin feels soft and silky, which is wonderful as it has not felt this way in a LONG time. I must say that I was worried about the argan oil because, even though it is good for skin, it makes my face feel greasy when the actual oil is used. However, this does not occur with the lotion. What has yet to be seen is whether my skin will build up an allergy to it after using it for a long time. Hopefully, that will not happen!

UPDATE: After using this product for several months, I still love it. My skin, which is very sensitive, has not reacted badly to it at all. I have bought several more bottles because I use it twice a day (morning and bedtime). I highly recommend!

2nd UPDATE: After using this product continuously, my skin seems to have built up a resistance to it. It no longer soothes dry skin and my rosacea has gotten worse. In fact, sometimes, it appears my face is more red after using it than before. I have discontinued this lotion and moved on to something else.

You needed a seat for visitors or grandkids that come by once in a while
