Upcoming on our first baby we researched the heck outta cloth diapers and tidy tots were the ones we decided on. The system, and the flushies and all that- they are made in the US... it all seemed great. After two months of trials and constantly reverting to disposables we finally switched to another brand of cloth diapers. We put in the time to feel like we have an informed opinion on these diapers.

The truth of the matter is, though... they kinda suck.

For the price of a great start pack you can get an utter buttload of cloth diapers from a ton of other brands and... they work better than tidy tots.

Putting together tidy tots diapers is a chore, simple truth. When you have an infant you don’t have too much spare time and these diapers are a process. So that’s a strike. They use a bunch of snaps, which is integral to their design, but it means you are gonna be touching pee soaked liners every time you take them apart to wash. They come with one bolster per diaper and that’s an utter joke. One. My kid soaks through one bolster in an hour. We have to use two to make it so we aren’t constantly changing him and the boosters are not inexpensive. If we want to use them at night it’s three bolsters, but these stupid bolsters are super tough and not soft or plush, so it’s like strapping a giant help blob to his crotch- that sucks. These diapers blow out just about every time he poops in them. I think any claim of blowout free diapers is a lie, but he never blows out disposables or the new cloth diapers we are using. So... yeah.

So, in review. Tidy tots is a great company I want to support, but their diapers are not good.

We have the Clek Foonf car seat and love it, so we purchased this bag since we had a few flights in our future. We expected it to be of the same high quality as Clek car seats, we were wrong. We have flown three times on three different airlines and each time something else on the car seat broke. Pretty much the only reason someone would buy this bag is to fly with it (maybe for bus or boat travel to a lesser extent). With that in mind you would think they would design this bag to take the abuse the airlines place on the bags.
The entire kit weights about 53 lbs when it has the Foonf car seat in it. Since it is a car seat the airlines generally don't mind. I have only had to push two times at the ticket counter, but have not been charged yet.

We have taken great care to pack the bag properly (per the instructions) and not add any additional items in the bag.

Problems:
1) The bag has nylon straps with plastic clips at key support locations so you can connect them once the bag is zipped up. This is a good thing. But, when we received the bag, the female ends of all four of the plastic clips were warped. This made it difficult to get any of the clips plugged in tightly. They just used poor quality plastic clips (probably saved them 5 cents on the production of the bag).
2) While the bag was traveling on our first trip one of the plastic clips broke (apparently it could not handle the stresses that it was meant to handle).
3) While on the second trip one of the carry straps ripped halfway down the side of the bag
4) Also while on the third trip the plastic inside the bag which is meant to support the base of the car seat, broke into multiple pieces.
5) On its third trip the seam holding the zipper in place has torn about a six inch long hole, which will no doubt get bigger on our next trip.

These are all issues of poor construction quality. Stronger seams, better clips and higher quality plastic in the base could solve all of these issues and probably not cost a whole lot more to construct. I would pay an extra $5-$10 for this bag if they built it right.

This bag might as well be sold as disposable. If you need a bag to protect your car seat for one or two trips and then you plan to throw it away, then by all means spend well over $100 for this bag. But if you are expecting Clek to make a bag that is of high quality, think again.

Note: I cannot seem to find a way to upload photos, otherwise I would include a photo of each faulty part of this bag.

**UPDATE Nov 12th, 2014
Even though the product has no stated warranty, I contacted Clek and after sending them photos of the bag and proof of purchase they said they would replace the bag at no charge. I don't know if the new bag will be of any better quality or will suffer the same issues after a few flights. I have a bit of travel coming up. I will post an update once I take a few trips with this bad and see how it holds up.

I'm going to buck the trend here.

These bags are very cute and stylish. They are effective if you want to reduce your usage of plastic baggies. I like how they are zipper and not velcro. They do a good job, for the most part, of containing foods, although, if you're trying to store something juicy (like cut up oranges), you might be pushing your luck as the moisture will gradually seep through and make the fabric outer cover damp.

If the only things you're going to use this for are dry snacks like crackers or cereal, you're probably fine just wiping the interior with a damp cloth after each use. And then once a week throwing it in the laundry for "deep cleaning".

But if you are using it for anything that is going to leave any residue (back to my original example of oranges... or chips which will likely leave some oily residue, PBJ sandwiches, you get the idea here) these are really not practical. Turning inside out and wiping the interior doesn't get it clean enough for me. You can do a load of laundry (but most people don't do laundry every day) or hand wash and submerge it in soapy water, but the fabric outer takes forever to dry. So you really end up having to buy a 2 day supply of these to rotate through if you want to use them everyday. And they are NOT inexpensive, so buying several might be cost-prohibitive for some.

Also, the outer fabric, while cute is... well... fabric. So it can stain. Making your cute bag not-so-cute anymore.

If your looking to buy this for your kids, I would instead go with the [[ASIN:B00814ZC8W Bumkins 2 Count Reusable Snack Bags, Blue/Green, Small]]. They are about half the price of the Itzy Ritzy and for anyone who has used the amazing Bumkins Bibs, these are the same material. They are a breeze to wash, dry super fast and I've never had it hold a stain.

Here's my review of the Bumkins snack bag for comparison: http://www.amazon.com/review/R33YNXHGAEY2KW

The prints are loud and garrish, but my kid likes it fine. Much more practical for busy moms (and dads!).

I have both the Snack Happened and the Bumkins bags, and I reach for the Bumkins every time.

I purchased this in the black color. For some reason this site is not allowing me to submit this review in the black color, so it's showing this as a review for the silver bag. Just as a side note, the silver bag was the same price as the black and blush. One day after this review was initially posted online under the silver color, the price increased from twenty-nine and ninety nine to over seventy dollars and now includes free shipping and free returns.

I really wanted to love this bag. However, when I first opened the box, I had knew this bag would have to be returned. I contacted the seller via Amazon and they were very easy to work with and provided no hassle in providing a prompt return authorization. However, when I went to the post office, the clerk let me know that even at the cheapest shipping rate, it would cost almost half the price of the bag in order for me to return it to the vendor due to the location from which it was going to be shipped. So, with that in mind, I decided to keep the bag. I will probably pass it on to someone with 1 child or a first time mother, or just use it as a purse.

Here is what I like about the bag:
1. It is beautiful and fashionable. The silver hardware is also nice. It doesn't look like a diaper bag.
2. The handles seem to be well made.
3. It comes with stroller straps.
4. The changing pad is not padded. For me this would not be an issue, as it only means that it could be tossed into the washer to be cleaned when needed. A padded changing pad would not be as easy to machine wash without getting torn up.

Here are the deal breakers for me on this bag:
1. The bottom part of the bag I received is not sturdy at all. It's very thin and flimsy. The faux leather is also very wrinkled, as if it were glued on improperly and left to dry that way. When you sit the bag down it just falls down all over the place.

2. A reveiwer stated the dimensions of the bag and its pockets. The bag I received has different dimensions. For example, it was stated that the back zippered pocket was 8x10. The back zippered pocket on the bag I received is actually 3x5. In fact, all of the pockets are too small and not deep enough. This translates into all of my things falling out withing the bag.

3. I could not fit hardly anything in the pockets. I tried to fit just 2 pampers cruisers size 6 diapers into the largest pocket. It did not work at all. I could not fit the adjustable strap inside any of the pockets. Nor could I fit a bottle into the insulated pocket. The insulated pocket is extremely small and narrow. My hand would not even fit inside , and I have small hands.

4. The pocket on the changing pad is sewn on crooked and is also much to small. I could not fit diapers or travel wipes or anything else in this pocket.

5. I am minimalist. I like to keep diaper bag packing simple. I could NOT fit a blanket, change of clothes for baby and 2 year old, juice box and small snack, diapers, and wipes into this bag. The bag I received was not as large as others described. I have 2 small ones and a 3rd baby on the way. There is absolutely no way I could fit what's needed in here. I tried and it didn't work.

6. This bag is heavy when empty. When filled, it's even more heavy on the shoulder. I'm not willing to sacrifice my shoulder for style. I need to be able to lift, and move young children and a baby quickly without having to contend with a heavy shoulder bag.

Complete and utter garbage. I don't actually think these are a new version of the product. These dryersheet-liners are so horrible that they've got to be a knock-off or something... Some trash somebody dug out of a dumpster somewhere, crammed it into a box and stamped a Real Nappies logo onto it. Gotta make that buck, after all!

After returning this crap, we're going to reorder a few directly from the website to find out for sure if the product has actually changed to complete rubbish, or if this is just a case of somebody lying and cheating their way into the Amazon store to rip people off.

UPDATE:
After a very informative back-and-forth with Real Nappies customer support, I thought I'd leave some additional information.

First off, they are indeed using a new formula. The original awesome liners we had were bamboo based, but apparently some customers complained that they broke down too soon (while still in the diaper). We never experienced that, but I suppose not every parent can be bothered to change their child within the first several hours of a dirty diaper. These new ones are made from corn, hence the change in texture.

Second, I've had to bump my review from 1 to 2 stars because despite the fact that these liners are simply a very bad product, the customer service of the company (and every other product we bought from them) has been top notch. An extremely helpful and informative exchange with Jana from customer support (along with an expedient refund) has helped immensely and I can't in good conscience leave a 1-star review at this point.

So, having said that... do not buy these liners. They are BAD. However if you do make the mistake of purchasing them, you can rest assured that the company behind them won't hang you out to dry. A nice consolation, I suppose.

Pros: Motor works well and is fairly quiet. Speed is good. It's small enough to move to different rooms without difficulty.

Cons: Constantly squeaky. The seat could use more support around the head. My baby's head will often flop around while she's sleeping. The sound is not loud or very clear.

Im not very happy. I ordered a grey bib and the only picture of the grey bib when I ordered it was of it in the box. They have since added a full picture of the grey and PINK bib that I bought for my son but the original picture of the grey bib in the box didn’t show any pink. I think pink is a pretty important color to put in the description.

I believe they failed at warning people about the smell. I literally felt like I had to vomit. Yes my daughter didn’t want to eat, she even said eww and she’s 17 months. But it didn’t stop her from coming back later. It works for that moment but then I dread reapplying it. I’m officially done breastfeeding but it’s not due to this. I had time away for a few days and refused to feed her when I came back. Wish I would have waited instead of wasting the money.

I got these because I thought they would add extra absorbency for overnight diapering. They haven't proven to be useful for that and overall I think they're pretty pointless. My daughter is only 3 months old (started using them when she was 2 months) so maybe they will come in more handy when her poop is less runny...? They are soft, but most cloth diapers/inserts don't need t be any softer.

I have been using this sheet in rotation with others for 5 months. It is already coming apart at the seams. The fit is loose on the long sides and too tight on the short. I have a standard size crib mattress. On the plus Side the color is nice and it feels very soft

The quality of the image is alright. The monitor itself feels really light and cheap. The buttons on top of the monitor is very stiff and hard to press and doesn't provide much information on what they do. The monitor needs to be constantly hooked up to the charger for it to work, which is very inconvenient. The straps for the mounting of the camera doesn't really fit all types of car headrest. I have a Toyota Sienna and the headrest is too big in girth for the straps. The suction cup mount for the camera is a bit awkwardly shaped so it's hard to mount it against the window and get a good angle of the baby. Plus, if you place it on the window you wouldn't be able to roll the window down (obviously). So with those hurdles in place, I had to resort to being innovative and just wedged the camera between the top of the headrest to the body of the car seat. However, the camera zooms in too much and so I'm literally only able to see my baby's head in the monitor. It's not like you can see very much else. But for the purpose of just watching the baby, it should serve its purpose. There is no option to zoom out any further. Overall, I think the quality of this product is a bit lacking in consideration of how much it actually cost. But I'm still giving it a 2 stars instead of 1 only because although it feels cheap and lacks in quality, it still serves its purpose--and that's to be able to keep an eye out on the little one while I'm driving since she's rear-facing.

I don't love it. We have a small house, and if you live in a small space, this chair is a MAJOR TRIPPING HAZARD. My husband and I have both REPEATEDLY tried to walk past it and gotten our foot hooked in it and tripped, sometimes holding the baby, and sometimes almost falling on the baby while he is in the seat. Or at least stubbed our toes, which just happened again a few minutes ago, causing me to finally write a review on this dumb thing! Also, I don't know why it is angled down at such a slope, but when I put my baby in the seat, he slides down to the bottom of it, making his head slump down to his shoulders and his feet hang over the bottom. The only way to make it work is to tuck a towel under his bottom so he is propped up higher, and place the 2 front feet of the seat up on small boxes, so he can lay in it without sliding down.
Good concept, but a bad design. I will be getting rid of mine and buying a rock and play.

We bought this intending to use it to shorten and protect the cord for a fan used in my daughter's room. It is a standard size cord that is not very long, but no matter how I wrap it it will not close with the cord wrapped up inside, rendering it useless. Really disappointed!

The problem with this cup like stated by others is the handles turn freely so when he gets it in upside down it is a struggle when he gets halfway through the bottle since the nipple is on the upper side.  Also the nipple collapses so we ended up using a nipple from another bottle that fit this cup.
Really did not hold pumps in place. The way the folds of the bra open up and close cause the bottles to lose suction. You still end up holding while pumping.

I don't usually do reviews but I wish someone had broken it down like this for me.
First, this thing is a pain to put together. Thought it would be worth it by saving the money, it's not because it does NOT work for what we needed. We put our Uppababy Vista v2 2020 bassinet in there, and:
1. Because it is a "rocking stand" it is completely imbalanced and leans very heavy on the side with the canopy. The weight of the bassinet is very heavy on the canopy side, and because of GRAVITY, it leans.
2. IF you shove your bassinet all the way to one side, it "could be straightened out" with a 7" gap between the edge which is a huge safety concern, so you would need to drill additional holes into the plastic that holds the bassinet in.
3. EVEN IF you do this, it is STILL crooked, and frankly I don't want my baby to feel like she's sleeping on a hill.
In short, if you don't want to do some serious rigging to get this thing sturdy and safe, pay the money, get the uppababy one. Get it used. That's what we are doing. Now we have to disassemble and attempt to return this huge waste of time. I attached pics that I hope help you decide.
I don't have a huge baby but my LG didn't fit in this.

I have very mixed feelings about this potty. On one hand, the size is right for my petite just turned three year old, and the ability to pull out just the center green portion to empty it is nice. But the negative for me outweighs the positives. It is very lightweight and the non skid feet aren't really non skid. If you've got one of those $5 IKEA step stools for kids, those have great non skid feet. This potty does not. As most bathrooms have very slick tile floors, this becomes an issue as your poor toddler is attempting to "slide into first" and make it to the potty before they pee and the potty slides away from them. The worst is when they pee a bit as they run to the potty, slip in the pee, grab the toilet as they're slipping and slide/fall on the floor as the potty slides away from them. Sure, you could put the potty on a rug but you'll be washing pee out of that rug every hour for a couple weeks. Or you could attach sturdy rubber feet but that may be difficult when you don't know where to find such a thing and the surface area on which to attach feet is very narrow.

Loved the print and got these to mix and match with the set of onesies. I don't like these pants because the fabric of the pants stretches out and gets very baggy after wearing for just a little while. Washing and drying is the only way to "reset" the elasticity.

Although these diapers are thin & sits high on waist ( so the strap doesn't rub against sons thigh and cause bruising..as occurred with the huggies brand) The BIGGEST fallback is that it is made up of silicone particles ( the absorbent) in the diaper itself and when wet, if child runs around ( like my VERY active toddler) then the diaper tears and the silicoe particles fall out the side.

Today was the 5th time this has happened in the space of 2 weeks. I DO change his diapers frequently and now I do it even more than I did with the huggies in fear that the silicone will fall out and give him a rash or dirty the floor. It is a mess to clean up, there's silicone 'powder' everywhere.

Tonight I've pretty much had it with these diapers. My son (19months) was running around kicking his ball and when it was time to change him, there was a big glob of silicone at the foot of his pants. Luckily he was wearing his thermal pants so the elastic band was very close fitting to his ankles and this is what kept the majority, not all, of the silicone within his pants and off the carpet.

In summary. These diapers and thin and does not leak BUT these 2 factors do not make up for the huge downfall of having silicone particles all over the place. Thank God he has not gotten a rash from it as yet.

This works well as a white noise machine. We like the white noise and the womb sounds. Most of the other features are so poorly designed that the machine might as well not have them.

Aside from white noise and womb sounds, the other sounds this machine makes are annoying. For all of the nature sounds, the loops are too short. The underwater sounds, for instance, is one "bloop-bloop" sound followed by one whale sound, repeated over and over. The loops need to be quite a bit longer not to drive an adult crazy.

The lullabies are pretty cheesy synth stuff, much like you'd expect, but with a small set of short lullabies making for a pretty short loop that gets old really fast.

The night light is okay, as far as the glow from the top of the machine, but the bright blue LED light that shines out the little holes in the purple part is WAY too bright, and shines even when the night-light feature is off. I have to hide the machine behind a Kleenex box to keep it from shining super-bright blue light dots on my baby's face.

The MP3-player feature is also poorly designed. When I plug my iPod into the machine, the music comes out really distorted. This is because the machine is doing a really bad job of blending the stereo input from my iPod into the mono output that the machine uses. I've been able to circumvent this by gingerly plugging my iPod only halfway in, but this is really annoying, because if I bump it at all, like by touching any of the buttons on my iPod, I have to fuss with the plug for a minute to get it right again.

So basically, the only feature of this machine which I regularly use is the white noise and the womb sounds, and if that's all I wanted, I could have bought a cheaper machine, or just used a CD instead.

I had similar issues with poor documentation with the Chicco clip on chairs. For some reason these manufactures go through lengths describing one dimension but leave out the others. If these manufactures just included a picture of the assembled product along with component dimensions this can all be figured out. Instead they don't provide that useful info and focus on only one possible problematic aspect--leaving questions that are only answered when you buy it and discover it won't work.

For this chair, it is never described how deep a table skirt must be from the table edge so that it will fit properly. The manual does describe not to use it if your table's edge has a molding 35mm deep, and lists other examples how it should not be attached INCLUDING the instance where the skirt is too close to the table edge to allow a flush fit but DOES NOT INCLUDE THAT DIMENSION!

Come on people! How can so many engineers design a product and have manuals written but does not include critical dimensions even when a graphic illustration shows there could be a problem! And yet it includes the one specific measurement for the table molding which is less likely to even be an issue. Very disappointing.

There are several reasons to look at other gates instead of this one. I currently have three metal gates in place that are better looking, easier to install, easier to operate, sturdier, cost around the same or just a little more, and are all rated for use with stairs.

My first issue with this particular gate is right out of the box the design is weird. It's two separate pieces of metal that you have to bolt together in a fixed width. If you have a doorway that's slightly odd in measurement - like mine - that makes this gate more difficult to use than it has to be. Compared to the other three brands in our home which are all fully adjustable via sliding arm extensions.

The second major drawback is the fact that this gate can ONLY be attached by permanently drilling holes into the wall/door frame and bolting it in place. That may not be an acceptable option if you rent or perhaps do not care to permanently ruin an antique door frame. Again, the three other gates we already use have the tension cup mounts as an included second option.

The next problem is that this gate is not rated for use with stairs. It says this several times all over the instruction booklet and on the warranty sheet. If you're going to use this with children, be aware. My last personal gripe is the open/close latch. It comes disassembled! Seriously? It isn't even a physical part of the actual gate. You have to screw part of it onto your door frame or wall and then it catches the gate. Just no. The entire thing is way more complicated and intrusive than it should be. In the end, because of the fixed width issues and the permanent bolting to the wall, the only place I can really put this is in our mudroom/garage entry doorway and I don't need it there.

Unfortunately, I find this to be really not worth it. Traveling with this sucks because it's heavy and doesn't pack down extremely small due to the thickness of the fabric and the aluminum rods for the legs. If you're trying to pack light for air travel or have limited space in a carry on, this feels like a huge waste. However, if you pack smart it can be fitted inside most pack and plays as they have a lot of empty space in between when folded down.

Besides that, it's pretty inconvenient to set up while traveling if your physical space is limited, like in a small hotel room or cruise ship room because the poles are so insanely long before you're done installing it. Depending on your circumstances it's also very annoying to find somewhere to keep it if it's not over the crib.

Lastly, I had real problems with using it for a toddler. My kid was scared to be inside of it and it would've been better to just sleep her in the crib as normal and not keep the lights on too bright at night when us adults weren't ready yet to sleep. The window coverings at most hotels are good enough for us that naps can happen while traveling without needing a $200 accessory. It really just did not feel worth it as it didn't improve sleep at all for my child and very barely gave us a tiny benefit of being able to keep lights on for an extra few hours before bed. But the struggle of having our otherwise great sleeper attempt to sleep in a space she's terrified of absolutely made this product worthless for my family. And again, at this price point, it only seems to make sense for babies under 1 and families who are extremely financially comfortable to spend a few hundred dollars on barely-useful accessories.

I don't like this bath at all. I was really whetted to the idea of washing the babies in the sink. I'm short and our tub is deep so the only way for me to reasonably wash them is to crawl into the tub since my arms can't reach from the outside. Before you purchase this, you need to consider the dimensions of your sink, shape, and placement of the faucet. I think if your sink is too small, this is going to be difficult to use. In addition, if the faucet is low or protrudes too much, it will be obstructive. The best combination would be a medium-sized, oval sink, with a faucet that isn't in the way. Having said that, I have a large, square sink with a very high faucet that can be rotated out of the way.

Cons:
1) It doesn't have a drain at the base. After you've washed your baby with soapy water, the only way to empty that dirty water is to lift him out of the Puj tub, flip it over to dump the water, and put him back in. It's a bit dangerous when you're by yourself and the baby is a wet, slippery mess.
2) It doesn't fit my square sink nicely. It tends to tilt to one side or the other spilling the baby out.
3) Even when they are older and bigger, they tend to slide down to the bottom leaving their neck extremely flexed and crumpled.

Pros:

-I love that it makes him happy.

Cons:
-I have yet to pull this set out of the wash and not find it overly wrinkled. It doesn't matter what setting I put the wash on or how much fabric softener is used... it just seems to be in a slightly worse condition each time I wash it.

Think about how much you are carrying for a baby, and if you carry a child, then the added weight of a heavy bag is just not helpful. It's doubled fabric and there's no reason for it. They could have used ripstop nylon or single layer canvas.

2. It looks large but actually it doesn't hold jack.
The depth is about 3" on the *outside*. On the inside, it's even less. As other reviewers posted, if you put anything in the top pockets, your inside area shrinks. The outside pockets hold maybe one thing each and stuff just gets lost if it's smaller than a bottle.

3. There's no interior organization for dipes, wipes or anything.
It's just an open area. Stuff gets smashed. Supposedly, you use the top 1/2 pockets, but then you run in to the issue in #2. Don't put a banana in there! It's a very deep interior (but narrow) so stuff is hard to get to.

4. Everytime I have seen a friend or person with this bag, it looks overstuffed.
So empty, it's pretty, but if you use it like you need to, it looks stuff spilling out. The magnetic closure, a JOKE. I have NEVER seen anyone be able to close it. The review who says they got their 13" laptop and all this other stuff in it, I'm sure you can do it, but then it bulges the bag out and makes it difficult to carry b/c it's a rectangular bag and if you overstuff it, it gets cylindrical which means it's against your body in a weird way.

5. It's not secure.
The openness of it due to the fact that you probably won't be able to close/zip it means that your wallet/cell whatever are open territory for pickpockets. If you put your wallet in the zippered area, you won't be able to fit anything else in the interior section.

6. The strap is not padded enough and is uncomfortable.
It's a thin "pad." Considering the weight of the bag and the stuff you put in it, you need more padding.

If you want a messenger bag-like bag for a diaper bag, get a messenger bag. We both ended up bailing on this bag and I used my daily bag (which is like a tote) made by an outdoor company b/c it was lightweight and had a good padded strap. I also found a larger purse at Brooklyn Industries to carry both my personal items and my child's. Believe me, if you need to carry stuff, you won't want to use this bag for long... Ours looks brand new. Find a bag you like for you that will fit your kid's stuff and get the Skip Hop wallet pad thing and carry that in your own bag. Skip Hop could take some cues from people who actually have to carry stuff (like messenger bags and backpackers) and actually design a great, hip, functional, urban-styled unisex diaper bag.

Marketed as a “white noise” machine, this tool to help your baby sleep soundly has a number of flaws that should keep any parent from purchasing. 1. It doesn’t come with the standard static white noise sound. It offers different water noises, but none as basic as the name implies. 2. There is a very bright light that shines when the sound machine is started and when the timer runs out it blinks even brighter. This is problematic because light can be incredibly distracting for babies and prevent good sleep. Additionally, if your baby sleeps in your room, the combination of the sound stopping with the timer and the bright light flashing tends to wake up the adults. If the light exists for non-hearing folks to know when the spin has stopped, then there should be some way to disable this function. 3. The battery doesn’t last long enough. Having to charge this daily is a huge pain.

For travel it is compact, and durable. The sound options are nice and the Bluetooth feature is good to have if you plan to use it as a speaker as well.

These bottles worked great at first.  I primarily breastfed my baby, but used these for times that I needed to bottle feed.  My baby did great going from breast to bottle - never had any problems. It's fine while my baby is drinking out of it, but as soon as I tip it upright, milk starts leaking down the side.  I made terrycloth "sleeves" out of old towels to handle the mess because we're nearing the end of bottle feeding and I don't want to buy anything new.  I didn't have this problem at first, so it might be something with the valve inside (I read somewhere that the bottle can leak if the valve slit gets torn and it looks like mine is).  I used to have a glass version of this bottle and I don't remember having problems with that one, but it may have been prior to the problems I've had with the plastic one (again...probably a valve issue).  Buyer beware.  Most plastic bottles are now BPA free and there are other glass options.  I don't think I'd buy these again.

The placemat itself is constructed of a sturdy, somewhat thin, 2mm soft silicone with small suction cups - three on either side and one on the top flap - moulded to the bottom. It is not nearly as "sticky" as most food-grade silicone, and the suction cups will stick to little except glass and clean plastic.

We purchased this placemat because our son - 15 months old - is learning to use utensils and ends up just pushing his plate to the side while trying to scoop up food. Our intent was to get a mat that would stay in place and add a little more friction to his plates, thus allowing him more resistance when he tries to viciously impale that piece of chicken he's after. Since the placemat will not suction to our oak table top, the placemat currently serves little more than as an additional "toy" at the dinner table...

If you have a glass table and are looking for a decent, easy to clean placemat that folds up neatly for transport, you will be satisfied with this purchase. If this does not describe your situation, look elsewhere.

I just got this car seat yesterday and have already installed it and used it. This was for my fourth child, so I know a thing or two about car seats. Right out of the box all you had to do was clip in the cup holders. One of them didn’t want to clip in (there’s only one way it goes in). I was able to click it in, but the plastic part underneath the cup put a pressure mark on the inside of the cup. I put my 15 mo old child in to get the straps and head rest to the right height and make sure the crotch buckle was in the correct position. Here’s the best part, there’s no more rethreading the harness straps, you just pull up on the head and it automatically adjusts. Finally after four kids we found an easy solution to that! It was fairly straight forward to install in my odyssey rear facing, however getting the latch tight enough was a struggle. I was sitting in the car seat trying to pull it tight, but it felt like the strap just wouldn’t tighten past a certain point. I think I finally yanked enough that it is in tight, but it was definitely the most effort I have ever put into latching a seat. We took a little test drive with my kiddo to see how he liked it. The chest straps are REALLY hard to get tight. Even my husband couldn’t get the straps to where we couldn’t pinch a little of the seat belt. I have to climb into the car so I have more leverage to pull on it. My baby is maybe 22 lbs soaking wet, so maybe a bigger baby would work better? But this car seat is for 4+ lbs so it should work better.

Overall this seems to be a great car seat. I would love to see improvements in the latch and in the chest straps being easier to tighten. I did leave a message with our city car seat technician to make sure I’ve installed it correctly. If it’s user error I’ll come back and update this review.

Rating this 3 stars because, while it served it's purpose, cleaning it seems impossible. Our old play pen had a zipper along the edge of the bottom pad so you could take out the boards and actually wash the cushion. This play pen offers no option to wash the bottom cushion. Anyone with a baby knows, spit-up happens! And it stinks! Once any spit-up soaks into the bottom pad, good luck getting that smell out! Having purchased this for our 2nd child, I had enough experience to put a waterproof cover/encasement over the bottom pad. Only problem with that is, now I cannot attach the straps under the pad to the bars that support the bottom of the play pen. Could be a potential safety issue. If I use a regular waterproof play pen cover that is open on the bottom, this will likely not be an issue, however, those are about $20 a piece... half the cost of the entire play pen itself.

Pros:
- easy to set up and take down
- light enough to move on the wheels when open

We don't like these food pouches. Had to return the 3.5 oz pouch. We will wait and see on the 6 oz pouch.

So the silicone quality is OKAY. It seems to pass the pinch test, but there is slight discoloration when I stretch it, which I don't find to be the case with my other high quality silicone products. The silicone is thick enough to be sturdy but appears to be soft enough for a squeezable food pouch for my baby. My 6 month old loved the size of the 3.5 oz pouch. It is just right for him to handle all on his own, even when filled with food/water. Most pouches, even the flatter 3.5 oz food pouches from town, are a struggle for him. The pouch itself is not why I am returning this item. It's the lid/spout.

First off, the plastic spout is VERY short. Far shorter than all other spouts baby and I have dealt with. He doesn't like it. That is a major problem for us. On top of that, it is hard plastic and not good for his tender gums. He just refused to eat out of it. Even the plastic spouts on the standard pouches from town are softer than this.

Second, I don't like the red insert. Other reviews claim that you MUST use it in order to create the necessary suction to efficiently empty the pouch, and I believe them. But I don't like the insert. It is supposed to be 100% leakproof even with liquid, so I immediately tested it with water. I didn't even have it completely upside down before it was dripping a steady stream of water. Shake it, and water goes flying. So clearly NOT a good liquid sippy cup.

But I really wanted this for purees, so I tried that next. I squeezed some homemade baby food currently stored in my Haaka food pouch into the Squeezy pouch to feed to my baby and see how he handles it, but first I sucked on it myself to test the flow. The food wouldn't come out. So I ended up up diluting it with equal parts water before it came out comfortably, and it didn't handle the slight strings from the food milled spinach mixed into the sweet potatoes. This puree was possibly thinner even than the stuff from town before it comfortably flowed. I suspect this is due to the very small opening resulting in a very small valve compared to our Haaka food pouch and the ChooMee pouch toppers.

After all this effort, and my baby wouldn't even eat out of it in the end because the spout with too short and hard for him to comfortably suck on. Plus I had to remove the EXTREMELY distracting lid before he would even focus enough to try.

So essentially this pouch is too leaky for a sippy cup and too small/stiff for thicker purees. I am trying food pouches because my baby is too underweight to follow pure baby led weaning but refuses to be spoon fed. He wants to feed himself. But having to dilute his nutrient dense foods half and half with water just fills his tummy up way too quickly, and he should be getting his hydration from nutrient dense breast milk.

As for feeding without the red insert, I tried that before I realized that he was just boycotting the plastic spout. It immediately let a bunch of air into the pouch, and I know that he gets VERY frustrated having to suck out air constantly to get down to the remaining food.

So maybe for an older baby or toddler, this pouch will work. The cap is tight and leak proof for tossing into a lunch box on the go. A toddler can learn to squeeze the food to the top without the red insert. I am saving the 6oz pouch for now to see if he likes it once he is older, but the 3.5 oz is too tiny to be useful for an older child, and this food pouch is terrible for a baby.

Also, the pouch easily dips in when trying to open or close the lid. The neck is too small to easily grip with my hands, and I kept accidentally popping the pouch out of the neck ring.

My wife and I shopped around for a PTZ cam for our newborn. We chose this cam based on good reviews.

However, upon getting this camera we found that it has overall very poor resolution. Think of a sub-1 megapixel camera from a phone 5+ year ago, and that's your image. Then consider lighting. This camera function best in fully lit rooms. If you have a dark room, the infrared kicks on and it's noticeably worse quality than daylight, but still functional. If you have any mild-lit situations, as in morning and evening, the infrared sensor won't turn on and you've got a black image. Then imagine a situation where you have blinds in the room and they're partially closed.. again you get a black image. You options are to have the blinds fully open and the room lit, or have blackout curtains so no light disables the infrared sensor.

Unfortunately, we bough tthis product too soon before my kid's birth and now we cannot return it as per policy. We're stuck with it, and I'd suggest to other to buy a baby cam and TEST for these differing lighting conditions as soon as you open it. You might sit back and say "well this isn't a big deal", but when you use this product each day these types of problems can make the video functionality non-existent a good portion of the time. And the portion of time you do have video, the focus and quality is so poor that you can 'barely' make out if the pacifier is still in the kid's mouth at 6ft from the camera. I don't believe I've gotten my value from this purchase.

This is a great toy but has done safety issues for smaller children who are just learning to walk and/or balance. The colors, shapes, and sound are great and it's a fun toy to play with, just be aware of the safety hazard when using as a walking aid. We purchased one of these for our daughter and I have safety concerns for babies who are just learning to pull up and/or walk. The wheels, even in the beginner mode, move way too fast for babies who are just learning to walk. The device also has absolutely no safety feature for children who don't quite have their balance as it tips backward too easily. Our daughter has taken a few falls that could've easily been prevented if there were some sort of safety feature to prevent it from tipping backward. This morning she lost her balance while playing with her toy and when the toy started to fall back with her, she pushed forward in an attempt to regain her balance but because the wheels have no grip and move so fast, she fell forward leaving a nasty bruise on her forehead. We have since taken the activity toy off of the walker portion and will only allow her to play with the toy portion from now on. There needs to be a warning on the box that this is not intended as a walking aid for babies who are just learning to walk, or there needs to be an additional piece added to the rear wheels to prevent the device from tipping over in the event that the child pulls back on it. This toy, as it is, has the potential to cause significant injury.

I love this lock system, but I have to give this specific product listing a knock due to its price. If you're looking into this system, let me make it clear: this key is nothing more than a magnet encased in plastic. There's nothing magical about this thing, and $9 just seems absurd to me, especially when the standard kit of one key and 8 locks is around $25. That's $16 for 8 locks or $2 per lock. If anything, the locks themselves are far more complex. They're also magnets encased in plastic, but they also have a spring, a catch, and a switch to keep them open or shut.

A while back, I purchased some rare earth magnets on Amazon. Wouldn't you know it, they open the locks too, and cost $10 for 50 magnets.

I needed to buy 3 lock kits for all the lower cabinets in our kitchen, so I have 3 keys around the room and I find that to be enough, but if I wanted another one I think I'd just glue something to one of my magnets with liquid nails and call it a day.

I have been on the hunt for a travel stroller. I wanted something lightweight which folded smaller than my bohemith Chicco Bravo. I needed a stroller which was easy to transport on a plane and to fold and carry on the subway.... I wanted to love this stroller so much!
Pros: ridiculously expansive sunshade, decent recline, swivel belly bar, nice/ easily washed fabric, suspension in front tires and carry strap when folded.
Cons: ridiculously difficult to fold and unfold. The mechanisms were constantly getting stuck and I was convinced I was going to break the stroller each time I opened and closed it. The little straps provided to attach a car seat constantly fell out and obstructed the fold as well. Once folded, I would go to pick it up by the strap and the sunshade part would flip out and appear to start unfolding. Basically the latch that keeps it closed only latches a portion of the stroller, not the whole thing. It completely defeats the purpose of a carry strap if while I'm on the subway the stroller starts unfolding. Just a really clumsy design. Finally the belly bar which swivels so beautifully... It is so difficult to unlock the sides. My child was screaming to get out and I struggled to open the belly bar. The button to open it is small and required a lot of pressure. It's very awkward to open correctly. This would not work well out and about.

Final takeaway: if you are simply looking for a decent lightweight daily stroller that you don't plan to fold and unfold, buy this. The sunshade and suspension are good and it's at a great pricepoint. If you want to travel or ever plan on constantly opening and closing it, look elsewhere. Also if you want to actively use the belly bar, not your stroller.

I really wanted to like this product. I have twins and thought that two high chairs would be too crowded, so wanted this space saving chair. However, I found that the cons are out-weighing the pros. I have used this chair for 6 months, and now that my babies are more mobile, this chair has become a problem for me.

Pros:
-Low-profile
-Washable (needs frequent washing, though)
-Seems to attach securely to table.

Cons:
-Sits my small one-year olds too far back, leaving a large gap between them and the table. This leads to many more issues...(1) food spills in lap and seat more (2) Baby struggles to get closer, pressing up her tummy against the belt (3) Baby has lots of leg room while sitting, and can easily maneuver legs into the seat, put feet down on the seat, and push herself up out of the belt and into a standing position, even with a tight belt!!!! Yikes! This may be less of an issue for bigger babies.
-I found that the belt had to be super tight for my baby to not get out. So tight, that I thought her tummy would hurt.
-Finger food gets stuck between the seam of the seat bottom and sides. I try to wipe it out with a cloth, but it takes a while to get all the little pieces out. Baby fingers are good at getting the pieces out, so I would often find my child picking up old bits of cheese and avocado that I missed and trying to eat it.
-While it is washable, I find that I wanted to wash it every couple days. This is a bit too much work for me. You need to line dry it, so that means either it is out of commission for a day, or you need to wash it before bed and dry overnight. This means having to assemble it in the morning, when everyone is rushing to eat breakfast and get out the door. I also worry that with such frequent washing will weaken the fabric, making the chair less secure. I haven't seen this yet, but I worry about it.
-You are limited to where you can attach the chairs to the table. They cannot go on leaves or near table legs. So, I had to put the twins right next to each other at a table end. This results in them grabbing each other and stealing each other's food while eating.

I can see this being a good chair for travel under a very watchful eye, but I would not recommend it for everyday use.

I have real mixed feelings about these wipes. I want to like them because they are real preservative free wipes that the user can control what does and does not go in the container. The container has some okay features - it can go in the microwave, which I am guessing is to heat the wipes to kill germs, but I am not a scientist and there is a suction cup on the bottom that holds the container on the counter so wipes can be easily pulled with one hand (see below).

I like that these wipes are DIY. I added distilled water. The directions say tap water, but our tap water is really hard and I did not want to have a hard water debacle on my hands. I measured the 350 ml on a scale and the line on the container is more than 350 ml, but I don't think it really matters. I put 350 ml by weight.

Feeding the wipes through the tiny hole on the top of the container is not a process for anyone with large hands. That hole is small. Once the wipes are fed through they do pull pretty well. I found using two hands and stopping the wipes and tearing one off before three or four come up is the best practice. I used a few wipes with just water the first day to wipe off our dogs' faces. They worked just fine. They are essentially wet paper towels.

The second day the wipes were still wet, but only damp. I added more water and I also added some antibacterial cleaner (Odoban) to see how that worked. I took the wipes out, added water to the bottom, squirted in four pumps of Odoban and then quickly dipped the wipes in from the top and then put the wipes back in and put the lid back on. I let the water/Odoban sit for a good three hours and then used a wipe. I did not detect any hint of Odoban (there is a smell) at all. I have a feeling if you want to use these wipes with a cleaning solution the best way to do this is from the very beginning.

I followed the directions on the English insert in the package, obviously. The directions on the roll of dry wipes is in either Korean or Chinese. There is also a second roll of wipes, which is nice. What is not nice, is I looked on Amazon for ways to purchase additional rolls of wipes and could not find anything. This means that once the two rolls of wipes are used that's it. For nearly $16 I don't know how cost effective this wipe contraption is unless more wipe rolls could be purchased.

Please note that you aren't buying a piece of luggage...this is simply a shaped, zippered canvas bag with wheels that makes it a slightly better option that having no wheels at all.

The Good:
1. Protected the carseat well. Fabric felt sturdy enough, seams and zipper seem sturdy.

2. Gives you a lot of extra space to store other items in - we stuffed this extra space with a TON of extra diapers, and didn't need to load our luggage with the extra bulk. Can load this up with anything you aren't afraid to get smashed up in transit.

The Bad:
1. My Britax Marathon carseat was too hard to fit into the bag. Design of the bag makes it impossible to fit easily. Had to muscle and shoe-horn my seat in, use both hands and two feet, plus the help of another person.

2. VERY hard to start the bag rolling. From a standing position, simply using the handle and straps provided (either the long strap that attaches via clips, or the short handle at the top of the bag) just drug the bag in a standing position, scraping the whole way. I ALWAYS had to kick the bottom of the bag while pulling forward to "get it started".

3. Awkard to wheel around. This bag tipped over every time we hit something with it.

4. VERY hard to wheel when you also have another piece of luggage to wheel. ANY bump by the other luggage sent this tipping over sideways, into people.

We have used four brands of breastmilk storage bags: Nuk, Honeysuckle, Medela, and Lansinoh. It's worth noting that we haven't had a leak with any of the bags, but we primarily use them for refrigeration. Based on other reviews, the "true" test of the bags seems to be freezing and subsequently thawing them. We have frozen and thawed a few of each brand with no leakage.

Nuk: These are our favorites. They are slightly smaller (maybe half a centimeter?) than Honeysuckle and Lansinoh bags, but you're not supposed to put more than 6 ounces in any of them anyway. They stand up the best, which is very convenient when pouring milk into them. I do hold the bags while I pour it in, but every now and then I lose my grip and these don't fall over like the Honeysuckle and Lansinoh bags. The plastic is thicker than the Lansinoh bags. These are also available at Wal-Mart, which is convenient if you can't wait for an amazon order to be delivered. The area where you write on is clear, and it's white with the other bags. I prefer the white background, but that's because I have black countertops. Small potatoes, though. The measurement is pretty close to the Medela bottles I pump in to. These are usually about 18-20 cents a bag depending on the quantity you purchase.

Honeysuckle: Our second favorite, these bags have more of a vinyl feel than a plastic feel. They're floppier than the Nuk bags, but more sturdy than the Lansinoh bags. The seal makes a clicking sound (like a Ziploc bag) when sealed, which is nice. The Nuk bags don't make that sound. My husband has had issues with the bags dripping milk out of the seal area when pouring instead of about a centimeter above the seal, where it is supposed to pour out of. The measurement seems to be off by half an ounce compared to the Medela bottles (if I pump 4.5 ounces, it will read as 4 ounces on these bags). These are about 18-20 cents a bag unless you buy a quantity of 300, in which they are 14 cents a bag (based on pricing as of July 2013). These are only available online, at least in my area (Virginia Beach).

Medela: These bags could be convenient for some because you pump directly into the bags. They work just fine, but I just prefer the bottles in case I adjust while pumping the milk can't splash out. They are a stiff plastic, which means they stand up well. They only hold about 5 ounces (compared to the 6 ounces for the other bags...but I've put 9 ounces in the other bags with no issue). They are a little harder to pour out of because of the design of the bag (the milk comes out about an inch above the seal). The measurement is accurate to the Medela bottles. They are also available in retail stores (Babies R Us, some Wal-Marts). These are more expensive at about 30 cents a bag.

Lansinoh: It's a shame that these bags are the most widely available, because they are the worst. They're thin, floppy, and have very little seam allowance. Based on other reviews, the bags changed in 2011. Prior to that, they were great, which is why the reviews on amazon are so high. They are about 18-20 cents a bag. They work fine in a pinch, but there are better options out there for the same (or better!) price.

I waited a bit to write this review because I was THIS CLOSE to returning it. Mainly the only reason I haven't is because it's a hassle to have to return then find another monitor then wait for it to come and we're in the middle of moving and I just needed a monitor. So this monitor works just fine. It's simple and easy to use. But it does NOT play nicely with continuous background noise: i.e. the fan that I have in my baby's room at night. If the fan is on the highest setting (which it always is), the monitor will let out this random static every 5-10 seconds, louder than the white noise level coming from the monitor. I think it is the noise cancelling technology or something, struggling to overcome the noise of the fan? If there is no white noise or fan or anything in the room, it does fine and there is no random static issues. It made me really angry and I wanted to chuck the thing against a wall because my baby sleeps terribly anyways and then I had this static surging in my ear every 10 seconds. I would love to have my old monitor back, without the noise canceling technology or whatever but I just keep the fan on the lowest setting and it seems to get along better with the monitor that way. Still, super annoying to have to adjust for the monitor's sake. Maybe I'll still return it. I have another few months to decide. Which means I need to refrain from throwing it against a wall so I can get my refund lol.

This product is average compared to other fans of it's same size as far as power and keeping you cool. If that is your reason for buying this fan, pass on this one... There is absolutely no way this is 6400mab. I have had some lowered powered fans that put out WAY more air than this fan.

The pluses of this fan... Very sturdy for sure! I have accidentally dropped this fan a couple of times and it hasn't broke. It is way more sturdy and well-built than most. It does have 4 speeds with a cool outdoor breeze speed which blows a slow rotation then a high rotation alternating. (Which I don't use, but still cool feature for some). The battery life on this fan is Ah-ma-zing!!!! I can charge it overnight and leave it for use in the car for car rides for my dog for 3 days (not even consecutively) without charging it in between. The only downfall I've seen is that once it is dead, you can't run it while trying to charge it (in the car) so I always had to remember to charge it before the car rides. Any previous fans I've had before were able to be used whole being charged so this was a HUGE disadvantage I found for this fan.

All in all, this fan is adequate enough though and gets the job done, however I could have bought 2 cheaper USB cordless fans that blow harder than this one does on high which I could charge while still using them at the same time.
So would I purchase this fan again personally, NO... but maybe I just got a bad fan?

HOWEVER... would I recommend it.... Yes if the features fit what you are looking for and you take into account all the details that I noted above and it fits for your needs. Since someone using as a stroller fan may not need a super high powered fan but more of a sturdy fan this might be right up your alley.

I purchased this item (admittedly not from Amazon), and was excited at the ease of use, especially at night. In that regard, the Baby Brezza does not disappoint! Very easy to set up, and using it is literally as easy as pushing a button.

However, we started off with one type of Similac formula (Similac Sensitive), and then switched to another (Similac Advance Stage 1) shortly after our daughter was born. According to the Baby Brezza manual and guide, the size setting for the Similac Sensitive was a 7, and the Similac Advance Stage 1 (one of the most popular formulas), was a 5. However, if you look at the mixing instructions between the two formulas, they are exactly the same! Each is to be mixed with one scoop (weighing at 8.3g for each 2fl oz). I bought a scale and weighed them to find out which setting is correct. If you use Similac Advance Stage 1, use setting 7, not setting 5!!! IF YOU GO BY THEIR CHARTS IT COULD SERIOUSLY HARM THE DEVELOPMENT AND GROWTH OF YOUR BABY!!!

I'm not sure which other of their settings are off, so if you buy this item, I suggest that you should also buy an accurate food scale to make sure the mixture your baby is getting is correct. This is a serious enough issue that I believe this item should be recalled and the correct settings given.

Outside of that major issue, it is easy and convenient to use. My only other gripe is that I wish you could set it for 1 oz increments rather than 2 oz. To a newborn baby, 2 oz is quite significant, and being able to set it at 1 or sometimes 3 would result in much less waste of formula.

I am still a Huggies fan but if theres an opportunity for cheaper price, I wouldn't hesitate to buy this one. I wish though that it is thicker than buggies wipes. However because it is sensitive, my daughter doesn't have a problem getting allergies on it.

As a parent of a young child, it is sometimes difficult to know when a doctor visit is warranted. This is especially true with ear infections because the symptoms vary widely and are subtle. The child may run a fever or may not. They may have trouble sleeping, but there could be a hundred different reasons for that. Nobody wants to run to the doctor with every sniffle. However, the "wait and see" approach sometimes ends up with a child screaming in pain in the middle of the night. (Been there, done that, too many times.)

We have three young children. Unfortunately, one is prone to ear infections and often exhibits no symptoms until the infection is in full swing.

We bought this Earcheck device when it was brand new on the market, so we've been using ours for a couple of years.

There are a couple of things that I can share:

First, I think the accuracy of the results depends on the individual. One of our children seems to get pretty accurate readings. Another child does not. I speculate that this may have something to do with the specific characteristics of their ear canal.

Second, this only detects the presence of fluid, not actually infection. You can have fluid without an infection, but the presence of fluid is a definite red flag.

I'm giving this product three stars based on the variability of the results. If it works accurately for you or your child, then it is easy to use and gives quick and painless results. On the other hand, it doesn't work for everybody. Truly a "your mileage may vary" situation.

If ear infections are a concern, I highly recommend buying an otoscope as your first line of defense. (An otoscope is that little light the doctor uses to check your ears.) The Earcheck device can also be used as a supplement to the otoscope.

We bought this monitor 6 months ago. I absolutely love the talk-to-baby and talk-to-other-receiver features. I have an older child who I can't seem to break of the habit of screaming for whatever he needs from whatever part of the house he's in, and it has been lovely to use this to talk to him and quietly say "please come downstairs and talk to me about it instead of shouting and waking the baby". I like the rechargeable receiver units much better than the plug-in or battery operated ones we've had before, and I've found the reception distance to be as reasonable as our other monitors.

That said - regardless of distance, reception will sometimes be dropped for no apparent reason. The receivers seemed to start holding less and less charge starting around month 2, and one of the two has stopped making any noise at all (though the lights still flicker when the transmitter has something to transmit.) Even when they appear to be working properly, there is no warning sound for a low receiver battery. The battery light turns red, but if you have the received clipped to your belt where you aren't looking directly at it, this is easy to miss. I don't know how many times I've thought that I was monitoring the baby until I suddenly heard screaming coming from upstairs and discovered that the receiver battery had completely died.

I hope that some of these problems get worked out. The monitor has enough going for it that I might consider getting a newer improved model even though my "baby" would be a preschooler by then. Just as an intercom and for monitoring playdates it would be worth it. But that's all rather moot if the thing doesn't work.

I read many reviews and specs before deciding on a high back booster. Overall I like the seat OK, but here are my concerns with the seat:
1. The arm rests do not move up and down. This doesn't seem like a big issue HOWEVER, the lap belt cannot get as close to her body as I would like because the armrest and the base of the armrest stick out to far. This really makes me question the safety of this seat and consider purchasing a new seat. My in laws have a Cosco high back booster which allows for the seat belt to be very tight against her and much safer, in my opinion.
2. The seat belt is not easy to latch. If you run the seat belt through the red clip holder, as it should be, and buckle the seat belt and pull the remaining slack out so the shoulder belt cannot move the seat belt does not have enough slack to re-buckle. Instead, you have to take it out of the red clip holder and let it to go back to a beginning position, re-thread through red clip holder and buckle. NOT convenient, at all! Right now I'm thinking I might switch with my in-laws and put their Cosco seat in my vehicle due to the safety features I mentioned and the convenience.
Note: I drive a 2012 Chevy Traverse. Different vehicles may have different experiences with the seat belt "locking" issue I mentioned.

I have been using the Embrace pump every day for 2 months and I pump about 8 oz a day to bottle feed. I think it is a good pump, but with reservations. Here are my observations:

Pros:

-Very attractive and discrete pump unit, it is fine to leave it on the counter. You don't need to leave it in a big, black bag.

-The low profile cups allow me to easily pump one-handed or slip the cups underneath a sports bra for hands-free usage. Time goes by much faster when I can check my email and pump at the same time.

-Comfortable. I used the hospital pump and I felt lots of uncomfortable stretching of my nipples. When I used the Embrace, at first I wondered if it was working - even at the highest setting - but I was letting down just fine and producing milk.

Cons:

-Noisy

-Assembly of the cups is a bit more involved. The soft cups need to snap into the housing just so, which has frustrated me endless times in the middle of the night when the lights are low and I'm tired.

-When I was engorged, the Embrace did not have sufficient suction to get me to let down. I had to rent a hospital unit for a week until the issue was resolved. Not a big deal, but important to know if you are suffering from engorgement, call the hospital if you can't let down with the Embrace. I have never used the Medela home units, so I don't know how it compares. I only use the Embrace on the highest setting, the lower ones are useless.

I think this is a good pump, but if you can try one out along with some other brands, you would be better off.

Like most other reviewers mentioned, tightening the harness straps on this model requires some serious force to get them to be properly snug. This is primarily due to the design of the hassle-free no-rethreading harness system which uses the adjustment of the head support apparatus as a method of repositioning the point of contact of the shoulder harness straps. Unfortunately, a design flaw in how the head support slides over and sits on top of the harness straps places far too much force on the straps causing excessive friction. So basically you're left with two options:
- Lift the head support so that it's high enough to avoid contact with the straps, meaning your child's head may not be properly supported
or
- Suck it up and deal with the frustration of trying to pull that strap each and every time you buckle your child in, with the risk that it's not properly tightened if enough force wasn't applied.

Thankfully, there's a third option if you're somewhat handy:
- Create a cylindrical spacer that can be placed between the head support and the padding of the seat to provide enough clearance so that the harness straps aren't being pinned down any longer. It was very easy to cobble together, I literally used half of a pencil, and wrapped it in some thin sheets of foam. Otherwise, I'm sure you can find something similar at your local hardware store.

Once I tucked the spacer in where it needed to go, the harness straps were extremely easy to tighten again, just as they were when the head support was in the fully upright position.

This stroller has some good features like the one hand fold and being relatively lightweight, but there are major drawbacks that make me feel that the stroller is not for us. First of all, this stroller is not like the other baby joggers that have an adapter for car seats. The one that Baby Jogger makes has a steel connector and this stroller just has a plastic slot. You can purchase the accessory set for this that includes the parent tray (also attaches by a cheap plastic slot), child's tray (which uses a plastic slot but that is at least hinged for easy in/out of stroller) and weather cover. However, you have to buy the whole set for forty dollars, which ups the price on this stroller to almost the city mini, which is a much better stroller (better fabric, padding, larger canopy). Albeit, you still have to buy the child tray but it's $20 and better built. The deal breaker is that I have not found a single car seat adapter that will work with this stroller - so bad on Amazon for saying so in its description! For that reason alone, we cannot use this stroller. Secondly, the stroller board that Baby Jogger makes will not work for this stroller. There is no bar to attach the stroller board to (although the Valco one will work). Lastly, the stroller is still quite bulky and takes up quite a bit of space still in the trunk. Yes, it's not too bad to carry or heist up into your trunk, but once it's in there, it takes about as much space as the other strollers do. So being lightweight is not a huge factor here since it's unlikely you will be carrying this one around a great distance. If you can afford it, I really like the City Mini GT as it runs very smoothly and has a nice hand brake versus foot brake, which is easier to use IMO. And it goes up to 65 lbs, which is nice. It is heavier but I don't notice the difference all that much. If price is an issue, I would still forgo this stroller and look for an earlier model of the City Mini. Albeebaby was having a sale for the City Mini that was pretty much the same price (actually a couple colors was ten dollars cheaper than this model at the time this was written) and you will get a much better stroller with more flexibility, especially if you want to use your car seat with your stroller. We have a Graco snugride classic connect and the universal car seat adapter works great with that one!

If you don't want to use a car seat with this stroller and don't need any accessories (unless you want to shell out $40 for the accessory set), then this isn't a bad stroller to get. The one hand fold is nice, canopy is still quite large, and the seat almost reclines flat. If you got the promo Amazon had with the fifty dollar gift card, then it's not a bad stroller for that price! Although, now I know why they had that promo only on this model. But at least you can add the accessory package with the gift card and not feel too badly about it. But the accessory package seriously feels like it should have come standard with this stroller (seriously $40 for some plastic pieces and a plastic weather wrap??) so I find it hard to shell out the bucks for that kit. Anyway, I don't think saving the seventy dollars is worth it between this stroller and the City Mini model. And look around to see what the best deals are out there, especially if you don't need the latest model out there.

This worked great for my baby from his first tastes of rice cereal until he was old enough to move on and sit in a normal chair - about age 2. This chair is STURDY. The straps are a little difficult to get through the openings to wash, but it's not too terrible. The seat is really comfortable - I was worried at first and thought that I should get one of those plush highchairs. But from 4-5 months old, my little guy sat upright just fine in it, because the seat isn't enormous and the tray is positioned low enough for him (some highchairs we saw had trays that came up mid-chest, or seat that were so reclined that he couldn't even get near the tray. I was surprised that he still fit it up until the time that he wanted to transition out of it.

The pneumatic feature works fine on ours, unlike some of the other reviewers. It's very easy to wheel around, which has actually been useful to us. Stains on the white parts come out pretty easily - a few have set in a little, but a "magic eraser" works nicely. The tray is small, like a lot of reviewers said - and that has been a little annoying fitting everything on it. Another annoying thing is that none of our relatives/babysitters have been able to figure out how to remove the tray to get our kid out (they end up pulling him out the top). If you're new to this whole thing, you have to bend over and try to read the instructions under the tray. It's the typical "simultaneously slide the spring-loaded bar over and pull toward you" so it requires a certain amount of finger dexterity and strength. My mother had trouble keeping the bar slid over all the way and then pulling it toward her at the same time. I was fine with it. But HERE'S MY BIG ISSUE: It's easy to clean the nice insert tray - it's a great design and can go right in the wash. However, the white tray that holds the clear insert tray is hollow (it's where the spring-loaded stuff is housed) and is definitely not intended to ever be opened. Here's the problem for super clean sorts of people. It can grow mold inside. You would be surprised that your kid can get food into the tiny openings in the tray where it clips into the seat, but it's possible. If you have a toddler like mine and have watched them eat, I guess you might not be surprised at all. But the problem with it is that it's tempting to run the whole tray under water to clean all the sides off that the insert tray doesn't cover. Then water gets inside the tray, and voila you have a perfect, dark, mold incubator. I peered in the side holes one time and was horrified. So I made my husband pry the tray apart, and I'm not sure it's the same again (there was a snapping sound, and it's never worked quite as well). It is not made to be cleaned so I guess you're just supposed to sponge-clean it and hope that water/food/etc never gets into it and you never develop a mold colony! I have cheaper highchairs that don't have an enclosed hollow tray and I sure am happier with those in that respect. Otherwise, this is a great highchair and I've really liked it.

Okay, I will keep this brief since you are likely a sleepless mommy or daddy right now...

PROS:
- It does work. It's a nice soothing SHHhhhhhhShhhhhhh sound for your kiddo to groove to.
- If it gets you even 15-30 minutes more sleep in your night the $ is well worth it (right?)

CONS:
-The timer function is silly to me. 15 minutes or 30 minutes those are your ONLY choices! Nothing more. The worst part of that timer is that when the time is up BAM the shushing just stops...mid-shush! It doesn't wind down to a quiet clean close, nope it just STOPS...at which point the baby tends to wake up about 84.5% of the time. What the heck - major design flaw there people!
- The controls for this thing just stink! It's like they were trying to win some design award or something and through functionality/usability down the list or something!? There is no means to get the same volume every time (it's the conical orange portion that controls the volume) and it just spins freely (with no clicks, no point of reference (to get the same volume twice), etc.) so if your kiddo squirms and you have this close enough to move the baby can mange to turn the volume up/down (think in car seat use).
- Replacing the batteries is more involved that I want and or need in the wee hours of the morning, see design complaints.
- Price (but see above re the extra minutes of sleep).

All that said, it is a clever thing to have, saves an ounce of sanity and with some design input from actual mom/dad users could be WAY better!

My wife and I picked up this monitor so we'd have one that could be checked remotely. We already had one that did not connect to WiFi but this one has a more fleshed out feature set so we gave it a go.

Out of the box it has some great features, and I was impressed by the flexible mount for the camera, so it was super easy to attach to the crib. It's non-smart features are pretty much plug and play... You just connect both the camera and parent unit to power and turn them on and you're good to go. The parent unit feels like a 10+ year old touch screen cell phone. It's slow, clunky, and often doesn't respond to touch. However it does show a nice clear picture of your baby day or night. It's simple to adjust the camera angle by swiping the screen as well. There are pretty standard 2 way speaker features and some white noise and lullaby's you can activate.

The smart features are set up through an app which is a little finnicky but I was able to successfully connect my camera to WiFi and therefore can view the baby on my phone. It also sends out notifications for movement and allows you to adjust camera settings, but just be aware the response time is much slower on the app so if you try to move the camera, just push the button once and wait for it to move. Just be warned there is a premium subscription available on the app that Hubble would really like you to buy, but it is optional.

When the monitor is working, it's really good. That being said, I've had a lot of issues with disconnecting - the parent unit loses signal with very slight movement or if you quickly move from room to room... and the only way to get it back is to walk back close to the camera and wave it around. It makes an awful, non-muteable beeping sound until it reconnects, as well. I don't live in an area with lots of houses or signal interference so I don't know why it struggles so much to stay connected. My other monitor never had this issue even clear across the house.

My intention was for this monitor to be our primary since it has a lot of great features. However it has become the backup option instead due to frustrations and inability to stay connected. I hope there is some kind of OTA update eventually that improves the connection stability, but for now I would recommend you explore your options before settling on this monitor.
