I got this pump through insurance and haven't had much luck with it. Some caveats: I'm a first time mom. I have an under supply. Worked with an licenced lactation consultant through all steps of my breast feeding journey. Have been using hands on pumping techniques/breast massage and hand expression.

So, this pump just never worked well for me. It has great suction, lots of different suction frequencies, and a wonderful battery.

I tried it out at home before returning to work and could never get more than an ounce out between my two breasts. I thought it was just my undersupply until I tried a manual pump. With the manual I was easily able to get 2.5 oz every pumping session with a faster letdown. I thought maybe I needed to replace the membranes or something, even though the pump was brand new. Even with replacing all the parts I could I saw no improvement in pumping. I thought perhaps it was too free form for me - maybe I needed a pump that just had preset intervals and strength to pick from because I had no idea what I was doing. Maybe if I used something with less choice I would see better results.

I really wanted to believe that it wasn't the pump. So, I purchased a Spectra to try out at home. I immediately was pumping less than I got with the manual pump, but double what I saw from Hygeia.

Now, several months later, I've returned to work full time I decided to give the Hygeia a try again. I tested it a couple of days before heading into work and saw results similar to what I was getting with the Spectra. So, I decided to go ahead and use the Hygeia at work because of the battery and easier to transport shape. But now after 2 weeks I'm going back to the Spectra. Slowly over the last two weeks my supply during the day has been dwindling, giving me less and less to take home at the end of the day. It hit a head yesterday when I found myself still engorged and uncomfortable at 3pm after pumping every 2 hours for at least 30 min. I had to go home early so I could feed my baby and get some relief.

Today I have pumped with the Spectra once and gotten more in one session than I saw in an entire day at the end of the last week with the Hygeia.

So, my conclusion is that it's a good pump but it just doesn't work for me. My lactation consultant has tried to help me and none of the suggestions have worked to address the issue. So, my recommendation is to give this pump a try if it seems like a good fit for you, but if you run into trouble like I did don't give up too easily. It could be the pump and not you that is the problem.

The concept of a reusable pouch is great. However, these pouches are only great in concept. They are severely lacking for everyday practical use.

-Reusable
-Strong zippered seal
-Cap is large enough to keep up with
-Dishwasher safe

Cons:
- Hard to open to it's full size. The bottom 'flaps' stick to each other and are hard to separate to allow you to fill the pouch properly.
-INCREDIBLY DIFFICULT TO CLEAN. If you have a Dr. Brown's nipple brush, you're a step ahead of the cleaning game. If not, good luck.
-Does not get clean in the dishwasher. Minuscule food particles get stuck around the inside pouch part.
-Difficult to fill because of the tabs on the top. They get in the way unless you have the time to use a funnel and a food that is thin enough to use a funnel.
-Very hard plastic means they are difficult to fill, to properly open and to wash. There's probably a good reason the non-refillable pouches are a softer, more malleable material.

Overall, I probably won't purchase more and will make the best out of what I have.

Before buying this, we actually thought that the bassinets were two separate units, that could be taken out one at a time.  Turns out that they are all one piece, and the bottom floor is actually moved to be the bottom of these bassinets.  The sheets made for these bottom parts don't fit at all.  Way too tight, so the 4 slats that are sewn inside the bottom to make it stiff will overlap, creating a rough surface.  We took the sheets apart and sewed two of them together to get a larger size that works.  The middle divider between the two bassinets sags slightly lower than any of the sides, so that there is an angle towards the middle divider, and the kids naturally start to roll that way.  Needs to be stiffer.  There are rods under the bottom, but they simply don't provide the support needed under the bassinets to keep this from happening.  When the bottom is used in the lower section, it seems to be fine because the middle support holds it up.  Bottom line, it isn't easy to go from using the lower level to using the bassinets, because you must remove the bottom out of the dual-bassinet part, to lay it in the bottom part.  This folding bottom, with the four slats to make it stiffer, must be threaded under the center divider between the dual bassinets, something not easy for everyone to do, as it is a very tight fit.  A last note, where you see a nice clean band around the inside of each bassinet, there is actually a HUGE warning sticker on one side.  I don't know why manufacturers advertise without these things in the photos.  Just an annoyance to see when it wasn't expected.  They do the same thing with their car seats.  HUGE warning stickers, right where your babies soft head will lean against.  Just show it as it is, not a cleaned-up publicity photo.

If you're buying a baby seat, I would say don't make your decision based on a desire to get something that will 'last longer'. Get the one that's better for your baby for the short period it does last. These seats have a very limited shelf-life in a baby's development cycle, and because of that, I say just get the Bumbo if you want one.

My daughter is pretty chubby, so after reading all the reviews I went with this seat because it sounded like it had more uses and a longer shelf-life than the Bumbo. However, she felt floppy in it and slumped over in a way that made me feel certain I was pushing her to do things she wasn't physically ready for. I returned it and decided to put the money towards the fancy high chair I wanted. I thought that was the end of story.

However, a few weeks later, we went to my MIL's and she'd bought a Bumbo at a yard sale. It was definitely a tighter squeeze, but I think that was a good thing because it seemed much more supportive for my little girl. She looked comfortable and happy in a way she did not in the Bebepod.

I know the Bumbo will probably only last 1-2 months tops, but if you really want to spend money on a baby seat, I think it feels safer and more supportive for babies whose bodies aren't made to sit on their own yet, which is the whole point isn't it?

I use this bottle warmer at work in the infant room at a daycare.
Here are the basics: Add a measured amount of water, put the bottle in, and push the button down. The button clicks and lights up when it's on. When the water is all evaporated, it shuts off. You hear a click and the light turns off. Remove the bottle, check the temperature of the milk on your wrist, feed to baby.
The directions are not great. It comes with a chart showing how much water to put in based on whether you're heating breastmilk, formula, or baby food, how many ounces, and whether it's room temperature or refrigerated. It's basically useless. This is the formula I use to figure out how much water to put in:
Refrigerated: For 4 oz, fill to line 4. For 5 oz, fill to line 5. And so on. It only goes up to line 5 so for 8 oz, you'll have to fill to line 5, dump, fill to line 3, dump. It comes out perfectly. It's inconvenient to fill the thing. The opening is small and I often spill. It's also inconvenient to have to dump, refill, dump to get the right amount. If it was large enough to have a line 8, it'd be better.
Room temperature: Follow the formula above, but divide by 2.

This fits every kind of bottle we've tried: Avent, Tommee Tippee, Dr. Brown's, Medela, Gerber... However, just because they FIT doesn't mean they work well. Here's what we've found:

For small (4 oz) sized bottles, use the included second basket to raise it higher above the water. This has two purposes. First, it is easier to remove the bottle without having to reach down into the warmer and risk burning your fingers with the steam. Secondly, it keeps it from overheating the milk.

Tommee Tippee and Avent wide-mouthed bottles: The ring around the nipple sometimes gets too hot. Take the ring off while heating to prevent this.
Drop-in liners: DO NOT use. They will melt. You will have to pour the milk into another bottle to heat, then pour it back into the drop-in liner to feed to baby.
Dr. Brown's: Occasionally milk will flow out of the air vent holes, spilling over into the warmer. The warmer then heats the milk, preventing the auto-shut off from activating. We don't hear the "click" alerting us that the bottle is warm. Several bottles have been completely drained because of this. We are alerted to what is happening by the sickening smell of burning formula once it gets low. We thought it was because of the discs under the nipple so we removed those, but it still happens. Now we remove the entire straw assembly while heating so that it cannot travel up the straw. I don't know that I'd consider this a flaw with the warmer or a flaw with the Dr. Brown bottles. However, we have no control over what bottles the parents bring for us to use. We do have control over what bottle warmer we choose. Considering that 5 out of 8 babies in our room use Dr. Brown bottles, it gets quite old removing the straws constantly, or cleaning up the mess and remaking the bottles when it overflows.

Overall, with some workarounds, it's a decent bottle warmer.

I purchased this because we had just set up a play room in the basement for my young grandchildren and wanted to be able to monitor them. At 4 and 5, they are ready to branch out to play without us nearby, but we knew that there would be times we'd want to see what they were up to.

For us, it was important to be able to talk to them.

Within the first half hour, my granddaughter climbed onto the play table and stood up, telling her brother she was queen of the hill. When her mom called out, "Get down from there!" she literally jumped about 8 feet, flying over the coffee table and landing on the couch! Her mom and I were surprised at her gymnastic skills, but we could barely contain our laughter as she sat on the couch, slowly scanning the room to try and figure out how her mom saw her. She called her brother over, asking him to help her find mom.

They came upstairs and my granddaughter said, "Mom, how did you know?" I was happy to tell her something I used to tell her mother decades ago...."Your mom has eyes in the back of her head!" Eyes wide, we told them to go back downstairs.

Not long afterward, they began to argue about the building blocks they were playing with. Once again, their mother called out and they froze. Once they realized mom wasn't in the doorway, they began to walk around the room, looking to find out where mom's voice was coming from. It didn't take very long for my grandson to find it. Again, we burst out laughing as he brought his face up close, trying to "see" his mom and asking if she was in there. Hilarious! (Too bad we can't record!)

Once the novelty wore off, it became a good tool for the simple fact that we could talk back and forth with them. There is a slight delay, so that can be confusing at times as they tend to talk over us. Now we can just tell them to clean up their toys and come upstairs. Much better than having to holler down the stairs.

We like that it scans the room, but the scanning is somewhat limited. It works for our needs, though, as for the most part we can see the children in almost every part of the room. (It doesn't pick up the floor area closest to the camera.)

My biggest peeve -- which seems to be common -- is that you cannot buy a spare camera. My youngest grandchild is coming for a one-week visit and I wanted to buy another camera to put into her room. She is just turning one this week, so I definitely need to monitor her in the crib. I thought I could just buy another camera, but I can't. Not happy about that, but i see the Foscam rep already made comments that they expect to have stand-alone cameras available soon. (Not soon enough to help me out, though.)

Because the packaging says you can connect up to four monitors and you can't (unless you buy four separate sets), I am giving this three stars. If it was available as advertised, I'd give it five. Overall we are extremely pleased as it does just what we wanted -- monitor the children and gives us the capability to talk back and forth. Once we are able to buy the second camera, I'll come back and re-address my review.

The cons: unlike other wetbags these bags are single layered- there's no outer fabric covering. When I've got a wet diaper in one, it feels damp to the touch. It's not actually damp (I've tested to see if it was leaking), but it's not a pleasant feeling when digging through my diaper bag. The drawstring gets really hard to pull tight. All-in-all; they're good for my use as a back-up bag. I'm not sure I'd use on a regular basis though.

I didn't buy this for use as a baby monitor, but rather a camera to view/listen to people in another room playing an escape game I host. I was replacing a similar system from a different company that was over 10 years old. I was not very impressed with this.

PROS
-No static or cutting in/out
-Reliable
-Temperature monitor is nice

CONS
- Pans very slowly
- Audio cuts out when panning
- When you send out audio there is about a 2 second delay until you can hear audio again, so any response is cut off - can't be used effectively for 2 way communication
- Limited angles - I put this in the same spot as my old camera, but could see far less going on directly below the camera.
- Inconvenient buttons: To turn on/off you have to hold down the power button, rather than a simple switch. To change the volume, you have to press the volume button, then up/down on keypad, then the center button to confirm (video is cut off during this time to see the volume icon and what level you are at) - rather than a simple volume dial.
- Dark - Using this in a fairly dark room and it was harder to make out details than previously.

Overall, I am keeping it because my old camera is cutting in and out and will eventually break. But I would have expected the technology to get better, not worse, with 10 years!

I am a disappointed in this product.

My issues with it:

Wrong recommended extension size: Our opening is 46 3/4" wall to wall and 46 1/4" baseboard to baseboard. For that size they recommended the 10" extension but that was too big. It barely could squeeze in there with the extension and just one set of tension rods put in. So I switched to the 7" extension.

Top and bottom of swing gate do not line up:
I used a level to make sure that everything was level/aligned and not tilted. I tightened all the rods into place and continued to check that everything was still level and not tilted. However, once everything was done being tightened, I swung the door closed and the top lined up with the clasp, but the bottom did not. The metal pieces that hang down to catch the bottom metal rail rested completely outside the bottom rail, creating a misalignment of about 1 1/2 - 2". I thought perhaps I had installed it tilted afterall and tried changing the angle (keeping the top rail in place and pushing the bottom rail further in the direction that the bottom of the swing gate rested), but it didn't make a difference. The rails were now no longer vertical and the bottom was still misaligned, so I slid it back in place so the rails were vertical.

The only option I had was to drop the metal pieces over the bottom rail and pull as firmly and gently as I could to bend the gate into proper alignment. Now, after pulling on it a bit, it still is slightly misaligned and takes a bit of finesse to get it to drop into place (align top, then push with my foot to make the bottom align as well). I'm really frustrated because I have three other young children who will need to operate this and I paid for a better quality gate so it would be that easy.

Rail ends/cap not firmly/permanently attached: After I had attached the 10" piece as recommended for a 46 1/2" gate and had to remove it because the 7" piece is what I really needed; the plastic inserts, that are *not* supposed to be removeable, were pulling out (which would leave a gaping rectangular hole in the metal rail. I was able to push them back into place, but it leaves me doubtful as to their reliability in the future when I may need to change out the extensions.

Chipped Wood: There was a little bit of the wood chipped in the top curve of the gate. Granted, it was just a little; but when you're putting money into a nice gate that is supposed to be easy to use and has a classier look, you want it to arrive in that intact state.

So, overall, I was definitely disappointed in this gate. I'm only keeping it because I think over time if I keep pulling on it, it'll eventually warp back into its proper shape (my guess is that in the shipping process, the lack of support for the swinging gate piece within the packaging--the ends of each four points were supported, but the gate was free to move 1-1 1/2" in the box--led to it's warped state). Everyone gets unlucky sometimes with their orders; so *maybe* that's what happened in my case and I simply received a gate that wasn't representative of their usual quality.

Before I realized that these rice snacks are made in China, I gave them occasionally to both of my kids when they were first transitioning to solid foods. My babies loved them because the taste is very mild and they dissolve in the baby's mouth quite easily to make eating them easy for the baby. These biscuits barely have any calories or any nutritional value so I used them only on occasion for baby feeding training. And I was quite pleased with them because my babies enjoyed eating them so much.

However, once I learned that these biscuits are made in China I stopped buying them. I don't prefer to buy baby food items produced in China as I know that their manufacturing protocols are not as stringent as they are in the US. Instead, I switched to buying puffs by Happy Baby and other biscuits by Plum Organics. Since Baby Mum-Mums are just basic rice biscuits many consumers are probably fine with knowing that Baby Mum-Mums are made in China. However, I believe that a lot of U.S. consumers do not realize that these biscuits are made in China when they purchase them. Anyhow, I now read the labels of all baby food products that I buy much more diligently to double check that they are made in the USA under US Safety standards.

The bottom line is that if it does not bother you that these biscuits are made in China, then I am sure your baby will love eating them and they do work well when the baby is learning to feed because they are very mild, dissolve quickly and are so easy for the baby to eat.

There was a long wait before I could send it in because I couldn't read the SN (badly placed label right where you're bound to scrape it as you hang the camera on a screw). But when I did finally get an authorization, it was repaired and returned very quickly.
Having now used both a Foscam IP camera and this Samsung one, I can give a bit of a comparison.
In favor of Foscam: Can use any smartphone or tablet as a monitor, and you can have more than one going at once. Clearer picture and better infrared. A lot more flexibility, like flipping the image etc. to accommodate all sorts of camera placement. Can view over the internet (though we kept ours totally private behind our network firewall)
In favor of Samsung: No delay in picture and sound like with an IP camera. Battery lasts much longer on a charge than my iPhone when it was streaming Foscam video. Much easier to speak to your baby (with an IP camera there's a weird delay). Camera is smaller and lighter.

**Update: Thanks to the comment from another customer, I was able to get the piece from Million Dollar Baby very easily. If your crib arrives with a broken piece, you should DEFINITELY go through them instead of calling Amazon. Amazon still shipped the other crib to me, and then I was not able to have it picked up, so I had to drag it myself to UPS. 90+ lbs is not something I want to be lugging around while pregnant! However, do call Amazon and they should give you a 20% discount for the damaged item if you choose to keep it.

SO FRUSTRATED... I was so excited to open this item. Opened it up, unpacked it, started assembling it, and about half way through (and over an hours worth of time) I realized that the top rail had splintered and a piece broken off. I contacted Amazon right away, and was told that the entire crib has to be returned. They cannot simply replace the broken piece. I asked if I could talk to the manufacturer and the customer service agent explained to me that they would ultimately refer me back to Amazon since the order is fulfilled through them, and I would just be going through more of a hassle. So, now I have to disassemble the crib, repack and somehow fit it back into the box, and then take a day off work so it can be picked up from my house. Then, the replacement will be shipped of an entire new crib. All the labor I have already put into and will put into returning the crib is frustrating. Loosing a day of work is extremely annoying. Plus, the shipment of the new crib will take a week - whereas when I initially placed the order, it arrived in 2 days. How is that fair?! Customer service was extremely poor on this and I am now seriously considering removing my online registry from Amazon if this is how problems with orders will be solved in the future. I will post an update once the item is returned and the replacement has arrived. I am extremely disappointed with this purchase!

I did not Kiinde pouches for formula, and I never pumped enough to try using them for milk, but I had a lot of pouches left over so I decided to use them for baby food, and this is where it really shines.

I make my own baby foods by steaming anything that needed to be steamed in the microwave or instant pot, and then putting all ingredients into the squeeze bottle and blending using an immersion blender. The squeeze bottle works a lot better than I thought it would for filling the pouches. We also have two kiinde funnels from my formula experiments that also work well if I mix or blend in a different container.

Since I have twins, freezing food in 6oz portions works, since we can have them share a pouch and go through it in 2 meals. With just one baby, a 6oz pouch may be too much until their food intake increases. I have had no issues freezing food in the bags, but I'm always careful to leave enough headroom for expansion while freezing.

We've never used the spoon attachment since we give our babies their own spoons; we use the spout attachment to squeeze onto food. The spout is wide enough for chunkier mashes, not just purees. We are hoping that they will learn to eat directly from pouches soon.

The one advantage that store bought pouches have is that they don't need to be refrigerated before opening, so these would need an ice pack to be an on the go snack.

The pouches are not reusable, which is another consideration. They are fully recyclable, though, and I think that we're going to be out of the puree/mash stage and on to table food before I use all the pouches that I have (from the pumping kit + this kit).

Update: Removed a star because we stopped using these after just a couple weeks. It wasn't cost effective compared to grocery store pouches when found on sale. Also they dont take ChooMee bite valves. We ended up using a combination of grocery store pouches and homemade food in reusable pouches, and will probably continue to offer snacks (not meals) that way through their toddler years.

I have had nothing but Britax seats for my son and have always loved them.  I feel they are the safest and I won't buy anything else.  I specifically bought this seat because I wanted to use it as a booster at some point and it is the only one I know of that can be both latched and anchored.  While I still feel it is very safe, it is certainly a pain to deal with!  First, installation is far from easy.  You certainly don't want to be moving this thing around very often.  It's heavy and huge.  I didn't have many problems when I was using the 5 point system, but now that I have converted over to the seat belt/booster seat with my son, it is extremely annoying.  The belt gets stuck in the shoulder routing area each and every time he uses it. It gets twisted and mangled and my son cannot even buckle himself in because of this.  Now I have to strap him in every time.  I thought a booster seat was supposed to build a child's independence.  Instead, now I have to strap in my 6 year old every time he gets into the car.  Additionally, the belt will not retract when he unbuckles himself, again because it is stuck in the seat's shoulder routing area.  It just hangs twisted and loosely, often getting shut in the car door. After spending close to $300 on this seat, I really don't want to have to buy another one, nor do I want a less safe seat for him.  However, I'm far from happy about how this seat is functioning as a booster.

I have had this play yard for about a year now, when my baby was 6 months old. The first problems I had was that her legs would get stuck in the slots on each of the panels. Being so young she would twist to get her leg unstuck, causing her leg to twist and make it worse.

Eventually after watching her carefully and helping her when she did get her leg stuck, she learned to stop doing that.

Time went by and the play yard was great. I was able to get things done knowing she was safe.

That was until she was around 14-15 months old, and she learned to climb. If you look at the panels there are slots and above the slots is a big open cloud shape. Well my baby learned to put her feet in the slots and then lift a foot into the cloud and then she pulls herself up and over the entire panel and escapes.

I was shocked to be honest, but the open slots and the open cloud part is perfect foot holes for a determined baby.

Unfortunately, I had hoped for this to have lasted for a few years but sadly it’s not practical to use anymore and presents a danger of her falling. If you have a spry or determined baby, I would suggest finding a playpen that doesn’t have perfect escape holes lol

It was a great play yard for the first 6 months, but now I wish I had gotten something else. Back to looking for something else!

I do love that this warms the wipes, my toddler knows when he's changed downstairs that the wipes are cold and he does all he can to avoid a downstairs diaper change. So it's certainly great for keeping the wipes warm. However, after 18 months of use, there are some issues. First - the tab that keeps the pop up top shut is no longer effective and I have to try numerous times to get it to stay shut, sometimes requiring me to stuff the wipes all the way back into the bottom portion. Second - there is a pliable grey "thing" that the wipes are pulled through and this has become worn - it's no longer as pliable and is clearly drying out. I imagine it'll start to crack and break eventually. Third - if you have multiple changing stations and aren't turning over the inventory in the warmer quickly enough they do turn brown and dry up. Because the warming plate is on the bottom of the unit, those wipes closest to the bottom dry out quickly. I have seen the top layers soaking wet and the bottom layers dry as bone. Fourth - the pillow definitely needs to be changed regularly, it also browns and dries out and becomes hard and crusty. Overall it works as I expected and the negatives are really just moderate annoyances to me. I use this high chair 3-4 times per day, just about every day. I have SUCH a love-hate relationship with this thing.

The good:
-compact, with a narrower footprint than a lot of other models of highchair, and it folds down nicely -- this is so much nicer than some of the other highchairs out there that take up way more space
-baby seems really comfortable in the chair -- the name "siesta" is appropriate as he has fallen asleep in this thing a few times and he is NOT an easy guy to get to sleep, and he also can sit in this chair for long (e.g., 40 minutes) durations before getting squirrelly, whereas we have a cheapy Fisher-Price chair at his gramma's house that he will only willingly sit in for 30 minutes tops.
-double-layered tray so that you can feed your baby and take off the top layer to clean
-relatively easy to move about -- I disagree with the other reviewers who said moving it is challenging, you just press and slide buttons on either side to lock or unlock the wheels

The bad:
-the tray.... urgh..... the tray really needs a complete redesign in terms of how it attaches to the chair. My baby got the skin of his thumb caught in the insert holes between the tray and the chair -- before you judge me and think that I just wasn't paying attention, you should really attempt to put a squirmy baby into this thing -- the pinch happened so fast and he wailed but was ultimately fine, and though it was just a small pinch, we have practiced "hands up" every time I put in the tray.
-to put the tray into the chair, you have to insert your fingers into a pull that is located in the center front of the tray. In doing so, my mom and I both pinched our fingers in that part.
-the double-layer system, while great in theory, has a lip on the bottom part of the tray that food always gets trapped in, so you have to clean that part off anyway
-cleaning the straps is a project -- the kid gets goop all over the straps and you have to remove them with a screw driver and soak in hot water with Dawn detergent to really get them clean, especially when the kid is still putting everything into his mouth
-cleaning food out of some of the crevices of this thing is also irritating

Overall, we're satisfied with this chair because the baby likes being in it, but we all have to be cautious every time we use it and think the tray could use a serious redesign. For the cost, this should be a 100% aggravation-free product, I feel.

UPDATE: I wrote this review about a year and a half ago, but my sentiments still stand. As my child has grown, I have found new things to love and hate about this contraption every day. Love: It's the only high chair that my toddler will sit in. It has two issues that the buyer should be aware of:

#1: It has a mounted piece that you screw onto the wall for the lower anchors. If you have baseboards, then this is a problem because there's not any give to account for the lower bracket coming out from the wall more than the upper one- and that's assuming your baseboard is high enough for the whole thing to fit. Mine wasn't.

#2: It's a tad misleading when it says the dimensions it can handle. This thing does not telescope to get wider- the side panels have to be angled to accommodate different sized spaces. If you're putting this thing in a corner, or at the top of stairs, this can be a problem because you have to account for it suddenly "having depth" to fit (viewed from above, it's like a rectangle without a top).

Hence, the ideal situation for this thing is a home with no baseboards, where you want it to fit a 71" space. Otherwise there are some considerations to be made.

A couple points of comparison on the Pampers diapers. We have been loyal to Huggies for many years but had occasionally used Pampers or other brands out of necessity. These Pampers were ordered out of necessity when people were hoarding diapers and other products during the corona virus lock downs. This purchase made me reaffirm my loyalty to Huggies.

First off, I noticed the Pampers were thinner than the Huggies Plus Diapers we were using. The thinner diapers did cause these to be less absorbant as evidenced by overnight leakage that was never present before when using Huggies. The other thing I noticed about these Pampers is they smell. Just like every other Pampers product I have used before they have this signature baby powder smell. You can smell it from several feet away and it is a smell that I don't particularly care for.

These diapers were fine for us for regular daytime use, but they appear to be overall less absorbant than Huggies. I am taking off one star each for both absorbance and smell making this a three star diaper. I would go with Huggies or Kirkland brand before buying Pampers diapers again, but they are still better than other brands such as Loves or Mama Bear. Bottom line, you could do better but could also do worse than these diapers.

I really wanted to maintain brand loyalty...but. I used this product for my child from birth and was really happy with these diapers in the beginning. They were a great fit, performed with excellence,well priced (with subscribe and save + Amazon Mom) and reasonable environmental compromise for a parent who doesn't own a washing machine to make cloth diapering feasible.

I was slightly less happy with the size 2 diaper. They were not bigger, meaning wider -just longer--freakishly long, & my baby is in the 95th percentile for length. Baby grew out of this size before we could finish the box, and my baby is very skinny.

Then came the real disappointment with the size 3 diapers. They are, thankfully, wider than the previous sizes, but they are constructed in manner that encourages leaks. The extra width comes from the addition of fold-out, non-elaticized tabs to wrap around the baby's midsection, and the pee comes pouring out. So does the poo.

And what smells worse than what your baby leaves in a diaper??? The diaper itself. THE SIZE THREE DIAPERS STINK! They have a sour chemical smell to them which is only made worse by baby's additions.

If I hadn't had the good fortune of Amazon taking 12 days to deliver my next shipment, I might have accepted that this is the way diapers are. But I ran out and had to go to Whole Foods to buy alternative granola diapers. The seventh generation free and clear diapers fit my skinny long baby well, and don't have the horrible smell to them. Although they are not as biodegradable as the Nature Baby care diapers, I have to prioritize performance. I've been peed on too many times this month.

I guess what I've learned from my adventures in diapering is that I might have to use different products and different stages, but I'd love to come back to nature baby if the smell improves and the fit is right.

Based on the stellar reviews this product had, and because I'm tall, I purchased the Brest Friend instead of a Boppy. However, after my (unplanned) C-section I found this pillow impossible to use. It was too firm and pushed uncomfortably on my sore abdomen, and with my limited mobility it was difficult to get the strap around me (and painful to clasp). A few days post-partum, I had the opportunity to try a Boppy, and then rushed out and bought my own, and used that exclusively until I healed up.

Once I was more mobile, I found the Brest Friend useful for daytime nursing-- I liked that I could sit more upright than with the Boppy, which saved my back. However, in the middle of the night, I went back to the boppy because it was just way easier to wrangle in the dark. Also, the Boppy was handy later on for tummy time and when she was learning to sit up.

So, I found both nursing pillows had their uses, and don't regret having both. But to be honest, if I had to choose only 1, I'd go with the Boppy.

The description on this is a bit deceiving - it's an over-priced night light. It's not a 'kit' - in my mind a kit is something that you assemble or put together before you use it. There is no assembly required for this, other then setting the dome on top of the stem. It's pretty, and fun to watch, the colors are very bright and vibrant. My 6 year old who had outgrown her Twilight Turtle enjoyed using this in her room. Much like the Twilight Turtle - this works best if you have it in the center of the room and up high on something, then the images are clear and distinct. If it's too far away from the ceiling or wall the images will be blurry and very indistinct.

There are several light options to choose from - you can stick to one color or choose a variety, there are 8 options to choose from. 3 AAA batteries are required - while the description here on Amazon's website say the batteries are included, the back of the box indicates they are not. My mushroom did not come with any batteries. I was a bit disappointed that they don't make it to use an a/c adapter cord, so you don't have to burn through a bunch of batteries. There is an auto-shut off feature for bedtime so it doesn't keep going all night long.

I was a bit surprised when I opened the box - the dome of the mushroom is a very thin layer of plastic that isn't even attached to the stem. You just set the dome on top, and I imagine it would easily be cracked or crushed if younger kids were using it and not being very careful. I think the ages 5 and up as recommended by the manufacturer is a good idea. And am I the only one who doesn't like the description of 'Uncle Milton in My Room...'?? It sounds a little pervy to me, not to mention makes the name of the product very long. Personally I just would have said 'Moonlight Mushroom' and left it at that.

Low Battery Notification - while the battery on this one isn't as good as my old one, that doesn't bother me as much as me not being notified when the battery is dying. Again, my Motorola one beeped as soon as the battery was dying so you knew you needed to plug it in.

It was massively hard to rate the Stork Craft Concord six drawer dresser, and if I could I would give it a star rating of three and a half. And technically, if I could give separate star ratings based on aesthetics/functionality I'd give that a whopping 5 stars, and shipping/ease of putting it together, I would give a flat out 1.

The miniature nightmare started when I tried opening the box. I opened one side, couldn't pull out the other end to see the furniture, and figured I had it upside down. My husband righted it, and I opened the other side to see the same thing, which was a large brown box inside the packaging with no flaps for opening on either side. So I laid the heavy box on its side, and cut along one side to finally peel the outer box off the inner one. Once that was taken care of I opened the box to find a mass of Styrofoam. We're talking crumbled Styrofoam everywhere, that clung to each and every piece of the dresser, to me, to the room I was in, it was insane. I had to clean each piece when I took them out, and after the box was removed I had to vacuum all the Styrofoam up before I could even attempt to put it together.

And also imagine my surprise when I couldn't put it together due to broken pieces. The top castor on the inside of the left part of the dresser is attached to a wood piece that was almost completely unattached to the panel. Only one tiny staple on one side was even holding it on. And the castor below that one also had to be pushed back down. Luckily I had nails and Gorilla glue, and went to work fixing it. The frame that goes around the dresser also had a full crack in the middle as someone apparently drilled a hole splitting the wood. I used some Gorilla glue on that as well, but it's a noticeable crack in the front. And the last part of the dresser to be damaged is the very top. One corner of the dresser was damaged, being pushed up slightly, and the color was scraped off on that side. However, this damage looked to be from the actual shipping unlike the other two damages. There was nothing I could do for this, but purchase a furniture marker in the same hue, and try to color it in. I did wait a full day for everything to dry before attempting to put it together again.

Personally, I believe two people should put this together, and please have someone with a lot of upper body strength. I'm a small female, and tried tackling this on my own, and was there for hours. The drawers are first to put together, and putting the little dowels in with Gorilla glue was the only thing that was easy on this dresser. The slats for the drawers have a small groove that the bottom board is supposed to fit into. I managed to get two of those bottom portions in perfectly without a struggle. The other four I had to mash into the slots and push and prod, and exert a lot of energy to get it to fit. Each drawer slat also has these "easy" (I say this very, very lightly) hinged areas that when pulled back turns a small metal "screw" that is supposed to fit easily into the holes made. Once the hinge is pushed back into place the "screw" turns, locking the slat into place. This was the most difficult, and aggravating thing I have ever done. I had to pry these "easy" hinges up with my nails, and trying to get them back into place was seriously a thing of nightmares. A few went back easily, but the majority was so difficult that I finally got the hammer, and used the tool to help me push the hinges down. I didn't hammer them down, I simply used the head of the tool to help me as I used my weight to push them down. I finally quit on some of them as I couldn't get them even with the tool, and left them for my husband, who is very, very strong, and he even had a hard time trying to get them down. I swear my thumb felt like it was going to fall off after all the pushing on the hinges I did.
Once the drawers were done I tackled the actual dresser. Much to my dismay, the other panel for the side area of the dresser had one piece of wood too far down, and the screw could not fit into it so I had to scrape away until I scraped enough wood out of the way to where it would fit. From there, the frame went on the front, the bottom, and finally the top portion (which my husband did help with those areas).

The dresser is very beautiful, even though the top is damaged on a corner, but we put that facing the wall, and the frame around the top drawer still has an evident line through it where it cracked and I glued it back together, but in all, it still is very eye catching. I honestly have no fear of it tipping over, but there is a small piece of material that came with it to be attached to the wall and to the dresser to make sure it doesn't, which is very nice.

I hate the fact that it came damaged, because while it is still beautiful I almost feel as if it isn't worth the hassle of trying to put it together or the hassle of trying to contact the company about the damage. It's a nice, solid dresser, once totally fixed, but I feel many people wouldn't want to spend that much money on something that could come to them damaged.

So I will start with the fact that I have purchased 4 different monitors :
1) 2.4GHz DIGITAL WIRELESS BABY VIDEO MONITOR SYSTEM WITH NIGHT VISION -- 2.4" Color LCD Screen (Two-way Radio communication) by Smart AV ,
2) MOBICAM DXR DIGITAL MONITORING SYSTEM,
3) SAMSUNG WIRELESS VIDEO SECURITY MONITORING SYSTEM w/ 3.5" LCD,
4) SUMMER BABY TOUCH COLOR VIDEO MONITOR by Summer infant.
I have a 3yr. old and I was still using my Sony baby call monitor which I still love, but now I need to see when she gets out of her bed and I wanted the two way feature "talk to the baby feature" so I could talk to her and tell her to get back in her bed. I should also say that I want to see as much of her room around her bed as I could her room is 11 ft. by 12ft I put the camera in the corner on a shelf six feet off the ground about 10 and ½ ft away from her bed, so if she got out of her bed I could see where she was. I could also see her during the day playing in her room. Well, let me say that they at least now don't make a monitor with a "clear" picture.

So I bought the 2.4 GHz MONITOR by SMART AV: It was good I could see her ok during the day, and at night with the night vision and I could hear her and she could hear me when I talked on it.
CONS: Not the best picture but it was good enough. The camera did not adjust down far enough I had to put a coaster under the back half to get it to angle down some more. The big problem was it did not have the rechargeable batteries the other reviewers said it had. (Amazon told me it was probably because they bought it from a different seller not DBroth.) You can put regular batteries in it but if you want to plug it in you have to remove the batteries first. I tried to purchase the rechargeable batteries from them it has been a week and a half they still have not answered my emails. I returned it. Update: I never received a response.

Next up the MOBICAM DXR DIGITAL MONITORING SYSTEM: it had a ok picture during the day a little grainy but you could see. Night vision was grainy but ok. CONS: grainy day and night vision, when you touch the talk button to speak to the child it did not always work I would have to let it go and press it again to get it to work. I had it replaced with a new one thinking it might have been that one and the new one did the same thing. I called Amazon and they said they are not selling these directly anymore because of that happening to the batch of these they had maybe a bad batch they are investigating it, but you can still buy it from third party sellers on Amazon. UPDATE: Amazon is now selling them again.

Next up, was the SAMSUNG WIRELESS VIDEO SECURITY MONITORING SYSTEM w/ 3.5" LCD: this one had the best picture of them all but only for during the day (although it had a yellow glow at the top of the screen from the light in the room but the light was not in the cameras view I adjusted the camera down even further and it still remained. It has a nice night light and music that you can turn on and off from the monitor. I really, really wanted to like it.
CONS: The camera did not adjust down far enough for me, so I put a coaster under the back half to angle it down some more, There were also some "delays" (like when walking or just moving fast the screen would "miss some frames/some of the movement" in the picture.) The temperature gauge was not correct, the alarm for detection of sound in the room was a pain to adjust, the zoom function was a BIG pain you have to go into the menu out of the "picture screen" and put it on zoom then go back to the "picture screen", the volume was not very loud at all my husband was like it doesn`t turn up louder than that? The "talk to the baby" function was "choppy"(not as clear as the summer infant baby touch) and my absolute deal breaker was, I would think the MAIN REASON you would purchase a monitor like this the night vision: at night with and without a night light on in the room I could barely see anything much less my daughter in her bed you would really have to stare and look good to make any thing out, the infrared led's must not be strong at all. (If you want it for close up it might work I don't know never tested close up tested all of them in the same place about 10 and 1/2 feet away from her bed up on a shelf I need to see at least part of the room around her bed.)

I was so aggravated by this search, I printed out a twenty percent off coupon from the internet for Babies R Us and went and bought the SUMMER INFANT BABY TOUCH MONITOR, the new one they have with the touch screen monitor and pan and zoom camera. I put it to the test compared it to the SAMSUNG and MOBI. My two most important things were the night vision to see her at night and the "talk to the baby" function so I could talk to her. This summer infant model has a secure private connection unlike the other summer infant monitors. Its picture is ok (not HD but none of them are) slightly, slightly, slightly grainy during the day but still really good, and its night vision although a little grainy was the best out of all of them for the distance, (again I did not test close up) plus I can move the camera around remotely from the monitor to see where she's at in the room and I can zoom in easily the functions appear below and to the right of the picture when you touch the screen although the closer you zoom in the grainier it got but that was with ALL of the models I tested.

AFTER A LOT OF TESTING AND DEBATE, I RETURNED THEM ALL EXCEPT FOR THE SUMMER INFANT BABY TOUCH MONITOR. I really like it. I am glad I just went ahead and spent a little more money and bought it. The pan and zoom features work great. (THIS IS THE ONLY MONITOR OUT OF THE ONES I TESTED THAT HAS THE ACTUAL PAN FEATURE. THE ABILITY TO MOVE THE CAMERA AROUND THE ROOM REMOTELY FROM THE CONTROLS ON THE MONITOR. The Samsung does not have the pan feature.) I can see her WHOLE room day or night. After a certain amount of time it goes into power save mode when it is not on the charger and turns off the picture but you can still hear the sound and if you want to see the picture again just press the button on the top. If it is on the charger the picture will stay on unless you press the button on the top to turn the screen back off. The monitor has a lithium-ion battery and the camera has the option to put regular batteries in it if you can not plug it in a outlet. Listen, this is way better than spending $200-300+ at Baby's R Us or Buy Buy Baby for something that is also made in China plus this has shelves that slide out and a dirty clothes hamper. This is a changing table and it serves a purpose; put baby supplies in it and changing your babies diapers. For the price its hard to complain but there is one major complaint I have to mention. Received the item quick as usual from Amazon which is great and it was packaged well. As expected "Made in China" was everywhere on the box which is typical  and expected for the price. But it seemed sturdy, the color was good and it matched other furniture we had already, so good so far. Once I started putting the table together, it was pretty easy and instructions were pretty typical. Ok I have the thing all standing up and ready to screw in the parts that hold on the sliding shelves. Oh wait a minute there is no screw hole to put the screws in, hmmmmm maybe I have the wrong piece somewhere, let me see, no this is the right piece and the only one that fits here, ok so I guess they just didn't put the screw holes in? Well at this point (only took 30 minutes so far) I really wanted take it all apart, put it in the box and send it back but then I remembered it was only $99, I am  already almost completely done so what should I do? Well the wood is only particle board so I decided to make my own holes with a small drill, easy enough took an extra 5 minutes. Just line them up decent, doesn't have to be perfect and there you go. So that worked for me just fine, got it all setup and it looks good and works well. The part the baby lays on is particle board with a small pad to put over it but strong enough that I felt comfortable putting my baby on it. If this thing wouldn't have been missing screw holes I would have loved it, especially for the price. Maybe you will be a lucky one that gets the screw holes and it will make your life a bit easier. You can't beat the price, it has shelves, looks nice, sturdy and serves its purpose well!

Positive[s]
- Price - $139 shipped.
- Looks asthetically pleasing when finally put together

Negative[s]
- If you HATE, LOATHE, and DESPISE putting together Ikea furniture - you're gonna really hate putting this together as parts of the instructions require a bit of figuring out [ie: step 5 and 6 - installing the drawer tracks is not clear unles you ignore the first of 2 drawings]
- M3.5 x 12mm flat head wood screws included with the kit do not sit flush on the left and right track panels which prevents the drawers from moving in/out smoothly. Fix for this is to get ~24 x #5 x 1/2" flat head philip's wood screws instead - as this allows the head of the screw to sit flush with the track and makes it so the drawers move in/out without draggin/catching on a screw head.
- Speaking of drawer tracks - there are no pre drilled holes but the drawings are clear on how to install the drawer tracks. You can either use the screws included with the kit or #5 - 1/2" screws that you have to buy seperately.

I'm amazed at all the fantastic reviews on this stroller. I'll admit, I didn't buy this on Amazon, instead I used another store where I had a coupon. But, I did read through every single one of these reviews before purchasing. I ended up buying this sight unseen and purely off the glowing reviews. Now I wish a store by me actually had this in stock so I could have tested it out because I'm not sure if I would have gotten it. I already own a side by side, but sadly my oldest gets annoyed with his little sister and sometimes tries to reach over and swat at her if she coos to much so I began the search of a tandem. I almost sprung for the Uppababy Vista 2015 or the Baby Jogger City Select but there were some reviews here that compared this to the Baby Jogger so I figured I would save some money and go with this.

First off, for $299 to get all of these features something has to give, and quality is what does. The seats are really cheap and flimsy. My oldest only weighs 26 lbs so we are still okay but, if I push on the seat where their bottoms goes it folds in on itself. When my kiddos are actually going to push the weight limit on this it does give me some concerns. I ended up buying some Tivoli stroller cushions to make it better, however they make the seat even shorter for their bottoms so I'm not sure that was the way to go. The straps are super cheap but I do like that there is a 5 point harness.

This thing feels like you are pushing a tank, now I know that most tandems are harder to push then a side by side but I just went out to a store a few weeks ago to test out various models after buying this because I was having buyers remorse. Other, yet more costly models, push a LOT easier. Yesterday I was using this stroller to go up a hill and holy crap it's like pushing a freight train. The foam on the handle bar seems like that cheap foam that come summer with hot sweaty hands they will probably get a little sticky and stained from the foam. Also, going up curbs in this thing is freakishly hard as well.

Though one element that makes it a beast to drive is the length, but I do actually like this feature. It is really long, much much longer then other tandems. The only nice thing about this is that the seats are not rammed into one another as most tandems are. This stroller has much more leg room between the seats then others do. That said, you still can't comfortably recline the two seats well, which is why I originally went for a side by side. I don't think I would ever want this stroller if I needed to nap kiddos at the same time. The buggy thing about napping kids in this stroller is that you can't get a true flat recline, the legs are always bent in the sitting position which is a negative for me.

The basket on this is fantastic! It's super huge, my 2 year old crawled into it comfortably when I was putting it together. I really like the side zips to get stuff out because if not for those it is a little hard to access if you are using the car seat adapter.

Speaking of the car seat adapter, this one is really low quality. Now I'm fan of the Snap n' Go stroller and have a review there as well so I'm not totally concerned about the car seat "snapping" or "locking" into position for safety. I'm not sure if it is because of the design of this adapter, but it's flimsy with the car seat in it. It rocks back and forth. UPDATE 5/17/2018
Since we bought these a couple years ago we have had 6 of the 12 break. There typically isn't any warning, they just break. My 2-year-old son was closing the cabinet and the white piece broke. We now have 4 cabinets without functioning locks. I ordered another package but it's frustrating that they break as easily as they do. I still think they are a great product and help deter new kids from getting into cabinets, but I wish they lasted longer (some are still going strong even though they are opened multiple times a day). One plus is that they are relatively easy to remove, according to my wife, as she has had to take them off so we can replace them.

UPDATE 11/12/2016
We had another one of the safety latches break on us. It turns out that if you access the cabinet with the latch often it causes stress while being bent back. This stress eventually causes the white/clear part to weaken (like bending a paperclip repeatedly) and then it snaps. This only happened on the most frequently accessed cabinets and all the others seem to be fine. However, it seems like these should last longer than a couple/few months if attached to a spot that needs to be opened frequently, like the cabinet below the sink where we get trash bags, dishwasher stuff, and dish soap. I appreciate that the company was so accommodating and provided us extra locks upon one breaking, but I would prefer them to last a longer time.

Update 7/30/2016
This morning my daughter came to me with one of the safety locks that had randomly broken. It hasn't been treated differently than any of the other 11 safety locks we are using, so I was surprised to see this one. It is a clean break as shown in the picture. Now I need to get it replaced because this one kept the toddler out of the art materials so he doesn't show off his drawing skills on the walls and floors. However, I don't need 6 of them.

These have been infinitely better than the latches that go on the back of the cabinets to keep them from being accessed by toddlers. These have done a perfect job at keeping our 2-year-old son out of the cabinets. He discovered quickly he couldn't get into the cabinets and now spends less time in the kitchen. This has been fantastic because now we don't have to stress about him destroying our dishes or getting into dangerous chemicals under the kitchen sink. If installed correctly, they don't even open outward much which has served as a huge deterrent for my son.

These were easy to install. I just watched the video online and was good to go. I also like that they come in different colors to better match the cabinets. I will definitely be buying another set for the bathrooms and other cabinets around the house.

Original review was 4 stars.. reduced to 3 after a month of using. See below for update.

First lets get the price out of the way: At first I was a little wary of spending this much on a highchair, but I am so glad we did. You are not purchasing just a highchair here. This is a multistage seat that will have a place in your home well after your child is done needing a high chair. This more than justifies the price.

This chair looks great and actually doesn't take up as much space as it looks like it might from the pictures. It was very easy to set up (it took about 30 minutes for me to do it alone with my baby climbing all over it) and is easy to adjust with the included allen wrench. This is especially convenient for the foot rest as it means you can adjust it to the proper height while your child is in the highchair.
The chair itself wipes down easily - I haven't had any issues with food getting into the bolt holes, but I have only been using it for a few weeks. I haven't yet tested the cushion in the washing machine, but that is because so far a baby wipe has been enough to spot remove any stray food.
The only issue I have with this chair, and why I removed one star, is that it is somewhat cumbersome to move around.. especially if you need to move it while your child is in it. I knew it didn't have wheels before purchasing, and they would definitely hinder the design, but they would have been useful for mobility.

Even without the wheels, I would make the same decision again.

On a side note - I did a lot of research deciding between this chair and the Stokke Tripp Trapp. I have not tried the Stokke chair, so please don't take any of what I say to be absolute, but it might help you to know what points sold me on the Svan:

1. The price. The Svan chair comes with everything you need for all stages (except for the cushion) for $250; The Stokke has a base price of the same, but then you need to add the baby kit ($70) and even the tray ($50) separately (and also select a cushion).

2. Stability. I had read some reviews of the Stokke being easy to tip over. Again, I do not have the Stokke so I cannot testify to this, but I can confirm that the Svan is extremely sturdy and I don't see any possibility of it tipping over despite doubling as a jungle gym!

3. Adjustments. The Stokke requires dismantling to transition the chair between stages; the Svan adjusts with the turn of an allen wrench.

Overall, we love this chair and would highly recommend it to anyone.

UPDATE (edited from 4 stars to 3 stars): When we first started using this highchair, we did not bother installing the harness because our daughter barely squirmed around while eating. However, fast forward a few weeks and she twists, turns, stands, anything except sitting still! So I installed the harness. The current version of this chair has a 5 point harness (it was previously a 3 point harness) and this is the most useless harness in the history of harnesses. I do love the release button that pops the straps out when you push it so there is less fiddling, but there is no point in even putting the harness on. At most it works as a 3 point harness that holds her down so she can't stand up. As for the shoulder straps, they have nothing to hold them up and are set too far apart so they just slide down my daughter's arms and become chewing toys resulting in a food caked mess on the straps. I emailed customer support who said they were aware of the problem and suggested I put a safety pin in the back to hold the straps closer together on her shoulder blades. While this somewhat resolves the issue, I should not have to perform modifications on a brand new product. While the harness does not prevent squirming, it does do it's job of providing safety and the child cannot escape from the chair... it is effectively a 3 point harness and I will likely just cut the shoulder straps off.

I should note that 3 stars doesn't seem very high, but I would still recommend this highchair, especially if style and longevity is important to you. Every chair I have used in the past has had flaws so you just need to know them in advance and decide which ones you can live with. For me, the lack of wheels and the harness issue are issues I can live with over, say, stability or safety issues that I have encountered with others.

We received this as a gift from a friend and I was thrilled because I'd looked at it, but based on the mixed reviews hesitated to purchase it. I can't fully say if I will buy one again until next year, because I'm not really sure how the ornaments we created will hold up. Here's what we've got so far:

Pros:
Relatively easy to use in comparison to mixing up plaster. Dough is kneaded and rolled out.
Comes with everything you need.
Sweet idea that has potential to make a great keepsake (or become an annual tradition).
Plenty of dough...you could get multiple kids done with one pack. We did our baby and our dog. =)

Cons:
Dough is very strange stuff. Spongy, a bit sticky and never seems to really harden. Not sure how it will hold up over time and I'm a little afraid packing it away will destroy it or make new impressions we don't want.
Frankly, getting a hand or footprint of a newborn is just not that easy to do. =) Don't expect to get a "perfect" print unless you have a really still child or hours to kill trying over and over again.

Since the dough is still somewhat soft the jury is still out on how this will hold up, but we're pleased with the two ornaments we made right now. A few tips for parents...

1.) Be prepared to have to try this multiple times. Don't try to pull it off in 5 minutes or when your child is crabby/hungry/overtired.
2.) I found the easiest way to do it was instead of rolling it out on a book or flat surface I rolled it onto my hand and then pressed my daughter's hand to mine, sort of like doing paddy-cake. It means our ornaments aren't a perfect circle (I trimmed it afterwards) but it made for the best impressions we tried.
3.) Your child will most likely come away with a little dough under his/her nails or between fingers at least once. Have a wipe or towel ready before the dough makes it to his/her mouth. Not really sure what this stuff is.

First off, let me start by saying that I didn't see the need to buy the most expensive car seat out there and was looking for the best deal. This led me down the path of multiple purchases and disappointment, until I ultimately found the right car seat. I have therefore seen and handled these three car seats in person and can hopefully shed some light on questions I had that I was unable to answer solely with the descriptions. The Snugride 30 and 35 are effectively the same car seat, with a few minor differences. The Snugride 35 LX is a completely different, and much nicer, car seat.

Head support - the Snugride 30 and 35 have the same infant head/body support - a very lightly padded insert that provides barely any head support. I have a long and curvy drive, and given newborns cannot support their own head, this left me searching for more support as I didn't want to resort to using rolled towels along their body and head. The Snugride 35 LX has lots of support with the built in head cushion and the removable infant body support. I've seen some reviews complain of their infant not being able to move their head with the Snugride 35 LX but this is the whole point of the head support. It's there to support the head in the event of a crash.

Harness - some Snugride 30's come with a harness that can only be tightened/loosened from the BACK of the car seat. If there is not a crotch strap hanging down in the photo then this is the case. Otherwise, it's a front-adjust Snugride 30 and it's got the same harness system as the Snugride 35. As an FYI, the Snugride 30 LX includes the front harness strap as well so you don't have to tighten and loosen the harness from the back of the seat. You slip your finger into the slot in the fabric to loosen the straps and then tighten them by pulling on the crotch strap. To adjust the height of the harness straps, you have to rethread them through the back of the car seat. The Snugride 35 LX has a nice button you push to loosen the straps and you simply adjust the harness height by squeezing and lowering or lifting the lever on the back of the car seat. It's so easy and so worth the extra $20 difference right there. The crotch/hip straps have to be rethreaded in all three cases but these won't be adjusted as frequently as the harness straps.

Latch - if you will be using the latch system, which seems much more secure in my opinion but is said to be equally as safe as the seat belt option, the Snugride 30 and 35 come with the standard latch hooks. These are very difficult to get on and off but do loosen up a bit over time and get easier as you learn how to twist them to get them on and off. The Snugride 35 LX comes with the In Right Latch, which you just push over the latch hook and it clicks on and then releases with the push of a button. Amazing!! This is another feature that I would gladly pay the $20 price difference for. I will say the Snugride 35 LX I ordered from Amazon did not have the In Right Latch but rather had the standard latch hooks. It was also an early 2016 model so I am not sure if that was the issue. The model number on Graco's website described it as having the In Right Latch so I am not sure what the issue was. I contacted Graco and they were very gracious and willing to send me the correct base to rectify the situation, which was a testament to their customer service.

Base - the Snugride 30's base is not adjustable in terms of height. If you need to recline it more, which you likely will for a newborn, you need to put rolled towels under the base. This did not seem very safe to me although is stated you can do so in the Graco manual. Also the level indicator is just a straight line on the base that you need to ensure is level with the ground. The base on the Snugride 35 and 35 LX is adjustable and I've found I use the highest position for newborn. Also, the bubble level indicators are much easier to use and take out any guess work in determining whether the seat is properly reclined. Side note, the main difference between the Snugride 30 and 30 LX, is the 30 LX includes the same adjustable base with bubble level indicator as the Snugride 35.

Seatbelt lock off - the Snugride 35 LX has an integrated lock off for seat belts which is another way to ensure the installation is nice and secure when using a seat belt. The Snugride 30 and 35 do not have a lock off.

Weight/height - the Snugride 30's allow you to use them until your child is up to 30 lbs and 30" and the Snugride 35's allow you to use them until your child is up to 35 lbs and 32". So you get a little more use out of the 35's which helps compensate for any added cost.

Overall - the Snugride 35 LX has feels more nicely appointed and the seat cushion feels thicker and more securely attached to the car seat. Also, the canopy on the Snugride 35 LX moves much more smoothly and interferes less with the handle than with the Snugride 30 and 35. For the small increase in price to get the Snugride 35 LX, it is money well spent!!

Whoever came up with this car kit had to have some experience with kids! Every component is easy-to-use and extremely helpful in protecting both your child and your vehicle.

First, the seat-cover is really soft and absorbent. It not only fits over the buckle of an infant or preschooler's car seat, but also works in a stroller, as well. The rubberized bottom keeps moisture from leaky diapers, sweat and spills away from the upholstery of the seat, and prevents the pad from slipping, as well. The turquoise colored gasket slips around most buckles and straps, but keeps moisture from accessing them, too. It is way easier to remove and wash this seat cover than to try and clean an infant or child's car seat or stroller padding.

Second, the window clings are amazing! When not in use, they twist and roll into about 1/4 their size. The plastic side sticks tight to the glass of any side window. The mesh fabric blocks the sun, but allows you to see out. There is a strong plastic smell when you first open the packaging. However, it either dissipated quickly, or I didn't notice it after a while. The white HOT alert feature on the window screen was pretty much useless, because it is too sensitive. The back of it is black, so it absorbs the heat of the sun. We were in a cool, crisp, air-conditioned vehicle, and it kept registering that it was dangerously hot.

Finally, the kick mat is a great idea. This seat cover has a fabric front and a rubber/plastic backing to keep a kiddo's wet or muddy shoes from dirtying the back of the seat in front of him/her. I found that it fits around a car seat with an adjustable headrest, but was hard to fit on a seat which has a one-piece back. The elastic at the bottom also has to stretch awfully far to get around the lower edge of a seat. Buckles on the straps allow you to attach and remove the cover fairly easily. It is machine washable on the gentle cycle, but you should NOT tumble dry the cover, or you will quickly degrade the vinyl backing and wear out the elastic straps.

Each of these components is a MUST for anyone who has youngsters in their vehicle. I would advise that parents, grandparents, caregivers, carpoolers, etc. make sure you have a set of the seat covers and kick mats for each child. For long drives in the summer, adults benefit, as well, with having the window clings to stick to the side of the car that faces the sun. This would also make a thoughtful gift for a baby shower or adoption celebration.

I've got several potty options in my house that we use regularly and I will say this is my toddler's favorite, probably because she can most easily get up and go on her own with this and she likes to be independent. That said, here are my opinions and observations...

The pros:
•The seat is just soft enough to be comfortable.
•It does allow my child to get up onto the potty without help, although I still recommend supervision to prevent slips and falls
•It is stable enough that she feels confident sitting on it and doesn't fear falling.
•It folds in half where the seat meets the ladder for putting away.
•the ladder provides a handle for getting on the potty unlike just placing a stool in front of the potty. This means less hands on the toilet seat itself.

The cons:
•This is a pretty cheap plastic and the sides on the stairs flex quite a bit if your kid is squirming around. I will never allow my kid to jump around on it for fear it will snap. She is over 30 pounds and I'm not really concerned it would just break, but if used inappropriately I could see problems arising.
•there is no locking mechanism to the folding of this seat so it can flop open and closed and therefore when they're sitting on the seat the ladder can flip upward making it seem unsteady.
•this is pretty large even folded so storage isn't easy
•having a ladder coming down from your toilet does take up room so if you're in a tight bathroom space or behind a door that swings toward the toilet be cautious that this could get in the way.

Overall I'd probably purchase this over again even with its drawbacks, especially since the kid likes it.

This game is on the one hand quite simple, and on the other quite profound in its concept. Your "equipment" consists of two decks of cards, one green (smaller deck) and one red (larger deck). Gameplay is very easy, but also a ton of fun.

At the start of the game, each player is dealt a hand from the red deck, with each card containing a random word or phrase, usually a noun but not always. During each round, one player (the "judge") takes a card from the green deck, which contains various (and again random) descriptive words and phrases. The other players then choose one of their red cards to best match the judge's green one, but that decision is totally subjective, according to the opinion (whim?) of the judge for that round. Whosever card the judge picks wins that round. The first player to win a certain number of rounds (players can decide in advance) will win the game.

The simplicity of the concept is also its beauty. The randomness of the words and phrases on the cards regularly leads to some rather unusual, even riotously funny, associations. And of course, the players often feel the need to embellish or to explain their occasionally absurd choices -- somehow there's a twisted logic behind every one. Doesn't matter though, because the judge is free to disregard every shred of logic and choose whatever goofy association he or she wants.

The long and short of it is, this game is good clean fun, and suitable for all ages from about teenage and older. Although there is a finite number of cards in the box, there is pretty good replay potential since everything stays random and it's statistically unlikely in the extreme that any two rounds will be the same. But expansion packs are available anyway. At $30 for the regular box set, the price is a tad steep for just a couple decks of cards (the "wood crate" set is about $35), but it's a worthy investment anyway. Try it, and I'm sure you'll like it.

Overall, this is a pretty good back support system. The build quality is mostly good -- the fabric covering is soft and feels very nice, the filling is very evenly distributed and does not shift in use, and the zippers that hold the pieces together are nicely done. The one area that could be better is the zippers that hold the covering on the pillows. They are pretty thin and somewhat fussy to zip open or closed. It's not a major con since those only need to be used when taking off the covering.

I like how easy this is to configure. Each of the two support tubes can be easily removed and re-attached, so you can configure this for just front support, for just back support or both. There is a Velcro strap that anchors the two support tubes when both are used. It is easy to attach and adjust.

My main complaint is that the tube diameter for the front support is too narrow. I don't get as good hip support as I do with another similar pillow. It's not horrible, but I don't sleep as well with this as I do with my larger diameter support. This would be perfect if the front support tube was about 2 inches larger in diameter or if the filling was more dense and didn't compact as much in use. As such, I use this for just back support and use my other pillow for front/hip support.

Still, for the price, it's a good value given all the options and the build quality. These are very handy to have not only if you're pregnant, but are also excellent if you have a bad back or have joint pain due to arthritis. It makes sleeping far more comfortable and restful.

Once I lowered our daughter's crib, this protector went in. I didn't want to mess with fixing a loose protector when her mattress was harder to reach, and she wasn't really moving around that much--requiring a fixed protector--until she got older, anyway.

So far, all is well. The protector fits our mattress wonderfully. The times she had a leak, nothing made it past the protector. Sorry for the gross-factor, but I'm waiting to see how this thing handles a complete fecal blowout, or vomit.

Why only four stars? I just don't know how well this thing will handle total saturation. I know her older plastic-backed ones will do it, and lasted from her older brother. I'm guessing that the folks looking at this item don't want that, though. After years of guiding in Alaska, I'm really picky about anything touted as "waterproof", and a non-membrane cloth layer doesn't strike me as being up to the task. That's it: Simple bias.

That said, I'll follow up if anything makes me swing fully one way, or the other.

A heads-up for first-time parents: Though this fits our mattress, make sure you actually MEASURE your mattress before you buy any full-coverage protector. You'd be surprised how many measure all over the scale, though their tag says otherwise (I saw this when initially shopping for a mattress).
