This is a pretty good video camera to monitor your infants movements and activities, but be aware that the audio capability of this unit fails on a semi-regular basis. After 3-4 months of fantastic use, we noticed the sound was not working. We initially suspected that it was the result of needing to re-pair the camera with the monitor unit, but that did not resolve the audio issue.

The video quality is outstanding. I am always able to see clearly even in my baby's completely dark room. The only weird thing is that you baby's eyes will look a little creepy when they are open (think Children of the Corn or The Stand).

The startup sound is annoying, but you can cover the speaker holes on the back of the monitor when you start it up to muffle it pretty well and it's not really a big deal in the grand scheme of things.

The battery life is reasonable. I think that over a year of use, it lost 15-20% of its battery life, but I am still able to get almost 3 hours of use before it requires charging.

The range is great. We've been upwards of 45 feet away from the camera and still had signal. The only times we have ever experienced an "out of range" error was when we needed to re-pair the units again.

The camera itself is VERY quiet when panning and tilting so it is highly unlikely to awake or affect your baby's sleep or activity. I think this is important because if you baby moves out of view or is only partially visible, you do not want to wake them in order to see them.

I am reviewing a Safety 1st OutSmart Flex Lock Decoy that I received at no cost through the Amazon Vine program.

We have a 13-month-old who loves to get into our cabinets and drawers. Some are okay, some are definitely not. And she's clever and strong so the lock needs to resistent.

This one just about does it. The key to opening it is pressing on the top and bottom from the left while pulling open with the right. This does mean it requires two hands (or one hand with a LOT of shaking) to open, which makes it tough to open when holding said 13-month-old. The buttons are not only hidden but also very tight so it does require some hand strength to do it.

I should mention it only works on side-by-side cabinets whose handles are reasonably close together. This is not something to buy if you need a drawer or single cabinet (without a paired cabinet whose handle is next to it) locked.

It also only comes one to a package, which is pricey but it works fine. While I've not had this lock long enough to say, I do have some concern about Safety 1st in terms of its durability. Some of our previous Safety 1st locks have been broken by our kids when they pull the cabinets hard enough. One type of lock simply wore out in the tab portion fo the locking mechanism and so it just falls open at slight pressure - that's not this Flex Lock but it was a previously made kind of flex lock. I have however made my recommendation on the basis of this lock's own performance.

It is funny to watch her press the decoy button repeatedly though, and then give up and go to one of the other locks that she's already broken.

Okay so we did a ton of research and then ended up purchasing both this model and the chicco nextfit. When they arrived we installed both car seats at the same time and compared them. First of all, the Britax was incredibly simple to install, I mean like watch a two minute video and go for it easy. Chicco was not as simple and took several times longer. Honestly the two seats are so much alike though that what made the decision for us was how little the Britax moved when we tried to shake it from side to side.  It did not budge. Didn't matter if we tried to get it to move at the head of the seat or at the foot of the seat, it did not move an inch. The chicco, even though it was installed properly, move several inches when shaken from the head of the seat, it didn't move at all when shaken near the foot of the seat of course. That was it for us. The fact that the Britax was solid and super secure after a quick 2 minute install was enough for us. Yes, yes, yes, the crotch buckle is WAYYYY to short. WAAYYY TO SHORT no doubt. It was at least a full inch shorter than the nextfit crotch buckle. My daughter is 5th percentile for weight and 25th for height. She is 16 months old and very petite and the belt does dig into her leg and leave a small pink line like pictures other reviewers have left. We're going to buy some thin seat belt pads and see if they alleviate this issue, but for now she does not seem bothered by it all. What's important is that she's safe in the event of an accident. We have a 2006 Honda Civic ex sedan and the Britax fits beautifully. I don't think it takes up any more room than the chicco keyfit 30 infant car seat we used previously.

I decided on another video baby monitor as I am expecting a third child. I used to own a summer infant video monitor that I bought from babies r us but it broke down after my 3 year old decided to throw the monitor into the sink. I was not prepared to pay another 200 dollars so I shopped online for alternatives. I got this on amazon (because of the price) and this product is great. I was prepared to return it if it was crap, (which cheap products are usually online...)
Pros: The VOX setting activates only when it registers loud noises (like cries) and it doesn't inadvertently turn on due to loud traffic noises (unlike my old baby monitor).
price, the price is unbelievable for a monitor with video, and static-free
video and audio quality - I can not complain. It is far better than my old monitor.
interference - it works fine with our wifi and 2.4ghz cell phone
presentation - comes in nice gift box and cute design
range - I can leave the camera in the nursery and be in the kitchen (around 300 feet away) and I still get reception
no background noise - the monitor cuts the background noise when there is no sound and becomes totally quiet. My old unit always had this constant clicking sound even when it was dead quiet.

Cons: the material falls below what I wanted, but for the price it makes up for everything. It's uses a light weight plastic material which is good and bad because it is nearly weightless when you strap this on your waist when you are moving around in the house.
features - I wished for a pan and tilt camera but this doesn't have it.

Verdict; if you are looking for something that works well and doesn't give you any problems, this is it. if you are looking for a high-tech baby monitor, this isn't what you are looking for. This is like a Honda - always works, does what it is designed to do very well, great specs and features, good price but lacks the solid feel, and the extra niff-naff 'nice to have' features that a mercedes-benz has.
4 star for the product itself compared to other video monitors in the market
5 star for what you get for the money.

These are really soft and adorable! Muslin blankets are very useful to have around. I got these for my third child and still have uses for the original set I received for my first kid. Of course, they are nice blankets because they are very thin and won't over-heat your child. You can use them for nursing covers, car seat covers, stroller covers, any type of cover you can imagine. You can swaddle with them, help breastfeed with them, add padding to the car seat if your baby is just a bit too small for it as a newborn. They also make great toys at the doctor's office when your child needs a distraction. We play "parachute" with these. You raise it up over you child's head and then let if fall gently on top of them. Our nurses love this, they can get the vaccines done while it is in the air and then when it touches my kids heads they were all distracted and didn't cry much at all. (my second never cried at all)

Because these are so thin they are easy to pack. I keep at least one with me in the diaper bag at all times. I have another one in the car, and pack them whenever we are going on trips. They weigh like nothing, so you won't even notice you have them with you. They wash like a dream, no shrinking and stand up better to washing and drying than thicker blankets. I even run these through the sanitize setting on my dryer and they come out fine.

The designs still look nice, just like they were brand new. I have run these through more washes now than I honestly kept track of. They seem to get softer with more use over time. I wish these were a tiny bit larger. When you fold them in half they are a little too small to swaddle, so you need to do it full size. I like being able to double the fabric when it is cold out or the baby is seriously fussy. Other than that, these are wonderful and I highly recommend them.

As a new mom, I was excited for the Bugaboo Bee! From newborn until 2 years old, the 1st generation Bee was indispensable. It went to Asia, on a cruise- Panama & Alaska, Orlando, Spain, all over NYC and more! I saw that the 2nd generation Bee was wider, and chose the ALL BLACK, and it's held up pretty amazing well.

The only reason I deducted a star, is that the height of the seat slides down, and if I don't notice it, my tall 3 year old hunches, that's definitely a disappointment.

The pros:

LIGHTER WEIGHT
FORWARD & REAR FACING
WIDTH!!! IT GOES BETWEEN SEATS IN A TIGHT CAFE / RESTAURANT | SMALL BOUTIQUE, ETC. BEST OF BOTH WORLDS OF UMBRELLA & FULL FEATURE STROLLER
HANDLE LOCKS IN PLACE (although sometimes you have to wiggle it)
ADJUSTABLE RECLINE
GREAT BASKET SPACE!
NOT TIPPY, WHEN YOU HANG ITEMS (original version adjustable handle got lose and would shrink down-they don't recommend hanging anything off the handles!)
ADJUSTABLE HANDLES FOR TALL/SHORT PARENTS / ADULTS or ADJUSTING WHEN CHILD IS COMPLETELY RECLINED
COMES WITH RAIN HOOD
EASY TO LOCK WHEELS

The cons:
OLDER CHILDREN, YOU WILL NEED TO WATCH THE SEAT HEIGHT AND RE-ADJUST ACCORDINGLY
MORE ASSEMBLY THEN ORIGINAL BUGABOO BEE (I REMEMBER ONLY ATTACHING WHEELS)
STRAPS ARE TIGHT SO RE-ADJUSTMENT ISN'T SIMPLE (I HAD TO REALLY FORCE IT-NEW AND TIGHT)
NEED TO PAY ATTENTION TO LEFT AND RIGHT MARKER TO MAKE SURE IT OPENED CORRECTLY
TO COMPACT THE STROLLER / NOT AS SMOOTH AS ORIGINAL / I HAVE OCCASIONALLY REMEMBER TO KICK THE BACK BAR OR REMEMBER TO RETURN THE SEAT TO UPRIGHT AND ADJUST THE STROLLER ON THE FLY TO CLOSE DOWN THE STROLLER

EXTRAS-CUP HOLDER
STROLLER HOOD- YOU HAVE TO PURCHASE SEPARATELY
TRANSPORT BAG TO REMAIN UNDER WARRANTY
OPTIONAL BUGGY RIDE-NOT THE BEST FOR BEE

This stroller goes all over, up and down subway stations, onto trains, ferries, boats, airports up to the gate, elevators, folds down on escalators, buses, and more!

You will love being able to walk between some tight places, that the other BUGABOOS can't. You will love the look, and spot another BEE EVERYWHERE YOU GO!

If you want to have 1 stroller ONLY, I recommend the BEE, BUT if your child is bigger-wider, then you might look elsewhere, for the child to be comfortable. Mine is lean but tall, now hitting the 37" mark.

Extremely Happy Strolling!!!

When breast feeding failed, I was so upset! Friends and family recommended the BBFP to help make life just a little easier! I was nervous given the mixed reviews. I initially bought a brezza at target first. Once set up, I tested as others had to ensure proper water/formula ratios dispensed (using the suran wrap trick!). Not only did the orange gears sometimes not spin, but the machine would only spit out 2oz of water and one scoop of formula (an appropriate amount for my formula setting) no matter the size selected (4, 6, 8, 10oz only gave me 2oz). So there must have been some computer error. Returned the machine and got another on amazon. So far so good!! Checked the ratios and they are correct! Given that there is room for error with the machine, I recommend checking each setting for proper formula/water ratio prior to use. Any errors can obviously be detrimental to your child! But if working as described and you take care of it, this machine is great! Having a baby is hard and anything that can make the process a little easier is worth it in my mind! 4/5 stars because of the first being faulty, but certainly can happen with any similar product!

If you have a child that moves around the bed a lot, I can imagine these might not work.  However, as my little ones' torsos typically stay in the roughly the same place, with only arms/legs/head moving around, these worked well.  That said........both of my kids have mentioned the sheets are somewhat rough.  After multiple washings they have become quite pilly/nubby and are fairly uncomfortable against skin.  It's a shame they didn't remain soft and smooth for very long, as they would have otherwise been perfect.

I bought this to help keep our cats safe since the railings on our balcony are kind of wide. Overall it does the job well so far. Seems sturdy and that it will likely weather well. What I didn't like in this case was that it was challenging to connect it to our decking with the provided hardware. You get zip ties and large silver metal hooks with screw ends. As you can tell in my photo, the railing has a large gap between it and the decking. Providing a very large area for a cat to squeeze themselves through. The phrase "curiosity killed the cat" is a phrase for a reason. Lol Thus it was important to make sure that I closed that gap if possible.

I didn't realize that there wasn't a way to attach it to decking other than with the provided hooks when purchasing, so my mistake. But it did bum me out. I didn't want to completely damage my decking by screwing in a massive hook but also didn't want to leave it open to tempt the cats. Luckily I had some small cable clips (tiny nail with a plastic hook attached) that secured the net to the decking. I wouldn't trust it holding anything back on it's own with just the cable clips. But combined with the zip ties, I think they will work enough to prevent an accident.

I needed something for my 6 month old that wouldn't take up too much space in my 450sq ft Brooklyn apartment, so this seemed the way to go.  That said, my door frame must be too low and my boy wasn't getting the leverage he needed to get the most out of his bounce.  THANKFULLY, we figured out a way to shorten the swing, allowing for further modification on the length strap.  Loosen the three straps on each of the prongs, run the clamp UNDER EACH, then tighten.  This super QUICK and safe fix lets you then further adjust the length, but is pretty much the exact fix you'd need, without having to resort to stuffing objects under the straps.  Graco, we love the bouncer, but there's gotta be a better way to shorten it!  Not everyone has 10 foot door frames!  Other than that, my big-little guy spends a lot of time in this bouncer (by "a lot", I'm talking baby terms - 1/2 hour most, and as you parents know: EVERY MINUTE COUNTS!!), loves the toy attachments, and overall just seems to love "hanging out".  One star off for having to spend half an hour scratching our heads over how to make it shorter.

You need these if you own an Instant Pot and enjoy eggs. I am sure they can be used with other pressure cookers but I have only the Instant Pot IPDuo60.

I've been obsessed with poached eggs for a couple years. I enjoy eating them but making them was a pain. I was making poached eggs frequently, but had quite a few fails. I can scramble the fails and my dog won't hate me when I add them to her dish. This would leave me without eggs too often.

Things were really looking up when I recently purchased my Instant Pot. Suddenly, I was able to eat poached eggs with fewer fails. My obsession wouldn't let me stop there, I had to have a perfect poached egg every time and knew the glass ramekins I used were not the best tool. I considered one of those dedicated egg poaching machines. I couldn't convince myself that wouldn't be overkill.

I decided to give these a try because the price was right and I liked the colors. I would prefer a set of pink ones, because pink is my favorite color, but these colors are bright, not pastel, so they are nice.

Put butter in one of these poachers, put in microwave to soften the butter. Then pour some of the butter out and into the other ramekins. Drop one egg into each cup. Season as you wish - I use pepper and smoked paprika. Place trivet that was included with the instant pot into the inner pot. Add water to the inner pot, but level should not cover the trivet. (About 1 to 1 1/2 cups.) Place ramekins on the rack in the inner pot. Place lid on Instant Pot correctly. Turn valve to allow for pressure. Use the Steam mode for 1 minute. Immediately release pressure. Cups are not too hot to handle to lift enough to get a serving spoon under the cup to remove. Then tilt over your dish to allow the egg to slide out. This may seem like a lot of steps, but it is easy and fast in practice.

I was thrilled to use my Instant Pot to make pineapple upside down cake, but making poached eggs is something I will repeat much more often, so I think these poachers are a must have. They can be used in the microwave and are easy to clean. I washed them all by hand. The eggs were contained in the poachers, so there were no egg pieces in the water like there are when poaching on the stove.

Only negative was that these poacher cups tend to wobble, so they were not easy to balance on the trivet. I think the base is slightly too narrow. It's possible these can go directly in the water, instead of using the trivet, but I did not try this. Too chicken? You bet - I didn't want my eggs to be drowned, or overflow into the water.

I bought a silicone steamer basket that I will try using to replace the stainless steel trivet. I think this will make the cups more sturdy. If these were more sturdy on flat surfaces and wet trivets, I'd definitely give this product 5 stars. Placing these cups on a paper towel or napkin, before filling with egg, makes these less wobbly on flat surface. Wrapping the trivet in aluminum foil might be just the adjustment needed to make the cups sit more stable in the Instant Pot. I love getting my hands on all the silicone tools I can, so my money was not wasted and I would recommend these to anyone that wants to make poached eggs in their electric pressure cooker. Once the eggs are in the Instant Pot, I can tend to the rest of the meal, which is exactly what I need. I no longer have a need to poach eggs on the stove, which will keep my kitchen cooler in hot weather. But I'm sure I will try these poachers in a stovetop pot, just to see them float. I think one set of poachers will not be enough.

We purchased the entire Travel System and it works as advertised. The front wheel problems reported in earlier posts have been resolved with newer models.

Things we like:
- This system fits a wide range of children. Our son was 6 weeks early and fit into the carrier @ 5lbs. This was due to the three shoulder strap positions (versus two available positions found in other models).
- The stroller rolls easily over a variety of terrain. We have taken the stroller on gravel trails without any problems. We have also been able to roll across a loose sandy beach if we were careful.
- There is a safety strap to tether the stroller to your wrist. This makes going down hills safer.
- The stroller has been durable so far. We have taken it on multiple airplane trips and outdoor walks. So far the tires have shown little wear and no damage occurred with the baggage handlers.
- The triangle grip allows us to hold the carrier in multiple positions comfortably.
- This thing is a tank and will carry a lot of bags, coats, and toys.

Things needing improvement:
- If you are going to do serious jogging, you'll want something with a larger front wheel and some form of suspension. The front wheel of the Expedition doesn't roll up over every bump in the road. However, the Expedition is great for a fast walk around the neighborhood or local trail.
- The front wheel's valve stem can only be accessed with the included pump which is not that great. If you have a good bicycle pump then get a "Topeak Pressure-Rite Anti-Air Loss Connector" from Amazon. This adapter allows you to pump up the tires quickly and easily with a full sized pump. [[ASIN:B000FIAVKG Topeak Pressure-Rite Anti-Air Loss Connector]]
- The little flap in the cover does not have velcro to hold it open (window to see the child when the cover is closed). We glued on a piece of velcro to solve the problem.
- The stroller base is heavy (as are all travel system bases). Baby trends makes an excellent lightweight base for smooth surfaces. My wife used this base exclusively for the first month as she recovered from child birth (not fun lifting heavy objects!). [[ASIN:B002U44XOI Baby Trend Snap N Go-Single Stroller]]

I got this for my 6 year old on a mom-and-son road trip. I gifted this to my son only on our trip back home (had it sent to my sister's place where we were visiting) not really expecting much of this contraption. At first glance I do agree the fabric and general quality needs much improvement. The zip especially was really difficult the first few times I was showing my son how to close it shut himself. All that said however, I still would give this 4 stars as it really did what I was hoping it would: which is provide additional space for some carefully chosen items I felt would entertain and comfort my son. He gets nervous easily and this worked out really well, allowing him to access some maps I'd printed, his markers to check off stuff in our scavenger hunt game, tic tacs as a treat when we hit a milestone (50% there, 1 hour left, etc) along the way, and a couple of knick knacks he wanted to have around. The "tabletop" area was surprisingly sturdy, allowing him to use it for many hours. He felt real special. Other than the zip which I've already mentioned gave us some problems when he wanted to hide the items away, the whole configuration worked really well. I totally expected to give this product a low review, but for the first time in a long time I suppose I've stumbled onto a product that undersold and overperformed. I hope this product gets a redesign to work out the flaws. If so, it'd be a handy must-have for many.

These Door Monkeys are the kind of product you don't realize how much you need them until you no longer have them. One tip: If yours broke in the same way a couple of ours have, where the spring which helps it grip the door no longer works, there's an easy, cheap fix: Search on Home Depot "3m 3/4 in. x 22 ft. Temflex Rubber Splicing Tape", (they sell it in-store as well), cut off a piece, give it a stretch and simply wrap one of the ends until it fits your door snuggly to extend the life of your Door Monkey (see pictures). The concept of Mag Lock is to hide the lock itself so that no one even knows there's a hidden mag lock. Well, sure, you can say this is a visible "keyless" lock using a magnet to open/unlock. But that's still not the pinnacle of what mag locks are supposed to do.

This product requires you to use 3M double-sided tape to secure the locking device into the drawer/cabinet/etc. Then the magnet is placed on the device itself and the door/drawer/cabinet is unlocked. A few problems were noticed:

1. The thickness of the drawer/cabinet/door makes a big difference. Too thick = non-functional mag mechanism. I further suspect it has to do with material + thickness. But the take away message here is: thickness matters. material matters. Obviously don't try this on a metal cabinet. It will mess with the magnets.

2. The sturdiness of the product over time. The installation was easy and required no tool: 3M double-sided tape only. That is in itself a curse and a blessing. Sure it was easy to install, but after about a month some of the locks have started to fail (fall off the surface). This was not surprising as this was an expected outcome of double-sided tape. Eventually they will all fail - it's just a matter of time.

3. Maybe if you are handy enough you can try drilling and screwing in a small screw to help support the locking mechanism onto the surface of the wood. This is a big maybe.

4. Price point - actually not bad for the number of glue-on locks provided for the price. It offers about 3-6 months worth of use, in my opinion, without much issue. But longer than that, well, durability (again, double-sided tape) is going to be your biggest challenge.

All things considered, this is an OK set of mag locks that worked pretty well under the right circumstances. I totally believe it is going to be a hit or miss depending on again 1) material 2) thickness 3) durability.

If you want completely invisible mag lock device there are those around but not this set. This is not invisible. It actually calls the question "heyyy what's that over there?? what's the thing on your drawer??" Then you have to answer it's a mag-lock.

So, please decide which application (purpose) this is for--it may work out great for you but not if you are looking for a more permanent solution and/or an invisible solution.

Good luck! Hope this has been helpful to you!

My husband and I practice attachment parenting. We were cosleeping for the first 6 months of our child's life. During that time we we're sleeping horribly. My son was waking every 45 minutes to an hour every night. I felt exhausted and our son looked tired all the time. I received this sleep machine from a friend, but never thought of using it. We tried the no cry method for several weeks and it wasn't working for us. We finally decided to give this sleep trainer a try. I decided that at 6 months my son could likely go with only one feeding in the middle of the night.  Before I was breastfeeding him every time he woke,  so he came to expect a feeding in order to fall back asleep. The first night we used this device our son cried for about 17 min, with us checking in on him every 1,3,5 and 7 minutes. We didn't pick him up, but instead offered comforting words and touch. He fell asleep soon after and only had a few wakings throughout the night with less than 1 minute of crying. I fed him around 2am.  The second night he fell asleep within the first minute we laid him down. Since then the amount he cries lessens and lessens. Last night (3days into the training) he fell asleep without crying. I think parents have to be ready for this to work and their child needs to be age appropriate. 4 months does seem young to start sleep training. At 6 months our son seemed more than ready! The key to this working is to have a calm 1 hour nighttime routine that takes place an hour before bed, one that your child can predict. We all feel more rested!

I took away a star because I have had a number of issues with losing reception that just shouldn't be happening. I mean, my home is under 1100 sqft, and the handset has to be set up perfectly just to receive the image if the camera is set up in my daughter's room and I am in my own room. Not to mention that it renders the ability to talk to my daughter through it completely useless, as I can get maybe a word in before it cuts out from my room- which is where it usually is. It can be very frustrating, but we make it work. ***Note, if it does lose reception, it beeps very loudly (not obnoxious intervals though, just enough to wake you)- so no worry that it'll randomly lose reception in the middle of the night and then you won't hear your baby wake up. That's very comforting for me :)
Also, the music feature is a mixed bag... It works great, and I have resorted to using it on MANY occasions because it doesn't shut off on a preset timer, and my daughter loves it! But, because the music comes out of so close to where the microphone is, it makes the monitor stay on, and *SERIOUSLY* amplifies and even somewhat distorts it on my end... so my daughter falling asleep to it means me also having it blasting in my room. Not what my husband and I want to sleep to! And even more importantly, because it IS so loud through the monitor, I can't hear my daughter over the music if she does wake up! Now that she's a toddler and sleeping through the night, it's less of an issue- but as an infant that made the music completely unusable.
I would buy this product again because this is truly the best thing you can get for the money. I have friends with $400+ monitors that blow this one away (larger screens, moving cameras, better music function & reception, etc), but if you're on a budget and still want a lot of features and some seriously great reliability, this is your monitor 110%!

After having a Chicco Cortina and then a cheapie Jeep Cherokee Sport (that broke), I decided that I was going to get the stroller I'd been eyeing that everyone who goes to Disney says is great - the Citi Mini. But I did NOT want another stroller with the hard plastic wheels. So I looked and the City Mini GT fits the bill. My husband was not sure it would be worth it at the price - until we took it to the zoo and he got to be the one to fold it and push it a bit. Funny thing is - as we were walking around the zoo, a woman pointed us out to her husband saying "that's the stroller I was telling you I wanted!" We plan on taking this with us to Disney and I think it will work great. It was wonderful on the bumpy not always paved sections at the zoo. MUCH better than a stroller with hard plastic wheels would have handled. We also take this stroller on walks around the neighborhood and it's great for that as well. I can now push it over a bump in my driveway without having to stop and tilt the stroller to get it over a 2 inch lip.

But it's not perfect, though I think the Pros far outweigh the cons.

PROS:
*It fits in the back of my Kia hatchback. This is a VERY small space. Even the Jeep Cherokee Sport I had took up more length space than this does when folded. I couldn't get my Chicco stroller in at all.
*It really is easy to fold (I have the child tray attached, that makes it _slightly_ more difficult to fold in that you have to move your hand under the tray when it folds, and remember to store it with the tray on top so the weight is not on the tray, but this is still a pro)
*It's LIGHT-weight
*Comfortable for my son
*Obviously will fit him until he's too old for a stroller
*Easy to push one handed
*Sun shade covers the entire child and can be folded out in sections for more or less coverage
*Love, Love, Love the handbrake

CONS:
*It does not come with a child tray or parent console. Buy the Baby Jogger Child Tray and a store brand parent console (the Dino or other brands would be almost identical)
*The basket is smaller than I'd like and a bit hard to get something wide/tall in from the back. You can pull the sides down, but it's a little annoying. The basket does hold more than you'd think once you start adding things from the sides.
*When in the folded position, the sun shade does brush my son's head. But if it really annoys the child, the shade can be removed fairly easily.

The Maxi-Cosi Gia XP 3-Wheel Stroller is a large well constructed stroller. Everything clicks into place nicely.

It weighs 24 lbs. Folded up it is 32" X 17" X 24". So this is not a small or lightweight stroller. It is large when open, large when folded and heavy. But it is very sturdy.

When you first get the box, you wonder, "how do I unfold it?" There is a gray latch on the side that you have to unsnap. Once you do that it begins to unfold, even if a bit unwieldy.

Assembly is straightforward. The wheels easily click into place. The same goes for the Car Seat adapters. They click nicely into place. When you don't need them, the zippered pocket on the back is large enough to easily hold them. You also get the obligatory Cup Holder which easily clicks into place on the right or left side of the handlebars.

The Stroller has large wheels so it works on all kinds of terrain (within reasonable limits of course). It handles very nicely, is easy to turn and rolls very smoothly. This is the area that this stroller really excels in. It feels very luxurious.

As you'd expect the harness straps are adjustable so you can easily adjust them to your baby/toddler's size. The seat recline is adjusted with a cinch/tab mechanism on the back. It can recline all the way back or adjust to any level you desire…very nice and simple.

The canopy is large and expands from 45 to 135 degrees. But then, you can unzip the top-middle of the canopy, and it will expand further out to almost 180 degrees. Really amazing. It also has a peek-a-boo window at the top so you can keep your eyes on your baby. Unzipping the canopy top also creates 2 more side windows. Think of it as the portholes on the old 1957 Thunderbirds. :-)

The bottom has a very large basket that can hold lots of stuff. You can access it from the back with the large open area, or access it from the front by lifting a tab on the front….all very thoughtfully designed.

The handle has 3 adjustable positions to adjust it to your height and comfort.

The seat pad is removable for cleaning…nice.

The rear brakes are firmly engaged with a tap of the gray tab on the rear wheel axle of the stroller. The front wheel has a swivel lock on it. You'll mainly want to have it unlocked so that the front wheels swivel freely.

All in all this is a top of the line luxury stroller as you'd expect with its $400 price tag. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because it is large and heavy. But if those factors are not important to you, consider this a 5 star stroller.

Before I go, you might want to know how easily it folds back up. At first I was confused about where the release handle was. Looking at the image in the instruction manual, I wondered is this an image of the front or the read of the seat? Where is it? Well, it is on the front through one of the cut out holes. You simply lift the release up and the stroller begins to fold up, just keep it going with the handle folding toward the floor and click the gray tab on the side. Voila! All folded nicely.

I bought a set of these bottles to get me enough bottles to pump for a couple of days without having to re-package milk or do dishes and they work fine for that. The lids are NOT interchangeable with the 2.5 oz freezer tubes (will leak a bit if you shake), so be aware, and you have to tighten them down pretty hard. I also work to always keep the bottles upright after the first time one leaked for an hour in my pump bag.

Also be aware that the ounce marks are not printed on, they are formed into the bottle and not terribly accurate. I end up weighing my bottles to get an accurate amount for freezing, though the other style with the printed on marks are about as bad and the Lasinoh bags are +/- 1/2 oz too.

For what I'm using them for - pumping at work - they work fine, and its nice to have a bunch of them, but don't expect accurate readable lines or to be able to store them sideways!

These cloth diapers are beautiful and very comfortable. My large 11 month old wears size 5 disposable diapers and we ended up returning these cloth diapers because they were almost to the point where they wouldn't fit him anymore, specifically around his thighs. I wish I would have bought them when he was smaller because they are great value. What I would do is use two inserts for overnight, and I would also use the Disposable liners for easy poo removal. The white inserts stained when he pooped, so next time I would get the charcoal ones. Don't use fabric softener or diaper rash creams or Oils with these because it reduces the absorbency. The diapers washed up well in warm water. The shells dried quickly so I hung them. The inserts were hung and dried in the dryer. Everything held up very well doing this. They're bulkier than when using disposable diapers, so that is something to keep in mind when dressing your baby. 18 diapers was enough for us to have time to wash and dry the previous ones before we run out. Just under $200 is what it took for us to get set up with cloth diapering.

I had terrible results with the Gerber ones currently available and started looking for alternatives.  I ordered one package of OsoCozy Indian Cotton prefolds in Newborn size.  When they were laundered they were tiny! Barely long enough to lay over your shoulder.  More research, and I ordered 2 packages of these.  They shrunk to a good size for my projects and the fabric weave is SO much nicer than the gauze ones, plus there is no shifting in the middle layers when they are washed.  I noticed in some of the reviews that there were comments that there was less rippling with these than the Indian cotton variety.  I placed both washed diapers side by side and I can't see any real difference in that. Altogether I am very pleased with these for burp cloths.  When my daughter saw the diapers, her comment was that she might even switch to cloth for diapers, she didn't realize there were any diapers that nice for sale! We've tried several brands of disposable training pants, and these have been the best overall value.

While I hate using disposables on general principle, my son has proved to be much more challenging to both diaper and potty train than my daughter was. While she was cloth diapered and potty trained at 2, he was too heavy a wetter to keep in cloth diapers (and keep my sanity) for much past 1. I'm of the opinion that a cloth diapered baby is much easier to potty train - my daughter pretty much just transitioned right over in about three days. I barely had to do anything, and the cloth training pants I got hardly even got a workout. But as my son has been in disposable diapers for a year, he's proving less eager to transition. And of course every kid is different. So these disposable training pants fill a niche - they're still absorbent enough to hold a decent amount of liquid, and they hold solid messes well, too. But they look and feel like real undies so a child can start to get the hang of the mechanics of going potty, even if he's not quite ready to lose the diapers entirely yet.

The only reason I mark them down a star is the smell. There are certainly diapers that smell much worse, but these still have an unpleasant odor to them that I personally find very objectionable. We are thrilled with our pack-n-play. It is lightweight, easy to set up and take apart, and easy to clean (my toddler spilled yogurt on it...) Our only complaint was that the thin mattress that comes with the pack-n-play did not lay totally flat because of the folds. It wasn't comfortable for our newborn. This was easily remedied, however, with a mattress that fits right inside. We bought a three inch mattress and for our newborn who doesn't roll over yet, it is still safe to place in the bassinet. Once she starts moving about, we plan to lower the mattress to the bottom of the pack-n-play and continue using. One word of advice to parents looking for a pack-n-play: we researched loads of these products and found that the fancy ones with the changers and napping stations and music corners etc were pretty useless. The best we found was the simplest. Just a pack-n-play and a bassinet attachment. She can nap in her bouncer, we don't need an attachment on top of the bassinet that we will have to fight with and remove every night so she can go to sleep in the bassinet. We also prefer the bouncer because it is lots more portable than moving the pack-n-play with bounder attached to whatever room we want her to be in. We didn't need the changing station, especially because reviewers mentioned that it often sags on one side with the baby's weight. We have a regular changing pad that we put on our bed and then move to the side of the room when finished. And the music was not very useful either, according to many reviewers because it was either tinny, too loud or too fake sounding. We have a CD player in the kids room anyway (for my toddler) and put in peaceful Solitudes music for bedtime. Basically, the added frills all seemed pretty useless. We therefore decided not to spend the extra money on extras that we weren't going to use anyway. Just go with what you need - a pack-n-play plus bassinet and skip paying for other bits that are unnecessary.

Even though my title directly address the pump, I'll leave that to the end and focus on the good stuff first.

This really is a very nice sleeping mat. From the comfy blanket to soft top layer to the more-than-adequate cushioning of the enclosed air mattress, there really is a lot of thought that's gone into this. While the initial smell of plastic is somewhat overwhelming, after several days (perhaps a week) of letting it air out, this has become a sleeping pad that I love to take on camping trips for my kids. It's a bit short for my 6 y.o. (his feet stick out a bit) but he nevertheless insists on using it whenever he can. For my 3 y.o., it's perfect. It rolls up easily, inflates quickly (when you skip the pump), and can be washed (by removing the air mattress insert). All told, this really is a great sleeping mat.

The only complaint is the pump. While I think it's a great addition for a child to use, as an adult, I wish they'd just left it off so this rolls up smaller. There are just too many "steps" required to pump the thing up completely. It's kind of exhausting for my 6 y.o., almost impossible for my 3 y.o., and just plain annoying for me. You'll notice that other people have had the same problem and "The Shrunks Team" replies that it's a defect. No, it's just a design flaw. Simply put, the physical volume of the pump is insufficient given the physical volume of the air mattress. Since no "step" is going to be 100% efficient (without risking damage to the pump), the number of pumps required to fill the mattress is far more than suggested. But again, this isn't a defect, just a matter of design. We prefer to just use an electric (or hand) pump, so as to save on excessive mixture getting trapped in the air mattress from blowing it up via mouth.

(PS Just as an aside, the 1-star review that decries the dangers of this sleeping pad really overstates things. First, fleece, unless it comes from an actual sheep, is made from polyester. This is both more economical and more humane. Second, polyester is no more "toxic" than any of the other thousands of materials to which we're exposed. Sure, I wouldn't eat it, but as something to sleep on, it's fine. That whole review is really overblown.)

Update: 12/2016

I used this stroller for awhile, and later switched to another one once my son was too big for this one. It did hold up, though. We mainly used it for going to the zoo, going to the boardwalk, and some other outdoor activities. It wasn't used every day, but I can say that I still have it sitting in my basement ready to sell at some point. It was a good stroller for us.

Original review:

I'll try to tell you what I wanted to know before buying this product. I have also included pictures with notes to help people out.

First, I only have used this stroller today. I can't speak to any durability over any length of time. This is strictly concerning my impressions after a few hours.

Height: I am 5'8" and I did not have to bend to push the stroller. My arms were bent even with my back completely straight. The handles went slightly past my bellybutton and it was like pushing a shopping cart.

Assembly: About five minutes. The only things to put together were the wheels, the cupholder, and the canopy. Everything snapped in, although you will want to watch how you put on the wheels. You can't mistake front for back, but I imagine some could put the wheels on upside down, or at least attempt to. You want to put them on so that pushing down on the red lever activates the brake. The cupholder and canopy are very easy to install as well.

Recline: I put my two-year-old in the seat to try it out and it reclined about as far as I would want it to. I have no plans on using it as a diaper changing station, so a flat surface is not needed. It went down until it rested on the frame, but felt cushioned enough not to be a problem for the child. I can see him easily sleeping in it comfortably.

Storage: There's a smallish pack near the handles with a zippered compartment 3/4 of the space and an open square pocket that takes up the rest of the space. The rack underneath the seat looks like it will hold a bookbag and pocketbook. Our diaper bag may be pushing it, unless we lay it on its side, but it looks like it's enough for anything we're going to need it for.

Color/Use: Anyone who's not a Farscape fan won't get this, but when I first took it out of the box, the color scheme struck me as very "Peacekeeper." In any case, it looks nice with a deep red and dark black. Folding the stroller was pretty easy. You just need to "pop out" one metal latch, fold it in half, and use a plastic latch to hold the wheels to the handles. Opening it up is just as easy. In fact, the totally bare-bones, smaller stroller I have which is basically just a thin fabric seat on wheels is no easier than this one. This one is heavier, though. If the weight means it's durable, that's fine by me, but don't expect to just toss this around like a car seat. It won't break your back, but it's not a feather-weight, if that's important to you. The canopy, which was very important in my decision, seems to be pretty decent. I'll only know when I actually push him around in the sun, but it's way better than nothing and will keep him shaded at high noon for sure. I sunburn easily, and don't want to find out if he does, too, so I may add some protection of my own when the sun is getting low during the day, but I'll have to see if it's needed first. I've also pushed it around my house with him in it and it steers freely. The wheels look like they are good and I'll know when I take him shopping. I don't plan on running through the woods or on the beach with him, so I figure they're good enough.

Bumper bar: I mention this in my pictures, but I will here as well: the bumper bar opens up quite wide to allow you to slide the child into the seat. The harness is nice and quick to latch and is able to be run through higher slots when the child gets taller. My only problem is that it looks like the bottom strap only goes so far, so the actual clasp will not "grow" with him, but will be down lower on his body as he grows. At the worst, I expect the clasp to be on his belly instead of his chest, so it's no real big deal, but I would have preferred having more strap to play with so I could adjust it perfectly.

I was prepared to pay more for a stroller but figured I'd give this one a chance at this price point. If it holds up and lasts me at least a year I'll consider my money well spent.

We have four strollers now... a jogging stroller that weights 30+ lbs, one we got that we could snap the car seat into (and our baby grew out of), a crappy one given to us from the hospital and then this one! I decided to get this one because I'm so tired of struggling to take them in and out of my car and trying to get it set up or put away while dealing with my little fussy boy. It's super lightweight compare to all the other ones I have, but still feel very sturdy and roomy. My son is almost a year old and he can sit in it very comfortably. The back can be adjusted to almost flat, I've even changed his diaper while he's laying in it when we were at the park. Most of the time I could take it out of my trunk and unfold it with one hand (and my foot). It is also easy to maneuver when we go to places that have tight walk way. The storage space below is pretty spacious and easy to get to (althou I have not tried getting to it while he's laying in it). We plan to take this with us when we travel to Taiwan at the end of the year as it folds up pretty compacted and is easy to carry around when not in use.

There are of course couple things I don't like as much ... one is that the sunshade doesn't cover that well. Feels like we need to buy an extension piece or else he will definitely have a very nice tan (burn) after sitting in this all day on a sunny day (or you can just put a hat on the baby, problem solved :) ). The other is that I can't put this away with one hand since I always have to hold the stroller with one hand and use the other to pull the little lever on the side.. but I think it's really minor stuff that I can work around.

How this arrived
This arrived in a clear non-retail, plastic bag with a zip top, to open and close. The bag measured 16” x 12” x 4” and weighed in at near two (2) pounds. Inside were two (2) car seat protectors. Each weighed near one (1) pound.

What’s inside?
Inside were the two (2) car seat protectors I selected. They are very soft. The seats are competitively y priced, a fraction of the cost of a competing car seat cover that we own. In today’s world of inflation, keeping costs down, but receiving a quality product is a necessity. We think we found price and quality in this item. This item fits both front and rear facing seats. The textured material feels durable and high in quality. Protecting our vehicle’s seats is important. Nobody wants a stained, beat-up seat. This latch compatible cover has a textured top and non-slip back that prevents slipping. The bonus is that front storage pouch, very handy, keeps items off the floor. We think this product is still five (5) stars, but a weak five (5) star. Our competing seat cover which, was much more expensive, does not have those handy pockets but is made of a heavy-duty durable hard-shell rubbery like material. This is a soft-shell, which is still better than that towel we were using. We think a hard-shell works best for stiff leather seats and a softshell cover for seats that have soft seats, whether leather or fabric. Reason being, our stiff leather seats, in our imported vehicle, had significant seat impressions, from the car seat, using a soft-shell cover, but near none with a hard-shell cover. Where our American made vehicle, with soft leather seats, bounced back quick. So, if you are looking for a Seat Protector and really do not want to spend a lot of money, without sacrificing quality, consider this (made in China) item. You get quality at a very reasonable price.

I want two things in a diaper pail. First, it needs to keep the odor in. Second, it can't require proprietary bags (they're usually a ripoff).

I've used a number of diaper pails and have settled on this one. Odors stay in -- even in a room with a humidifier, which tends to, uh, enhance the odors if any are leaking out. Sure, when you slide the lid open and drop a diaper in, some stink does escape. But that's basic air displacement -- when the diaper drops into the Ubbi, some of the stinky air in there is going to be pushed out through the open lid. There isn't really much you can do about it unless your diaper pail contains a black hole. The smell will pass.

Bag extraction, however, is a significant issue. There are downward-facing plastic tabs around the rim of the Ubbi that catch on the bag and tear it. Every time. With some practice, I'm able to minimize the tearing. But I can't avoid it altogether and the results are less-than-appetizing. This seems like a correctable design flaw, but for now, it's one that exists.

I still think this is the best diaper pail on the market. Hopefully Ubbi can fix the bag extraction issue and it'll be perfect in my book.

These are small in size and they’re short in length. They are 4 inches long. The turtles are 2 inches long by 1.5 inches wide. The turtles have a stiff silicone body. The silicone is thick but still smooth and soft as one would expect with silicone.

The mouth of the turtle holds the utensil tip. It does slightly bend which makes me a little nervous about long-term use. The package does not say anything about dishwashing. Technically it’s metal and silicone, but I do worry about the place where the metal is inserted into the silicone of the turtles mouth. There is a small gap there but that should also probably be watched because food could easily get stuck in it and become moldy and one would ever know. Because of this, I have been hand washing and trying to use a scrub brush to brush the utensil/silicone joint. It seems like there may have been a sealant there in the beginning but it didn’t last long.

These are easy to grip for both adult and child. They are sturdy enough to use for self feeding or assisting baby. I like the combination of the silicone turtles and the stainless steel utensil heads.

This camera is great for the price. We registered for this camera and received it as a gift. The Babe is now 7 months old and we use this monitor EVERY DAY.
Pros: It is not over the top and is a great basic monitor for being able to hear and see baby. It has a white noise cancelling function, so white noise is cancelled out until the baby cries or a loud noise registers on the camera. It has infrared for being able to see in the dark.
Cons: It doesn't stay charged for very long, needs to be charged every night after using it for 3-4 hours during the day. There is a loud and annoying beep when the battery is low on the receiver.
This device works through the wi-fi which is a good an bad thing. Its great because the signal is outstanding anywhere in the house, but bad because it slows down the internet for any other device it is near.
Overall, this is definitely something I would recommend and purchase again in the future.
The adhesive isn't great but I switched to double sided tape and no problem.  Be careful cleaning because they scratch easily.

This is a really nice stroller! The standout feature of this stroller is the super canopy (I've included a picture). I turned mines into a travel system using the Graco Snugride 35 carseat in the color Logan (R'Us exclusive color). I attached the carseat to the stroller using the [[ASIN:B003Z6TJWG Cybex Infant Car Seat Adapter]]. The travel system is good for pushing the baby around town but I didn't feel that it worked good for transfering from the car to the stroller. The problem here is that it takes a little practice & is not practical when you are in a hurry.

The recline feature is really nice in that it reclines almost all the way flat. My little one is 13 months old so I still use the legrest in the up position. The legrest goes down easily with a little squeeze under both sides. This stroller is a little on the heavy side & cumbersome when folded. Getting on & off public transportation is a pain because the carrying strap is not comfortable to hold & when I use the carrying handle on the side the stroller tends to open on its own. I believe the weight will come in handy for a bigger baby to prevent tipping & it did come in handy keeping the stroller sturdy as a travel system.

I never purchased the plastic cover made by Cybex. This one works very well though [[ASIN:B001CUPT76 Jeep Deluxe Stroller Weather Shield]]. This covers the stoller completely! I have even used it with the canopy open. This is the only plastic that I've encountered that does this. Thus far I have not encountered any major problems with this stroller & I anticipate that it will still be in use until my baby is no longer in a stroller.

I got this swing as a gift from my father-in-law. I have the munchkin diaper pail and like it so it was decided the swing was a good option. My daughter loves it! I play her music from my phone all the time while shes in the swing.

For those who complain that the speed doesn't change between the settings, it's not so much speed as it is the range of swing. 1 is barely any swing and as you work your way up to 5 the swing goes further left and right. The speed itself doesn't change. I have no issues with this, just want to clarify it for those who are wondering about the speed settings.

The only reason I dropped a star is because of the fact that it doesnt have an option for batteries. I like the portability of the swing as I am a vendor at craft shows and my daughter goes with me, but I wish I could have batteries in it. I was thankfully able to get around this as my husband has a halo power bank and the cord that comes with the swing is usb. I would recommend a power bank like that as I am at shows for hours and her swing keeps going the entire time. Overall a good swing for the price!

I first purchased an ezpz mat about a year ago when my daughter was a year old. We purchased the larger mat, which I believe was the only one available at the time. She quickly figured out how to 'break the seal" by lifting one corner of the mat, and for some reason or another we stopped using the mat. I think because I felt it was too large to be practical for us.

However, we just endured a rough 3-month phase of my now 2 year old ending each meal by throwing her plate, food and all, on to the floor. Fed up I decided to get out our ezpz again, and it's made a huge difference! While she could lift the mat and throw it if she truly wanted to, she doesn't. Maybe because it's a bit heavier than the ikea kids plates she usually uses.

Once we started using the larger mat more, I decided I wanted another one in case the one was in the dishwasher. I decided to go with the smaller mat thinking it would be easier to take traveling or to restaurants. We did take the larger mat to restaurants a few times but found it wasn't super convenient because it was hard to carry there, and awkward to clean off after dinner to take home. I actually had to take it into the women's restroom to rinse it in the sink more than once. But I do feel this one will be much easier and more convenient for restaurants.

I also like the way it allows me to separate her food. And, maybe this is silly, but I've found it pushes me to make sure I give her three different food groups with each meal. The OCD in me likes to make sure I fill each 'bowl' in the plate, she she almost always gets a fruit, a veggie and a 'main dish.'

My baby was early term and wouldn't latch. Then he was given bottles of my milk in the hospital when he was having his jaundice treatments so he developed a preference. With his screaming at my boob (tried for weeks and am still trying to latch), nursing wasn't an option and I became a pumping mom exclusively. I was an extreme case where I developed a breast abscess after getting a cracked and bleeding nipple after using the medium standard medela flanges. After I developed the abscess, I purchased these which saved my pump life. The three sizes have fit me all throughout my stages of engorgement and attach directly to the medela pump parts. My abscess had to be drained and where the wound was I was able to used the smallest flange to avoid the incision. I initially thought I would have to let my boob dry-up! Pumping still hurts but it hurts way less with these and I get soo much milk. I only pump 4 times a day and I can produce up to 10 oz in each pump. My boobs have learned to store the milk for later which reduces the stress of pumping constantly. I for some reason still get cracked/bleeding nipples but it occurs way less often and I don't think I could've kept pumping and giving my baby my milk for this long without these flanges. My baby is 4 mos old and our goal is 6 mos!

This only gets 4 stars b/c I still think they could improve the design even more by adding a gel like material (think dr. sholes) that would like cradle and contour to the shape of the boob. I get indents where the ridges are. I have not found any flanges like that.

Diaper Rash is some bad stuff. It equals an unhappy baby and an unhappy baby equals no sleep.

I have been using this product as a way to avoid diaper rash. It is extremely easy to use. However, being a first time parent, I had a lot to learn. First off, this product works well, but you still have to make sure baby is completely dry before applying or you will still have diaper rash. Secondly, when the baby does have diaper rash, use a liberal amount of aquaphor rather than this product.

This works well as a quick application. However in the long run, you still need your tub of magic cream (aquaphor) if a rash develops. Since I have been applying this product correctly, I have had great success from the baby developing diaper rash (knocks on wood) when used in conjunction with the magic cream.

I hope I send you positive vibes of sleep with the approval of the product. It doesn't do everything, but if you dry completely the baby and apply a liberal amount, it is a quick application when you are in a pinch. Reason for 4 stars is cause in the end, you still need the magic cream. I recommend this product for those traveling and putting it in the diaper bag. Everyday home use, magic cream wins.

We bought it to replace "Fisher-Price Deluxe Cradle 'n Swing, Rainforest Friend" swing. We were skeptical because the Fisher price swing had better reviews on Amazon than Graco and still it turned out to be a horrible product. But this swing rocks (pun intended :-)).

The seat is larger and deeper than FP. It feels more cushiony too. Seat belts are also easier to put on than FP's and seems like they are more comfortable as my daughter doesn't fuss about them like she did in FP.

Another great feature is that rocker is removable!! we take the baby to the dining area while having dinner and she rocks herself to keep her entertained. That's another great feature that rocker rocks with baby's movement so you don't have to do it.

The reasons for taking one star off:

1. The hanging toy teddy from the motor don't turn. That was one feature in FP that my daughter loved. Especially when she was younger (1 month), still teddys didn't catch her attention. We bought another revolving toy to keep her entertained.

2. Motor makes clicking sound with every swing. The sound is not too loud and the baby doesn't seem to mind. We were concerned that motor might die soon (as some reviews had mentioned). We called Graco directly. They sent a new motor within a week at no charge!! that's great customer service. We never had to replace the motor.

3. At higher swing speed (3 or higher), the swings rocks very violently and hits the side bars. However, we never use anything above 1. 1 is enough to put the baby to sleep. So it wasn't any issue for us. It could be with this motor and the new motor could have fixed it but we never bothyered since level 1 is sufficient.

Overall, I would highly recommend this product.

The child base is rechargeable, which is a nice feature. Unfortunately, the parent unit is not (requires standard batteries). From a design standpoint, this does not make sense. The baby usually sleeps in same place (crib) but the parent usually moves around (bedroom, kitchen, living room). Thus, it would make sense that the child unit would usually be plugged in to the wall and the parent unit would be more mobile. It is the parent unit that requires rechargeable battery. But this is not the case. It would, of course, be nice if both ends were rechargeable.

Additionally, although a much minor point, when the child base is turned off, the parent unit starts emitting this incessant and shrill beeping, which is highly annoying. I'm sure it's a safety feature to alert you if the battery goes dead, but a more reasonable yet audible beep every 15 seconds or so would be much better, so everyone else in the room doesn't think the house is on fire!

Both of my exclusively breastfed babies easily transitioned to this bottle when starting daycare, which was awesome. I initially tried the Dr. Brown bottles on my first (now 2 1/2 years old) and she refused to drink from them. Her daycare teacher recommended that we try these and we used them until she was ready for a supple cup and are now using these again on my 3 month old. The nipples are definitely soft and more pliable and it helps the baby transition easier from breast to bottle and back to breast. They are easy to hold and overall are good bottles.

A few notes:
1) Cleaning the bottles is easy for the most part and there aren’t many parts involved (just the bottle, nipple, collar, and lid) but I haven’t figured out a great way to clean the little blue air valve at the bottom of the bottles.

2) Make sure you pull the nipple all the way through the collar so the accordion at the bottom of the nipple is fully on top of the collar. You need to pull it through using a back and forth motion as opposed to just pulling straight up (or else you’ll just pull the whole nipple out entirely and need to start over). If you don’t do this proper, the nipple won’t be able to move as it should.

3) As some other reviewers noted, sometimes the nipple does become inverted when the baby is sucking which is annoying and can lead to more air bubbles getting in the bottle which can contribute to gas. This is probably the biggest issue with these bottles and I don’t have a solution. I thought it was happening more frequently when the baby was sucking really hard, so I moved him up from Stage 1 to Stage 2 and it’s still happening, even though he’s only 3 months old. I’ve tried to hold the bottle at different angles to avoid this, but it still happens pretty frequently. I would try other bottles that don’t have this problem, but he hasn’t had any issues transitioning from bottle to breast so I’m afraid to mess that up by trying something else new.

I love the concept of a no-touch IR thermometer for measuring body temperature, but there are severe usage caveats that commonly result in incorrect readings --

A user must understand that this IR thermometer measures your forehead skin temperature (from an inch away) and the ambient air temperature (averaged over the last ~10 minutes), and then tries to CALCULATE your internal body temperature using a FORMULA.

Because of the way it works, the thermometer must have been sitting in the same room next to you for at least 10 minutes, you must not be sweating too much, you and the Veratemp must not have been lying in the sun, you must not have recently popped out of the shower or pool, and you must not have had your forehead covered by a ski-cap or washcloth or something.

In other words, you can't walk in from outside and expect to take your temperature right away, but perhaps you can walk inside, grab the thermometer, wait for 30+ minutes for your skin temperature to acclimate to the room temperature, and THEN use it to take your temperature. Similarly, you can't run downstairs and grab the thermometer from a drawer and expect to take anyone's temperature right away, unless it happens to be the exact same temperature upstairs versus in the drawer where the Veratemp was stored.

However, if the thermometer is sitting on a nightstand next to a stationary patient, and room air temperature is stable and doesn't vary by more than a degree or so, then the Veratemp works pretty well (in my experience) and is much more convenient than other thermometers.

The thermometer also allows direct measurement of surface temperature, so you need to make sure that it's in "BODY" mode when you want it to calculate your body temperature -- do read the instructions.

I’ve had trouble with thermometers for a while now. No idea why but they’re never accurate. After my son spiked a 105 fever (he’s fine now, as I’m sure you, dear amazon review reader, care deeply about) my “best thermometer for home use” POS was giving me very inconsistent readings as I was trying to bring his temp down. Literally 2 degree differences from minute to minute. So I ordered this! And I am so very pleased with it! There is some room for improvement as there is with most every product ever, but for what it does it’s amazing! Here’s my breakdown in a handy dandy pro & con list!

Pro:
Constantly monitors temp
Night mode lets you keep a darker screen up with the current temp and a graph of the temp over the last hour
High and low temp alarms which you can set thresholds for!!!! (This helped me actually get some sleep instead of staying awake to check temps manually)
You don’t have to bug your child to get a temp
You don’t have to try to find a pinpointed spot on their forehead in the dark overnight
You can track medications and symptoms
The app tells you how their temp responds to meds
The app can even give you Tylenol and Motrin dosing info!!!!
The readings have been accurate every time I’ve checked it against a standard oral thermometer.

Cons:
There are some connectivity issues (but find me one gadget that doesn’t, amiright???)
Sometimes the temp reading will go wonky but it usually adjusts within a minute
The temp alarms continue to go off even after being muted.

This infant seat from Britax is a very nice quality seat. The fabric seat pad is a nice easy to wipe clean material that feels smooth to the touch and not grabby and rough like some infant seats. The harness for this seat is easy to adjust. Simply pull the front adjuster strap to tighten the harness for secure fit and release by pressing the red button when you want to loosen the straps to easily remove the baby from the carrier. The process for adjusting the shoulder height for the harness is relatively easy. You will need to rethread the harness when changing the shoulder height, but the process only takes about a minute (see owner's manual for instructions for how to properly do this).The canopy on this seat is generously sized, but I don't like how it droops a bit when it is only partially extended. When combined with the B-agile stroller you get full coverage for the baby when extending the stroller and car seat canopies. The carrier handle is comfortable to hold for when you are transporting the baby. This seat easily clicks into the Britax B-Agile (single) and B-Ready strollers for travel system convenience. The installation process for the car seat base is very easy. The leveling foot for the base adjusts with just the press of a button to get just the right fit to your car. Both sides of the base have a level indicator so you can check to make sure the incline is right from either side of the base. The seat feels slightly heavier than the Chicco Keyfit 30, but seems to be comparable in weight to the Chicco Fit2 infant seat. The B Safe 35 is supposed to be able to accommodate a child up to 35 lbs, but I seriously doubt a 35lb child will fit in this seat. My 10 1/2 month old daughter who is not yet 20lbs is very squished in this seat. I'd say this seat is ideal for newborn through about 4-7 months old depending on how large your baby is. The seat is narrow and deep, so babies with broad shoulders are likely not going to be very comfortable in this seat beyond the first few months.
Overall it's a nice seat. It's a quality seat that is very safe and easy to use.

We have the DaVinci mini-crib but it has been sitting around unused for a while (I'll save the complaints for the review on the mini-crib). Now our kid is old enough we decide to give the conversion rail kit a try. The package contains the 2 rails on each side, and 8 bolts and barrel locks. the wood feels sturdy, although it's the same kind as the mini crib so it'll be prone to scratches.
Installation was easy, just take apart the mini crib and attach the headboard and bed end to the rails using the provided bolts and barrel locks. It's a little tricky for one person, but for 2 people it'll be a piece of cake to install. I do have some concerns over relying on just the 8 bolts to handle the weight of the bed. It would be a better design if they used a joint to attach the rail and headboard (I think it's called Mortise and tenon joint), that would be much more reliable.
The conversion rail kit doesn't come with slats/bunkie board or box spring, so we had to buy it ourselves. the width between the rails is exactly 38", so keep that in mind when you purchase the slats/box spring. We went with Ikea Luroy slats because it's cheap and has 16 slats; the Ikea boxspring would also fit (37.5" wide) but we didn't have means to transport it and didn't want to pay for delivery. Anyway, the slats fit right in, but tends to move around. This is a typical problem for Ikea beds so there're plenty of suggestions on the web for fixing it. for now we just placed the mini-crib mattress and the mattress board beneath the slats and that was tall enough to push against the slats, keeping them mostly in place. The bed is pretty low and around 1' off the ground, so depending on how thick your mattress is you may want to go with a box spring instead of slats.
Overall we're happy with the results, although it would be better if DaVinci also offers the slats/box spring along with the conversion rails so we don't have to go out and buy something on our own.

From 2018:
I want to love this monitor, I really do. If I could give half stars I would have given a 3 1/2.

Pros:
1. Good cameras. LOVE the night vision.

2. Nice sound.

3. Easy to use - especially pairing the cameras to the parent unit.

Cons:
1. We have twins, so I wanted 2 cameras -1 per crib. There’s zero way one camera can cover the entire crib, unless maybe you mount it to your ceiling (unlikely). But for the majority of people who have one crib, 2 cameras will definitely cover the whole thing. And if you’re using this to just look at a room in general, I’m sure it’s fine.

2. No belt clip. There’s a stand that pops out, but it’s pretty flimsy. I wish it had a belt clip so I could wear it around while I do chores.

3. Blinking light. It lets you know it’s on, but if you’re like me and sensitive to light in the middle of the night, the blinking green light is a tad annoying.

4. Thermometer. It currently says one camera is 73 degrees and the other is 79, even though they’re 10 feet apart, so I don’t believe either.

Despite my list of cons, I’m keeping it. It does its job for a decent price, and gives me peace of mind when I want to see if the babies are awake or not.

- Rinse them out AS SOON as your kiddo's done with them. Use the sprayer to get at the corners.
- Use a drying rack like boon grass to keep it open and upright while it dries.

The instructions call for hand washing and laying flat to dry. I tried it this morning and it wasn't hard to do. I started early due to the time of year. First I filled my clean bath tub up a little over halfway and added liquid laundry detergent. I swished it around for a few minutes before opening the drain while still moving it around til the tub was empty. I repeated this process twice with plain water to rinse. I had already checked the days weather to make sure rain wasn't a possibility, set et up my porch. I had a 100' length of clothesline which I strung back and forth from rail to rail leaving 6" or so  of space and laid the blanket over it. From there i just laid the blanket over it and let it dry. It was a cool overcast day, Temps were about 35F when I placed it outside and only got to 53F. It took 8 hours under those conditions, which are about the worst case I would attempt this. I looked at it after I laid it out and realized a rope hammock would be ideal for doing this!

Look, I'm not a millionaire and cannot justify spending hundreds of dollars on a baby monitor. This one does the job, and it does the job well. It has a temp Guage, zoom in feature (which is the reason I purchased it because this mama wants to see if her boy is breathing) I can move the camera up,down,left,&right. It plays music but In my opinion that feature is dumb because it plays it on both the camera and the parent unit? I don't want to hear that. We have a hatch so don't use it. I can turn up the volume and even hear my baby breathing if the camera is near him. The voice option is great to "shush" baby from downstairs, night vision is great too. I like that the camera and parent unit are charged with the same charger. Great for this lazy mom n for travel. So fat no connection issues, and the range is working great. Haven't tested how far it goes but In my 1700 Sq ft house I can go anywhere and can still see my baby. I've seen in another review that a mom had connected multiple cameras and got someone else's house. Not sure what to think about that, but in all honesty, if your posting pics of your kid on social media, your already taking that risk. So far this has definitely surpassed my expectation for a 70 dollar baby monitor.

This seems pretty sturdy once you have it properly in place, but if the doorjamb is even slightly uneven, it's surprisingly difficult to install snugly. If you over-tighten it by lengthening the screws too much, it's way to hard to open with one hand. But if you don't tighten it enough, trying to open it will pull it right out of the frame you've installed it in. We like it and won't bother getting a different one, but it's a pita to put back, if someone stumbles into it or pulls too hard trying to open it. If you can use both hands when opening it, it's fine: relatively easy. With one hand, you really have to push back on the button and lift the bottom at the same time, which can pull it loose.

When I was pregnant with my twins, I got a double travel system from Graco. It included the Graco Duo Glider MONSTROSITY. The thing was so big that it ate over half of the cargo space in the back of my van. It was heavy, but really easy to use as long as you didn't use the infant carriers with it. It felt like the front kid was SO far away from you.

I don't remember where I learned about the Combi Twin, but I tell ya...I couldn't craigslist the Graco fast enough once I had!

The good points:
*Small & compact
*Carrying strap
*Light
*Easy to fold (my husband can even do it)
*Fits through doors (sometimes takes a little manuvering as the wheels have to be straight, not at an angle or you won't make it)
*Independent reclining seats
*3 child cup-holders

The bad points:
*TINY storage baskets
*Sometimes a pain to lock once folded because the clasp gets tangled in basket fabric
*Tiny sunshades
*NO adult cup-holders

Despite the "bad" points, as all you mom's will know, you can remedy all of them:
For the tiny storage baskets, I have little hooks on the parent handle that I can hang shopping bags or my purse on.

The clasp getting caught in the basket fabric is cured with preventative measures. I lean down & turn the clasp out before folding.

For the Tiny sunshades, I just bought the kiddopotomus sunshade ([...]

The lack of a parent cup-holder is the biggest challenge. I use the Skip Hop Double Duo diaperbag because it will clip onto the back of the stroller. I use one of the front pockets or one of the side-sippy cup pockets of the diaper bag for holding my beverage.

All in all, I love this stroller. My g/f who had twins a year behind me visited recently & was insanely jealous of mine (she also has the Graco). I'd recommend it despite any "set-backs"!!
I would say this mat does not have enough cushion for a baby that is trying to walk and still need more head protection but good enough for crawling baby and play mat overall
