Everything about this camera was great. For $100 it beat many of the other cameras I tried in person for the same price. It had great quality picture! The night vision was even phenomenal compared to other models I tried. The screen is small but that seems to be the screen size for this price range. You don't need a huge screen if you are just using it to alert you to go check on your baby; your going to go there in person anyway. The battery life was great and it had fantastic range. The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 was the sound. When I had the volume turned all the way up it emitted humming/white noise. This noise got me curious on what the DXR-8 version was like. I ended up returning the DXR-5 because I like the DXR-8 much more. The DXR-8 is double the price but for good reason. I had also tested a Levana. For $100, this is the best monitor in the price range I tried.  The DXR-8 just had more buttons and whistles and I was willing to spend that kind of money.

My husband and I love the Moby! I was intimidated by the wrapping at first, but after I practiced a couple times and watched the video on their website, I've got it down. Our daughter is one of those "don't put me down...ever" babies, so this has saved us. Much more comfortable to wear than the Baby Bjorn we used for our first child (the BB made our shoulders pretty sore), and our daughter much prefers to be in the Moby as opposed to the BB. I just wish it were as quick to put on as the BB is, and that it were as easy to store. 18' of fabric still drags on the ground, even when draped over the top of a door.

I'm a nursing mom and I've nursed with the Moby on. It can easily serve as a modesty drape, but it's far easier to use if you're wearing a nursing top.

We bought two Mobys: one with the owl pattern and the plain blue one. The blue one still feels a bit stiff (not necessarily in a bad way) and has stayed close to its original size. The owl pattern Moby feels softer but has shrunk enough that it's hard for my husband (5'11" 175 lbs) to wear it.

One more thing: changing a baby in a public bathroom stall is much easier with a Moby because when you're done you can plunk the baby in, gather your stuff, and both of your hands are free for washing (much better and safer than the baby-juggle-while-one-hand-washes-itself technique).

I would buy one again, and I would definitely give this as a baby shower gift.

We waited to buy this hoping someone would come out with a review first but finally just bought one and decided we'd review it ourselves.

We have 3 kids with plans for more. We bought the full package with Joey seat, canopy, and ride along on the back, cost us close to $1,100 when it's all done, but it was worth it.

The thing about larger families and strollers is the choices are awful. For a double the britax was our first stroller, it had a special pull tab to fold up and we loved it, spent over $500 on that stroller but with wear and tear of travel and use it lasted us 3 years and we needed a new one.

To our knowledge the valco is the only option with the 3rd seat setup like this. We've had all 3 kids on this stroller including a 4 month old, 2 and 3 year old and they love it. Trying to get all 3 in a double just for a short distance was awful.

And trying to get a triple stroller through a standard doorway is pretty hard when using the wide strollers or insanely long versions.

This stroller folds up extremely easy and is very similar in size weight to the britax double when collapsed. The wheels are air filled vs rubber which can be an issue with a flat and sticks out more than other strollers but it makes going through grass so much easier-our old stroller got stuck constantly due to small rubber wheels.

The only downfall is you can't push down on the handles to pop over a curb. The way it's designed to fold it cannot handle the extra force, doing that long term would definitely break this stroller.

That being said, just turn the stroller around and go up backwards or go up the sidewalk ramp like you're supposed to and you'll have no issues.

This thing is a tank with all the extras. Some families might not like that, but to parents with more than 2 kids it's well worth the money.

Many complaints on pairing a additional camera. The other top reviews may be helpful on this subject but not so for us. The instructions left out few simple steps. BE SURE TO READ ALL STEPS, MOST IMPORTANT ARE 3,4,5

*It will probably be best to do step 5 first to get monitor onto C2 prior to pairing

1) Turn additional camera power to off

2) Cover the light sensor (try a dark room in addition to a finger or cloth)

3) Turn additional camera back on
it will flash a red light for a few seconds - the pairing must be done during the red flash

4) With the monitor on (does not need to be turned off) hold the play/pause button
*be sure to press the play/pause button during the red flash sequence or it will not pair

5) The pair icon will appear as C1
5.a.) Use side arrows to cycle to C2
*this step can be done prior to the pairing process so when you actually pair the monitor will already be set to C2 in the menu
C1 will still be showing after this but when you do step 4 it will be set to C2

6) press the menu button

7) you are now paired

We have a 10 month old little girl (and by "little" I mean tiny...only 16 pounds!) and we've had this stroller since she was born. It has been a great stroller, is very sturdy, has an awesome canopy, and is easy to push.

It also can handle some abuse. Unbeknownst to me, one day my wife set the Joovy on the driveway behind my car (still have no idea why she did this). When I proceeded to back up I ran over it, wedging it under the car. I heard a little scratching sound and slowly backed up while trying to figure it out. I eventually got out and to my horror found our $200 stroller trapped under the car. I got on my belly and saw that it was really stuck and I pulled and wiggled it for about ten minutes before finally working it loose. I popped it open and set it on level ground to find that it still worked perfectly...it just had a few cosmetic imperfections.

Here are some pros and cons:

PROS:
1. Very easy to push.
2. Huge canopy.
3. The reclining mechanism is easy to use, and it reclines almost flat making the stroller a viable changing pad if needed.
4. Cup holders on back of canopy.
5. Wheels are very easily removed (which works well to lessen on of my cons below).
6. Very sturdy. If you lock yourself out of your house, the stroller could double as a battering ram to get you through the front door.

CONS:
1. When you fold and unfold it the plastic pieces that latch the sides of the canopy to the sides of the stroller often come undone, and most of the time you have to refold the stroller a small bit to latch them back on. We have now learned to check that out before popping it open so we can go ahead and fix it before we put our mini-baby in it.
2. Wheel lock is INCREDIBLY difficult to push down to engage. It is so difficult that I often have to put almost my full weight on the lock while rolling the stroller back and forth. I'm beginning to think we have a faulty unit.
3. Due to the way the wheels are designed, it is bulky when it is folded. But...since the wheels come off and reattach so easily that can reduce the bulkiness.
4. This stroller is really designed for a bigger and probably older baby. We really had to wrestle with the straps to get them to fit our baby when she was itty-bitty (2 months and less). It's not a problem now.

*EDIT (August 2, 2011): I've been meaning to put in this edit for a while now. Con #3 finally did the locking mechanism in. Last fall I was using my foot to press down the wheel lock on the right side (which actually locks both wheels) and it finally snapped off. Fortunately the left side will still work, but I imagine it's only a matter of time before that one breaks as well rendering the stroller unlockable. It's still a good stroller and I do recommend it, but you have to be extremely careful with the wheel locks.

I looked long and hard to find a lightweight stroller that had a large enough underneath storage, parent cup holder, decent sized sunshade, and under $100 since we are using it as a 2nd stroller for neighborhood walks and for my husbands car for quick errands not as our daily use stroller. Our son is 9 months now and he fits fine in it (he is about 28"long and 20lbs)- I wish we had ordered it sooner but I kept putting it off since I could not find a store locally that had a model set up for me to check it out in person before ordering it and I was afraid it may be too short for my husband who is over 6' tall. Sears sells it for like $100 currently so this truly is the best deal for it at $54. It has the bells and whistles of a lightweight travel system stroller that would cost about $150 at babies r us, but it is light compact, a good color, and honestly the best thing you will find under $100 especially when you compare it to the features on the $100 umbrella strollers out there that are junk. It took us all of 10 minutes to put it together with no issues it was very easy to do. Also it reclines back really far for even a small baby to sleep who is 4 months or older who can hold their head up on their own without issues.
My ONLY complaints if I had to have any (which I still gave this 4 stars so its really not huge issues) about it is that the childs tray is a little high up for a small baby to see over but I am sure it is fine for a toddler a year or older, and it CAN be removed if you wish and dont need to use the tray. Also the "sitting up" position is still kind of reclined, which sometimes annoys my son so he will hold onto the tray to pull himself more upright to see over the tray. Also the sun canopy is very decent sized for a lightweight stroller- but I wish it came down a bit further to shield the sun from his eyes- we may purchase the shade extender for this issue.
Honestly all in all its a great value for $54 and could be used daily as a sole stroller no issues. Also,I like the roomy underneath storage basket on this one even more then my Bugaboo stroller!

This set is great as it includes everything you need: ink, print cards, labels and photo mat. The ink sheet is an awesome concept since no ink ends up on the baby!

However, if there's one think I'd change: the ink sheet.
- As soon as you buy it - check the ink sheet. All 3 sets I purchased had some substance (crystallization? mold?) on the ink sheet so it was ruined. These sets really should have expiration dates on them.
- As another review mentioned, I wish it included an additional ink sheet since it obviously is designed to frame 2 hand/foot prints. You can easily get multiple prints from a single sheet. Unfortunately, the subsequent prints get lighter and lighter - so you can really only get ~4 prints out of the sheet. Not a lot of room for error/practice with a squirmy infant. I like the suggestion of waiting for a sleepy baby...
- The size of the ink pad limits the size of the hand/foot print that can be done. The ink surface is 2 3/8" x 3 3/4". Make sure it's large enough if your baby is older than 2 months. My baby is 8 wks and it was about the right size.

Great concept - and despite the issues with my ink pad, Pearhead has great customer service. If you do have issues with the inkpad - just email their customer service. They responded within an hour and mailed replacement ink pads!

We have been using this monitor for a month and have been pretty happy with it. We bought the Motorola digital monitor (3.5" screen) and used both last night to compare. Here is a comparison:

Look and Feel:
The Summer Infant looks and feels MUCH nicer. It's more modern and sleek, feels heavier and just looks and feels like better quality..by quite a bit actually.

Zoom:
It's easier to zoom on the summer infant because you just touch the screen once, the menu pops up and you touch zoom..and it zooms. On the Motorola, you have to press a button, the menu pops up and you have to press an arrow button on the other side to scroll through the menu a few times to find zoom..then press a 3rd different button to zoom. So if your baby is doing something and you want to zoom..you kind of need both hands and it's not nearly as quick as zooming in with the summer infant. The motorola zooms a little more than the summer infant so that could be important if you have to keep your camera far away. You won't know until you try it.

Sound:
We didn't compare the sound because we also have a angelcare sound and movement monitor and we use that one for sound so sound isn't that important to us on the video monitor.

Features:
Motorola has more features including temperature (it was 2 degrees less than our angelcare temperature reading but they were 10 feet apart so that could have something to do with it). The Motorola also plays a few lullabies for the baby...but they sounded really cheap and more like carnival music to us. It would have been better if they played white noise as the weird carnival music isn't very relaxing in my opinion. We have the homedics sound machine and play it on rain so we didn't care that the motorola sounded poor. You can press "talk" on the summer infant and talk to your baby/kid. I'm not sure if motorola has that feature...we didn't play with it long enough and I'll get to why in a moment.

Image quality:
Motorola wins this one and it's the only plus to motorola for our needs. The quality of the actual video is better on the motorola. The infrared lights are pretty powerful on it..so much so that they make the crib cast shadows on the mattress. At first we thought the camera was shining a bright light on the crib and my husband snuck in the room to see and it was dark...no light. So we were pretty impressed with the magic of the infrared. The summer infant picture quality is less, especially at night when it's super dark in the room. If we gave the motorola picture quality an 8, we would give summer infant a 6 if that helps. It's a tough decision but this is why we're leaning toward the summer infant...

Camera:
The Motorola camera takes up a little less space and the picture quality is better but it doesn't pan down as far so you would really have to get it up high and somehow point it down manually as it faces straight out too much if that makes any sense. The camera sits lower to the base and whatever it's sitting on (a bookcase, tall dresser, etc). Because the summer infant camera is taller, it can pan down further and thus see more of the crib.

The camera on the motorola needed to be propped up in back to tilt it down and even then it couldn't get the whole crib in the picture. This is important to us because she sometimes scoots down to the foot of the crib and with the motorola we wouldn't be able to see her if she did. This may or may not be an issue for you...it depends on where you are able to keep the camera..again, you'll have to try it yourself to see.

Here are all the reasons why we are leaning toward the summer infant:
1. camera panning-summer infant pans down better and can get the whole crib in so we can see her when she scoots to the foot of the crib.

2. it's quicker to zoom in if we need to see her more closely (this was tough, though, bc we can see better with the motorola)

3. we really like how the summer infant sits upright in a docking base whereas the motorola lays flat and charges by being plugged into a little usb type cord. With the summer infant, I can grab it out of it's base or put it back down with one hand while holding our baby. The motorola is just more annoying and needs two hands and then you have a loose cord.

but i really wish summer infant, for the price, would use the same infrared technology. it's been around forever, there really is no reason why they can't get a clearer picture.

I guess what most people look for in a review are the cons, so I'll start there. This stroller is huge, making it less than ideal if you are looking to put it in the trunk of a car. Sometimes I catch the rear wheels on stuff--but they are what give it a great smooth ride. They are also solid instead of inflatable, which means no maintainence.
It folds pretty compactly if you take the seat off, but it isn't necessary. The seat is reversible giving you the option of being able to see your baby while pushing it.
It would also be nice if it included a cup holder or child's tray. I purchased a Baby Jogger cup holder and installed it--which is a bit of a pain. The pockets inside of the basket hold drinks fine, but it would still be nice not to have to bend over.
Everything is removable, which is usually great, but sometimes my wheels come off when folding it. It only takes 1 second to put them on, but I fear really losing one when gate checking it at the airport.
It is supposed to be easy to fold, but this took me a while to actually figure out. It is very simple once you understand it, but I'm impatient and didn't read the instructions.
Some great things. I love, love, love that the bassinet is included. However, you probably won't get too much use out of it if you use it for your baby, I think it's supposed to be used until they are 15 lbs. I however, never follow these rules and put both my 6 month old and 2 yo in it together. The older one just sits with his legs straight out and the baby sits between them. I also have the optional footboard that my 5 year old stands on. I can push the Vista with all 3 kids in/on it with minimal effort. If it's just the baby, its really easy to steer and push one handed. Seriously, its the best ride of any stroller I've tried (and I've owned at least 7 or 8).
The colors are great, although a little more subdued in person. It was really hard to find a purple stroller, so it made me so happy to find the Vista. Unfortunately, it's been discontinued in the 2009 lineup.
The adjustable height handle is a lifesaver. No more stooping over again. Everything is washable, which is great for the mattress cover in the bassinet, since my baby tends to be leaky. It also reverses from a breathable side to a warmer microfiber/sueded side, which would probably be nice in a cooler climate (not for this FL gal).
And best of all, it just plain looks cool. It's a head turner of a stroller and who doesn't love being envied? Unless of course, some steals it, which is always on my mind when we are at Disney.
So if you have a place for a larger, sturdy stroller with a super easy ride, this is a fantastic choice and one you don't see every mom in town pushing.

Set up wasn't difficult. It just takes a little while (30 minutes or so) because there are so many screws. But those things are a necessary evil in something you want to make sure is stable as it can be. The directions were OK, could have been more detailed, but I didn't miss any steps on the first try, fortunately. No need for any tools. They provide everything, though your own Philips may be more comfortable to use.

After putting together all the wood pieces, the last piece you install is the safety strap that goes along the back to keep the child from falling backward. This seems to be the only weak spot on the stool. I think there could have been a better way to secure the back than a yellow card. However, once installed, it does do the job. The weak parts are the "metal" rings that you screw into the stool for the straps to go through. These rings are very cheap and not made of strong materials. One of our rings broke before we even put them on. I had to use a mix of wood and crazy glue to get it to work. I made sure I placed it in a position that works even if it does "break." It's frustrating, though, as these should be made of steel.

For $100, I think the materials should all be top-notch. The wood is great, though. Very strong. All in all, we are happy with this but wish the pieces could be more quality.

We are purchasing the foam mat to put under it and taking one users suggestion to add the rings to clip toys on the gate itself. All in all I am pleased with the product. I would mention it is six panels so if you want to use it in more of a square shape I would suggest buying either a second one or the 2 panel extension which is what we are doing. Otherwise the square is actually a rectangle and it's not as large as it is in the octagon shape.

PROS:
- Inexpensive (ours was $48 w/ free s&h)
- Gives me the freedom to do chores without worrying.
- Gives my daughter the freedom she craves in a environment I can easily move and baby proof.
- Heavy material but light enough to move easily.
- It's short enough I can reach over it without having to climb in (see CON below).

CONS:
- The color of the gate (if that bothers you, it is a "cheaper" looking heavy plastic)
- If I had known the shape configuration I would have bought a second or the extension immediately.
- No gate - So if you are short like I am if you needed to get in it would take a bit longer.

Personally the color didn't bother me and we are satisfied. Since today is our first day of ownership I will update after we own it for awhile if there are issues.

We had the Diono Pacifica for 4 years and we absolutely loved it. I was so grateful for having had such a safe seat to protect him. We wanted to replace it with the same seat but were sad to learn that the Pacifica model had been discontinued and the width of thee side wings on the new Diono Rainier was just slightly too wide to fit comfortably in our back seat. We settled for the Radian 3RXT as a replacement. It’s pretty good quality, sturdy and feels super safe. My son seems to find the seat part less padded and not as comfortable as his old Pacifica but overall it’s comfortable. I was looking for a pet gate that was very tall and would swing out of the way for full width gate access when moving things.

This one does the job, it covers the stairs down to a basement area - if mounted properly to a solid wall / wood studs or solid wood framing it seems very solid. Most of the width is available to pass through. It is reasonably straight forward to install assuming reasonable mechanical skills with finding studs / using a tape measure etc.. The gate is relatively heavy, the two pieces are held together with plastic clips which work but aren't super easy to join and seem solid enough but not amazing.

The gate is relatively heavy (solid) but you have to lift it and depress a lever to open. My mother can get through it, but it isn't super easy for her. Unfortunately it does not swing closed and latch - you also have to lift it and notch it into the latch to close it properly. It works fine, but isn't a easy hands full operation and I wouldn't want it on a frequently used space, it does the job well for occasional access.

We bought another gate, for another area, which is tension fit (not as solid, but still good) not quite as tall - but it springs closed on its own, stays open when fully open, and latches automatically - much better for frequent use and easier to pass through when your hands are full (it has a smaller section that swings open, lighter and easier to handle, but not full width for passing larger objects through. Still does require lifting and pressing a latch, but a bit easier - mostly easier to close.)

All in all, pretty happy with it, but it doesn't function as easily as some other options.

When my daughter was born I used the Skip Hop Grand Central and I loved it. Once she got older and more mobile, I wanted something a little smaller and hands free. I purchased the Forma in the teal color. I did like the bag but found there wasn't enough internal organization for me. I ended up selling my bag locally. I currently use the Miss Fong bag.

What I liked:
- Very Pretty Color
- Light Weight
- Has a Grab Handle
- Packing Cubes, Changing Pad & Stroller Clips Included
- Large External Bottle Pockets
- Good Quality
- Can Hold A Lot
- Comfortable to Wear

Things I Would Change:
- There are only 2 pockets inside the main compartment. I need more. I don't like packing in pouches but had to with this bag.
- The zippers aren't very smooth. I couldn't open or close the main compartment with one hand. That's very frustrating when you're holding a crying baby in one hand and needing to get into your bag with the other hand. (My Miss Fong bag is so easy to use 1 handed)
- I didn't use the packing cubes. I found them too big for anything I carried, thus taking up valuable space. I would really love the bag if the compartment where the packing cubes go had some internal pockets for those of us who don't want to use the cubes. All my items just fell to the bottom of the compartment and I had to dig around to find what I needed.
- The bag didn't feel classy enough to wear at church or special events. It would be so pretty if it came in a faux leather, though the bag would be a little heavier.

I love having a video monitor that I can take anywhere around the house and still keep an eye on my baby.  I've been using this monitor for two months ever since I moved my baby from the bassinet to her own room and crib.  I love being able to, for example, go exercise downstairs and still keep an eye on her while she's sleeping.  I can do chores, go outside, or simply relax on the couch knowing I don't have to go into her room to see if she's okay.  The best part is flipping on the camera in the middle of the night when she's been sleeping for hours.  I like being able to see that she's still fine and isn't in any SIDS danger without having to get out of bed.  HOWEVER, I also have a voice monitor that runs constantly in concert with the video.  This video camera comes with voice activation, which is worthless in my opinion because it doesn't turn on unless the baby is crying.  I'd rather have warning that the baby is waking up versus not responding to her until she's pissed off.  So, the voice monitor is great for that, especially at night.  This video monitor alone wouldn't cut it.  So, if you can find one that has constant voice along with video, that'd be perfect.

I received this high chair as a gift. I love the solid-color design but could do without the obtrusive logos.

My biggest gripe is cleaning it. Yes, it wipes clean, but there are all kinds of cracks that food gets stuck in, so it takes multiple passes and digging in said cracks to really get everything. I just now turned it upside down to empty crumbs outside, and they were still stuck in there. Also the lift-off tray that you can put in the dishwasher inevitably gets food stuck underneath it, so it's just an extra thing to clean. All the ledges, footrest, etc. just feel like crumb collectors.

Guess I'm used to the Bumbo, which I loved as a eating station with tray, precisely because I could wash it in the tub afterwards.

It's unwieldly to move also, unless you fold it into carrying mode, which forces you to dump all the crumbs on the floor.

If you plan on transporting your high chair, this is a great choice since it easily collapses to a small size with a handle. However, I typically leave the chair at the table and wish it were easier to clean.

The swing-open tray also feels a bit flimsy, like it might break off at some point, particularly if you put a lot of food on it.

No recline feature on the high chair--but no baby needs to eat lying down, right? This was not missed.

The five-point harness feels very safe, a big plus.

At the end of the day, though, maybe cleaning any high chair is a drag? Why don't they make them where the seat and tray pops off and you rinse it in the shower?? Grrr

I find myself wishing I had spent more and gotten the Graco convertible seat I had been looking at. My child seems to be super comfortable in this chair, we made an 8 hour car trip and she did okay with this chair. This is the only reason it is getting four stars from me.

This seat was the cheapest seat I was comfortable with buying for my child and you get what you pay for with accessories and conveniences... which is to say nothing. It is a pain in the you know what to install. My Graco infant seat took my 5 minutes while pregnant to install. This seat took me half an hour. The instructions in the box didn't even match my model of chair, they seemed to be for the model prior. To get this chair right and not wiggling took so much effort! I had to try it in three different areas via LATCH to get it safe. You have to be careful when using the button ton release the seat belt, the first couple times you learn really quick... I cut the skin off the back of my index finger on a sharp plastic edge. This seat is also not quickly adjusted and will likely require removal from your vehicle to do so... but really, how often does that really have to happen?

Bottom line is the seat is functional. No, it's not easy to adjust and will only last a year or two, but for the price you really can't beat it... especially after you figure out how to not skin your finger taking your baby in and out.

My daughter had a ridiculously hard time leaving the bottle, well over 12 months old. After 6 different types of sippy cups, this is finally the one that she'll use. I think it's mostly because she wants to do everything like Mommy and this sippy cup looks similar to my [[ASIN:B007IRMX6C Rubbermaid 7R07 Hydration Beverage Bottle, 30-Ounce, Chug, Colors May Vary]]. Now, we drink side by side!

Also, there are some good plusses with this one. The hard spout lets her bite down & gnaw on it without worrying that the silicone will fail & she'll bite off a piece of it & choke. The spill-proof mechanism is very easy to clean and mostly hard plastic, not silicone! I'm not worried about mold collecting with this cup. The whole cup is easy to clean, as long as you have a bottle brush to get into the flared sides at the bottom. There are also spare spill-proof mechanisms available on Amazon, if we should ever need them. The 10 oz capacity is great, since my daughter is a water chugger at night & barely drinks during the day. The cup can easily be used without the spill-proof mechanism, once she's ready to regulate the flow herself.

The downsides are minor. The bottom is too wide to fit correctly in the cup hole on my [[ASIN:B00J36ZXOU Fisher-Price Spacesaver High Chair, Luminosity]], but it sort of fits by resting on top of the cup hole, if placed just right. It actually helps her learn to balance things. Also, there are no measurement markings on the cup.

Also, this is not a complaint, just info for frugal folks like me. I took my chances with the "colors may vary" option on two different orders. Each time I received the following combination: orange & green cups with blue & lime green lids. My daughter doesn't mind & neither do I.

When I registered for my baby shower, I inadvertently registered for the regular Ventaire bottles as well as the Natural Shape bottles (which is what I was wanting), so my review will discuss both types.

NATURAL SHAPE VENTAIRE

For starters, the Natural Shape bottles are good for babies who are breastfeeding, because the milk doesn't flow out when the bottle is tipped over. The baby really has to suck to get it out, and it has to open its mouth wider due to the size of the nipple.

Feeding my son with a stage 1 nipple took a REALLY long time. Approximately 40-45 minutes. However, I tried a Stage 2 nipple when he was about four months old, and the milk flowed out pretty easily. So quickly in fact that he got really mad and refused to eat because he was getting choked. I switched back to Stage 1 nipples, and also began relying heavily on the regular Ventaire bottles. He is now 5 months old and we have switched to Stage 2 nipples in the Natural Shape bottles, and he is doing well. He tends to finish a 6-7 oz bottle in about 10 minutes. These bottles are a lot wider than regular bottles, and he has a harder time trying to grasp and hold these bottles.

REGULAR VENTAIRE

Now for the regular Ventaire bottles. I found these bottles to be the better of the two for us. Although I had initially breastfed, and chose the Natural Shape bottles for that reason, I had to quit breastfeeding at four weeks. So the issue of having a nipple that wouldn't confuse the baby was no longer a concern for us.

The regular Ventaire bottles had no flow issues, even with Stage 1 nipples. He finished his bottle faster with this type of bottle and seemed to have no problems with the speed of the flow. We switched to Stage 2 nipples a couple of weeks ago and the transition was smooth. I didn't notice him getting choked, and he doesn't have to gulp as quickly as he does with the Stage 2 nipples on the Natural Shape bottles. These bottles are also slimmer, which makes it easier for him to try and grasp and hold the bottle.

Now for the operation of both types of bottles. They have a plastic disc that fits into the bottom ring of the bottle, then the bottle screws on, and finally the nipple in its ring screw on top of that. On the regular Ventaire bottles the disc fits snugly into the bottom. On the Natural Shape bottles, it has to fit into a little notch, and it is easy to think it's in right only to find out that its not (ie, when the milk starts leaking out).

We heat our bottles in a pan of water on the stove, and the bottom rings have a tendency to hold water. So if you use this method, you need to tap the bottle sideways on the pan to shake out the water in the ring, and I usually hold a dish towel up to the edge of the ring as well and tip the bottle so that all the hot water comes out. If you don't, when you tip the bottle to feed your baby the hot water will run down onto your hand (or the baby's hand if s/he can hold the bottle). This isn't really a reason not to buy the bottles, just something to be aware of.

Finally, some people have wondered if babies swallow less air with this type of bottle. I have two older children that I used standard bottles with, and I have seen no difference between those and these Playtex bottles. My son still burps just as much as the next baby. Occasionally during feeding you can hear some air leaking out, but overall, I really don't think it makes any difference.

For some reason there is an extremely limited number of wooden high chair models available in US. All of them are not cheap, but the Beyond Junior Y High Chair was on the lower end of the price range. This and the nice look of the chair sold it for me. When the chair arrived I found several things about it that were not evident from the pictures.

First of all - tray holders and all locks are plastic!!! I was really afraid to break all this parts when putting this chair together. When you put seat and foot rest in, you suppose to press this plastic lock and when I did it, all of them were making cracking noise. I am not sure those locks will survive several times of use, forget "life time".

Second - cushions are ridiculously cheap-made, paper-like fabric and provide no cushioning what so ever.

and the last, but the most important - the restraint. Abiie advertises it as "Dual Restraint System that can be adjusted for a 5-point harness or a 3-point harness, keeping your loved one secure and comfortable". The part about switching from 5 to 3-point is correct, which is really nice feature. However, those points are not fixed anyhow to the chair! Even though the company website states that the high chair "meets or exceeds ASTM F404-10, HR.4040 & JPMA 2.0 standards" it is difficult to believe that loose restraint system can meet safety standards. (And if it is true, something is wrong with those standards).
I noticed this issue when I was assembling the chair - pulled the restrain to adjust the length and it got loose on two out of three points. The restraints are held just by a little plastic buckle, which when moved slides through the cut-out and gets loose. (See the adjusted pics).

UPD. I have been using this high chair for about two months. After I fixed the restraint system (taped it to the seat) I am pretty satisfied with it, that is why I changed my rating from one star to four stars. The chair is very durable and can hold even an adult as advertised: we used it as an additional seat during a party.
Cushions are not very soft and looks like a paper fabric, but survived a laundry machine (gentle cycle) and came out very clean.

Did not give five stars because of several issues:
1. The restraint system (as stated above).
2. Plastic locks - one of them got a crack after third time I put the foot rest in and out.
3. Removable tray is made of quite soft plastic and scratched very easily. My child is learning how to use fork and knife and sometimes she would just start playing. As a result, the tray has fork marks all over.

So, if you can put up with this minor inconveniences, I would recommend this high chair.

I did a lot of research on a single fixed wheel jogger. My son is now 3 months, 12 lbs., and 22 inches, so not the biggest guy. But he is just now simply too big for this sling. We used this in our bathtub. He LOVED being in this sling for his baths, up until now. Pros and cons:

PROS:
- Sling has just the right amount of give in it that a smaller infant weighs it down nicely and their bottoms, and if you make it deep enough, chests, stay warm and submerged. (This is what made it so worth it for us, it really fit his little body just perfectly.)
-Contours to baby's body so my son seemed very comfortable always. (Ditto above.)
-Dries almost instantly.
-For the most part lived up to its 15 lb. weight limit.
- Very compact when folded.

CONS:
- Like others have written about he has finally gotten long enough to kick the grey plastic seam and cut his foot.
- He also wiggles a lot now and can almost fall out, and he is an underweight, short kid.
- Hard to unlock from the folded position. We don't shut the locking part anymore because we feel we're going to break the plastic tabs from pulling so hard to open it.

All in all, this sling made our baby very happy until he grew out of it, and its functionality makes me feel okay about him growing out of it a little early. I still think it was worth the three months we got, even though now I have to look for new bathing options.

Tiny baby finger nails as a new mom brought me a ton of anxiety when it came time to trimming my baby’s nails for the first time. I knew it had to happen of course because baby nails end up scratching both baby and yourself. They are so paper thin which scared me and I didn’t want to hurt my baby so I had to find an alternative way to trim them without feeling like I was going to clip her skin accidentally. Great alternative in that sense but the time it takes to file her nails down now that she’s older, wiggling and moving a ton in comparison to getting over the anxiety with practice using nail clippers is worth the price for that time period for this mama. You most likely won’t be using these very long, (est. NB-3mo) but, getting the practice in with this electric nail file was totally worth the purchase! I still use it sometimes to even out her nails after trimming them down! I would recommend this electric nail filer to a New Mom for sure. The speed settings (R2,R1,OFF,L1,L2) got a little confusing for me at first but you’ll get the hang of it and most likely set the speed and direction that works best for you and baby! The light on the devices is super helpful especially if baby is napping! Make sure to keep the instructions too so that you can differentiate the file heads from age and purpose! (I didn’t lol and I wish I had!)

I have a few children along with a 2 month old. Almost all my baby monitors have been a Summer product. Currently I have four cameras running but none of them hook up to my Wi-Fi like this Vtech does. Being Wi-Fi enabled means I can use the app to view and hear this camera even when I am not home. This is currently being used as our floater around the house. I have a baby swing in our den and a rocker in our living room. I wanted something I can plug-in quick and be able to throw a quick wash on or run to the kitchen while keeping an eye on the newborn.

We purchased this back in November to monitor our baby based on a friend's recommendation. The monitor works well, with plenty of range in our condo. The picture quality is good, particularly with night vision, so that it is always easy to see our baby and how she is doing. We like the temp feature to make sure the room is at the right level (which is important in our place, as we have a weird AC unit). Also, the auto-off on the monitor, while still showing the LED for sound and the audio is great so that we don't burn the battery (this setting is adjustable). The camera can be controlled remotely, which is helpful when setting up, and has a zoom feature that can be used to check that she is breathing (first baby - we're very nervous parents). The camera also doesn't make much light in the room, so doesn't disturb her sleeping. Generally we are very pleased with the device.

Only issue we ran into is after about size months of use, the monitor piece stopped working one night. Unclear what happened, but it would no longer turn on (the charging lights still worked). The company was very quick to support us, and sent us a new monitor with 2-day shipping immediately (we returned the old one). The new one was easy to set up and is working great. No hassles with the return. Great customer service!

We would buy this monitor again and recommend it to others.

We have a few different brands of diaper covers.  The Thirsties brand is one we like more than the others.  First off, is the bulkiness.  The Thirsties does not have bulk.  When your baby already has a bulky cloth diaper on, the last thing you want is more bulk in the cover to make clothes fit that much tighter.  This diaper cover is thin enough that it doesn't add much bulk while being thick enough to keep the wet stuff in.  The double gussets are a nice feature for keeping the mud from escaping out of the leg holes.  Though it does sometimes hit the cover, the inner gusset usually keeps it from getting much further and onto outfits.  The adjustable rise means that the cover grows as we move up in diaper sizes.  Our opinion is buy the Thirsties brand covers when you can find them at a fair price.  They are good at what they're designed for.

I ordered 6 different lightweight strollers in an attempt to find the perfect travel stroller for our little one. I was looking for an alternative to our Uppababy Cruz with a focus on airport travel since babe has outgrown/is no longer interested in her baby bjorn. Weight and convenience were big factors, but also want babe to be comfortable and would like stroller to last us a few years and a good amount of travel. I'm 5'10, my husband is 6'3, and babe is in 98% percentile, so needed one that worked with our heights. For reference, babe is currently 7 months.

The 6 I ordered were the qb pockit, qb qbit lte, summer infant 3d lite, summer infant 3d flip, uppababy glite and uppababy gluxe. We [unfortunately for my wallet] decided on the gluxe, but here are my comments on all 6:

qb pockit: this stroller is SO compact. if you need compact, this is awesome. The height was great for both parents and baby, and the fold is amazing. It does require both hands to open and close. It was easy to assemble, but I did think it felt a little flimsy for what we needed. The ultimate decision factor was babe did not seem very comfortable as she couldn't quite sit right in this. great idea, just not best for us. 3/5 stars.

gb qbit lte: this might be mom's fave. The fold is compact, not like the pockit, but still pretty small. The raspberry color is pretty and not overwhelming, the basket is big enough to hold something, and the one hand fold is GREAT! This felt sturdier than the pockit and wasn't too expensive. Also because of the handle design, you can push with one hand! however, babe also didn't seem comfortable in this (almost like the seat wasn't deep enough for her bum). I think this might be better for a slightly older baby, but unfortunately we need one now. 4/5 stars.

summer infant 3d lite: despite the amazing reviews, i was a little nervous that this would look and feel like a $56 stroller, especially compared to the others. I was VERY impressed when I played with it. I put this next to the gluxe and they are almost the same in terms of size, height, recline angles and the tires are very similar. If price was a big factor, this would be the clear winner. It's a great stroller for $56. I'm not convinced that this would last through more than one kid, but at that price, buying another wouldn't be a big deal. My issue with this stroller was babe's legs were in a funny spot. This would be good when she was taller (she's probably about 29" right now). Her feet hang off but the base hits her in a weird spot and I think would get uncomfortable after awhile. Again, I think this is an age/height issue, and if she were closer to 1 year it would be fine. 3/5 stars.

summer infant 3d flip: this seemed like a great idea... the lite with the added convenience of having babe face me! However, babe can only be rear facing until 25 lbs (so like next week). If we needed when babe was younger or if she wasn't a giant, this would be a great feature, but right now, isn't worth the difference from the 3d lite. I didn't take this out of the box as the weight restriction is clearly marked on the outside. i'm assuming the stroller itself is similar to the 3d lite, so 3/5 stars.

uppababy glite: i do love our other uppababy items, but wasn't sure the price of these lightweight strollers was justified. I liked the mesh seat back since babe always seems to get so warm, but that also doesn't provide a ton of support when she would be in this for longer periods. The stroller is light, but at 7 months I do think we still need to be able to recline and take a nap. this does require two hands to close (one hand and a foot to open) and i think should have only one brake for this price point. I liked it, I just thought the features fell a little short compared to the others. the wheels/tires move well, but the tires are not as good of quality as the 3dlite or the gluxe. 4/5 stars.

uppababy gluxe: i hate to love this, but it was the winner. the seat was by far the comfiest, the seat recline is easy and the angles seem perfect. this is a little heavier than the others but not noticeably. like the lite, you can open with a hand and a foot, but need two hands to close. to be compact, you need to take the front wheels off, but that is easy (one little button). it does stand on its own and I can see how the basket is hard to access, but there is no way my diaper bag would fit in there anyway so it will just be used for smaller items. babe definitely seemed most comfortable in this seat and the leg adjustments will help as she grows. i'm not thrilled about spending this much on another stroller, but based on how much i love our other uppababy products, i know i won't regret it in the long run. 5/5 stars (despite a 3/5 star price ha)

This bag is super cute, with many pockets for organization as many reviewers had noted. So I wanted to talk a little bit about the prints, weight of the bag, and noise factor, as I don't seem to see those in the reviews. Before this diaper bag I was wearing a BB gear backpack style diaper bag that was gifted to us. It's very functional and light weight, but after 7 months, I was sick of having to wear a "diaper bag" around. I wanted something more stylish that would go with most of my outfits, and that's where the BFF comes in.

After watching many youtube videos and doing lots of research, I took the dive and bought a BFF even though it's a wee bit pricy for a diaper bag. I first bought it in the Queen of the Nile color, thinking that it looks classic and elegant in picture. BUT, when it came, I was disappointed. The print is SUPER DIZZYING to look at!!! The white is a very bright white, with zigzag black lines through out. I tried to like it, but it just didn't work. It hurts my eyes to look at the bag! But because I love the bag itself, I exchanged for a Duchess print, which is a lot easier on the eyes and still looks cute.

The construction of the bag is high quality, it feels amazing to touch, and the hardware is high quality and a very pretty gold color. But because it's high quality (and not cheap plastic) the bag JINGLES when you walk around wearing it. Some people might like it, but I get kind of annoyed by the noise. A quick solution is to tug one of the zipper thing inside the bag so they don't hit against each other. Another issue is weight, this diaper bag is not that light compared to my old bag pack diaper bag, probably due to the hardware and just the general nice construction of the bag. Just something to be aware of. I let it slide because it's so cute! I don't plan on wearing it for long periods of time because I have back pain, would just put it underneath the stroller.

I included in the pics how I pack my bag. Some reviewers complained that the bag is too small. It is not as big as a true backpack style diaper bag, but any bigger it would've been too heavy and not look as cute. I bought their set pieces in the first lady print which helped me organize my stuff (my diapers and wipes are in the largest set piece). Sorry for the super long review, I hope it helps other moms in the market for a stylish and "mostly" practical diaper bag ;)

Installation is very easy (just 4 eye-hooks screwed into the wall), but it would have helped if they had included some drywall anchors. I had some anyways, so I didn't have to spend any extra money, but unless you're screwing the eye-hooks into solid wood, you need them. It's great that you can latch/unlatch the gate from either end, which makes quite easy to adapt to any opening and a snap to remove completely when you don't need it. Also, since it's accordion-style, it truly does fit any opening within the range, as opposed to the gates that you have to attach pieces to until it fits, and sometimes it just doesn't work at all. It does flex a bit when it's pushed, leaned on by my daughter, but certainly not enough to break. The plastic piece across the top keeps it quite secure enough for any normal use and abuse. It's tall enough, that my baby will never be able to get over it before we are able to quit using it. The open/close latch is not as easy as some, but after you do it a time or two, it's pretty easy and anyone should be able to handle it with one hand, while any typical kid of the age this should be used for should not be strong/dexterous enough to handle it. Overall, this fit my needs perfectly, and is a TERRIFIC VALUE at a fraction of the cost of much more elaborate gates.

I really want to LOVE this cup. I love the design, I love that it is transparent, I love that there are masurements marked on the side, I love the handles, and I love that it can easily convert to a straw or "big boy" cup. There are two big problems, however, which keep this from being 5 stars.

First, the lid is HARD to screw on. It's designed so that the spout is always directly lined up with the measurements-- but this means a lot of fiddling before the lid fits on properly. It's not ideal when you have a tired cranky toddler who just wants his cup of milk.

Second, the valve is CONSTANTLY popping out of the lid. Usually this only happens when there are temperature changes (putting warm milk into a cold cup, or allowing cold water to come to room temperature), but it is still a HUGE pain.

And here's a "bonus" con if you will: it's non-microwaveable. This is a huge deal for me, especially since my toddler won't drink his milk cold.

All this being said, I do really like this cup. It's easy to clean, easy to see how much liquid is left (and what kind of liquid it is), and I love the handles. I lust wish the lid was easier to use, and the valve would stay in place.

**UPDATE**
After 4 months of daily use this cup has started leaking BADLY. It dribbles all over my son while he is trying to drink from it. I did put it in the microwave for a couple seconds a few times, so I'm sure that's probably the cause, but it's bad enough that the cups are no longer usable. OXO guarantees replacements for defective products, so I will see if I can get a replacement. But be warned: when it says NOT microwave safe, it means it!

I bought these to fit in the Tommee Tippee bottles. They work excellently for this. When we found the Tommee Tippee bottles caused my son to spit up a bit and that he had a hard time latching onto these, we thought they'd be a waste. However, they are not. We slip them into a flip top sandwich bag, add a twist tie, and voila, a portable dose of formula. They stay closed nicely this way and are still very useful so nothing wasted. I wouldn't buy these if you don't have the Tommee Tippee bottles, but they can be repurposed easily enough and they work very well.

Pros:
1. They don't seem to have static cling and the sides are very smooth. So you can easily pour all the powder into the bottle.
2. They have a nice funnel in the lid to help prevent spills.
3. They are easy to clean.

Cons:

I wish it were possible to leave a review without a rating. But if you go look at the other kind of "reviews"--that is, what the parents selling it used on a famous online auction site say about this in their listings--it sounds like a lot of families only got to use it for a few days or a couple of weeks at the most. So if you're a daycare provider who sees a different group of kids in this age range every year, or if you have a large family that you can pass it around as part of the hand-me-downs, then this might be great, but if not, you might wait a while to see whether you actually need this kind of thing before you shell out a lot of money for something that you might not use.

First of all, the diapers came in a plastic bag that is sealed up with tape. The plastic was yellowed in color and so was the tape. I don't know if this is old stock that was lying around.

Upon opening the bag, the diaper covers, and the inserts have no odor to them, but they did have a lot of loose threads. I would definitely suggest washing these before using them, but that is just common sense when it comes to things going on the baby.

There are snaps galore on the covers themselves making them be one size fits all (but I would prefer to say one size fits most). The snaps are plastic and smooth. The snaps snap together very firmly, so I have no fear that they would come apart. But because some effort is needed to unsnap them, I do wonder how long they will last. The covers are solid colors, very bright.

On the inside of the cover there is a soft white material, which in my set of covers, there were bits of lint all over. That was easily taken care of with washing. Inside the cover at the back top edge, is an opening that you slide the insert into.

The insert is made of an absorbent material, reminds me of a thick microfiber. Even with sliding the insert into the pocket, I am not sure what would keep the top or back sides of the insert from sliding down and just bunching up in the crotch area of the diaper cover. I would think that an active toddler would have that insert bunched up in no time at all.

Also, for a toddler who is fond of their sippy cup or bottle, you might be going through a lot of these inserts and covers each day. The set does come with 6 covers and 10 inserts, but even with the insert being like a microfiber, I think leakage is highly possible.

When the baby is younger, I think these are going to be ideal. Even with the inserts not being held in place, an infant is not going to be running around and getting the insert to slide down and only cover the crotch area. Also, urine output is less with an infant, so hopefully less leakage.

Besides the covers and inserts, you do get a wet bag to put the dirty/wet inserts and covers in while you are out and about. Would even be nice to have at home to keep soiled diapers out of the regular laundry.

The inside of the cover, not the part facing the baby, is rubberized so hopefully that will help with some leakage. But where the outside of the cover and the inside are sewn together, there is a thin section of material all around that is not waterproof, so again I worry about leakage. That section is pretty much so in the crotch area where you would not want leakage. If you look at the closeup picture that shows the crotch section, you will see where the green material meets the white. There is nothing to stop the wetness from seeping to the cover.

All in all, I think these are very nice. But I guess it will actually depend on the baby that is wearing it and how well you can keep the insert from moving around.

Is this the safest infant seat on the market? Who knows, but it may well be. Perhaps the
"air-protect" is a gimmick, but it makes seems like a considerable advance in safety. Airbags in cars are particularly effective, and the use of passive airbags for head protection in a carseat sounds great to me.

What isn't a gimmick is that this car seat fits up to 35 lbs - which is more than any other infant seat. Plus, it isn't any heavier than a normal infant seat - the carrier weighs just 8 or 9 lbs.

The materials feel top notch, and look snazzy... Well, it looks about as cool as a carseat can look, which isn't saying much. The seat is very deep, which means true side-impact protection (airbags nonwithstanding) and more leg room for the little ones. The harness is very adjustable, and the single pull tensioner makes securing the child very easy. (The straps can be nice and loose to put the kid in, and with one tug on the tensioner, all the straps tighten right up.)

The base has an adjustable wedge so you can find the correct installation angle (supposedly) without using any towels or pool toys as shims. It works really easily, and can raise the seat to a fairly good angle to make up for deep or soft seats. Also - the infant insert isn't just a bit of padding - it has several parts and can be adjusted in many ways, which is probably why this seat can fit all the way down to a child of 4 lbs! Very well thought out.

Since some of our friends have complained of outgrowing even the (supposed) 30 lb weight-limit seats within 4-5 months, we're hoping to get much longer out of this seat. (It appears that most manufacturers raise the weight limits of their seats arbitrarily... Many children simply don't fit in the seats well before they reach the weight limit.) We were planning to get a Maxi-Cosi Mico, but heard countless stories of babies outgrowing it at 16-18 lbs! Because this Safety 1st Onboard Air 35 seat was designed significantly deeper and larger, it should last many months longer.

The canopy is plenty large enough and effective, although it isn't the smoothest to use. It's not bad, but as with many car seats we're looked at, the mechanism just isn't all that great. It is fantastic that you can leave the handle up when in the car if you want (many car seats require you to lower it) and the seat snaps into the base clearly and effortlessly every time.

For now I'm happy to give it five stars, even if there isn't much independent data supporting the air-protect feature. It's a good carseat anyway, and very competitive on features and price to anything else out there.

My only lingering concern is what stroller to dock it to. The Safety 1st Stroller that it is intended to dock with (the Aerolite LX) looks reasonable, but there are no reviews for it anywhere, nor can I find any store that sells it to have a look.

I'll post an update once the carseat gets some good use or we find another stroller that it works with.

With my first son we always labeled his daycare bottles cups and tupperwares with blue painters tape and a sharpie marker....I knew I wasn't interested in doing that for months and months with my second son so I looked into getting some of the fancy labels or the rubber rings that are out there for sale.  I wasn't impressed with the high prices or the huge kits that you had to buy and I couldn't figure out how I was going to go about putting a different date on them every day.  These write and seal labels turned out to be a great solution.  I wrote my son's name in fine point sharpie on the first layer and folded over the laminate layer and the sharpie has maintained its clarity.  Every day I write the date and either "breast" or "formula" on the label using a china marker, you know those waxy pencils.  I had a hard time finding them in stores but I easily found a two pack of them here on amazon for a couple of bucks.  They are great because they stay on the label until you rub them off or use soap and water.  No more tearing off small pieces of painters tape.  I also love the disposable blue tupperware with the round screw on lids for baby food or cereal and a bunch of those in my house also have these labels (lids usually only have half a label with my son's first name so we don't lose caps or lids).  I even placed a label on my older son's sippy.  I haven't had any problems with labels peeling off and I've been using all this for about 6 months now, its been great!

Initial Review:
The product arrived 2 days ago and after using it for a day I am really scared. My daughter is 1 year old and she is regular height. Her arm got stuck between the gaps.
Had she tripped while it was still stuck her arm would have snapped(see screenshots).

After this happened I checked reviews and couple of customers already mentioned the same.
I am not sure why amazon is tagging this product as "Amazon Choice"? The seller also did not change the design even after customers complained.
Amazon should stop selling this product until seller fixes the issue.

I temporarily fixed it by putting the anti-skid buckle on the top(see screenshot) but now the playpen skids.

Pros:
# The playpen is decent size (76x46) and it covers Large size 82.7 x 55.1 inches Baby Care Play Mat (https://www.amazon.com/Baby-Care-Play-Foam-Floor/dp/B0058K5IIQ/)
# Seller claims product is BPA free, non-toxic and non-recycle material with HDPE, no any odor.
# Bright colors
# Quality looks good and panels are sturdy.

Cons:
# Gaps are huge and it is very risky.

Update:
I contacted the seller and asked for 15 extra anti skid buckles which the seller has immediately sent. Now I have enough buckles to put on top and bottom. In order to secure the buckle on top I have put double foam tape so that my daughter doesn’t pull them out. Now the playpen doesn’t skid and I also closed the gaps.
I am happy with what I have but I would like seller to fix the problem permanently.

I also compared Uanlauo playpen with this one and this is better in size and sturdiness. Uanlauo is safe but it moves a lot and it is small.

My husband would like it kept on all night, but since it is on my side of the bed, I find the picture light too disturbing... We've had our Tripp Trappe high chair for 5+ years and it's being used by our 2nd child. We had the original tray which slid over the back of the chair. I was forced to buy this one b/c the original tray snapped when our 60lb dog jumped up on the high chair. We tried gorilla glue and even contacted Stokke about a replacement but alas - they don't make this model anymore. I was super annoyed at having to buy a new tray but once we started using it, I'm glad we got this newer model. Of the complaints I've read in previous reviews, here is my take:

- CLEANING: I purchased the white tray. My son has eaten food of every color and texture on this thing and to date, we have no stains. Red pasta leaves a slight "shadow" but I find that if you wash the tray immediately, or at least rinse it, the stains do not linger and are gone after another washing. Also, keep in mind this is a tray primarily FOR FOOD. IT IS GOING TO STAIN. Some other complaints were around food getting stuck underneath the tray in the honeycomb pattern. It can be annoying but again, I find that if I rinse it out as soon my child is done eating, it cuts back on the headache. The honeycomb pattern also makes the tray much sturdier so I appreciate that given how our original tray snapped.

- REMOVAL: You have to have the baby set with this in order to attach. Once you figure out how to put it on and can line it up with the baby set seat section, snapping it on takes about 2 seconds. Some complained a lot about removal and I did not have any issues at all. It's a simple release so all you have to do is squeeze the release and pull up on the tray and it's off. Again, once you know how to remove, it's really very simple.

- SIZE: The original tray (it was clear and slid over the back of the chair) was bigger than this tray. I thought that would bother me but it's actually been space saving and so much easier to clean in the sink. Since this tray snaps onto the baby set, there is no gap between the tray and seat section (at the waist) so food is not falling through the gap onto my son's lap.

I was annoyed that the white version was $10 more than the black or gray but such is supply & demand. I would recommend this tray and have not regretted buying it since we started using it. I'm now just trying to make the dog understand that he owes me $60 for breaking the other tray.

I’m not a person to review things but ALWAYS read reviews before I buy an online product. I’m a first time mom and had been using the medela pump in style for the past 6 months. I recently was noticing a decline in my supply and had contacted a lactation consultant about it and she suggested I rent a hospital grade pump. I was going to, until she realized they didn’t have any in stock :( . She recommended the spectra pump. So naturally I did what I always do before buying something I’m unfamiliar with and went online to research it. After reading positive reviews I went ahead and purchased it. When I received it, I read the manual and it was pretty easy to assemble and figure out. I WILL NEVER GO BACK TO MEDELA OR ANYTHING ELSE! This pump is amazing! It’s so gentle and quiet! My medela was on the highest setting and it was uncomfortable. The “massage” feature on the spectra is really nice. It’s similar to my baby’s natural suckle... unlike the medela. Within a few days, my supply was back to normal, and I didn’t have to spend $60 every two weeks to rent a hospital pump! I love the backflow protectors on the spectra. It keeps the tubes clean and prevents moisture from getting to the pump. It’s so much easier to keep clean. One thing I read from other reviews that was a complaint was that the spectra is for wide neck bottles. And for me, I use narrow neck bottles.  BUT you can buy flange attachments that will fit onto your medela flanges so you can use those instead of the spectra ones. They are little yellow inserts that attach the flange and tubing. I bought those the same day I purchased the spectra and it was a win win! So thank you to previous reviewers for that tip! Overall, I’m very happy with this purchase! It’s worth the money! I’m a happy momma!

We ordered and just received the Britax Boulevard 70 Convertible Car Seat in Onyx, (manufacture date 9/9/10), and the Onyx pattern that is shown in the product's picture is NOT what you will get on your actual seat.  The picture on Amazon's site is of the most recently updated fabric on Boulevard in Onyx, where the black/charcoal plaid pattern covers the seat, back, most of the arms and most of the wings of the seat.  What you will get is the previous fabric layout where the plaid fabric is in the center of the seat and covers the center top, back and seat, and the black fabric covers the arms and wings.  You will get the silver cord which outlines the seat as pictured, however.  The only reason I am not totally upset about not getting what was pictured is because we already have the Britax Boulevard 65 in Onyx for my preschooler, and her fabric looks just like the new Boulevard 70 in Onyx we just received which means I have very closely matching car seats now (except for the new silver cord and slight changes to the base on the Boulevard 70.)  I will be fine with this, but I just wanted to caution folks who have their heart set on the Boulevard 70 in Onyx EXACTLY as it is pictured, that it will likely be an altered version. Other than that, we LOVE our Boulevard 70 which we bought for our "big boy" one-year-old and the 65 which we've had for three years for our little girl.  They are big, safe, comfy seats which work perfectly in a Honda van. The shipping is very quick...we ordered on Monday night and received it on Friday afternoon.  We have nothing but love for the Boulevard 70, except for the fabric differences in the picture...which is, thankfully, fine for us but may not be for other buyers.

Of course other bottle warmers are so much faster but then you'd have to worry about over heating/remember to stop it/unplug...etc. Yes, sometimes it's a little frustrating to wait 10 minutes at 3 am in the morning but I just set an alarm for myself to get up 10-15 minutes before feeding time.

- Easy to assemble - just had to snap on the back wheels
- Lightweight

- Comes with a nice travel bag with handles, a cup holder, and a rain cover

- Lightweight - 14.4lbs
- Adjustable legrest
- Padded shoulders/buckle pads with 5 point harness
- Padded seat
- Adjustable seat (wish it reclined to be completely flat or sit upright to 90 degrees)

Cons:
There really aren't any cons. My husband says he wishes the wheels were a little bit thicker to make the ride a little smoother. Baby Jogger Strollers has to be one of the most over-priced brands around - hands down. I couldn't get over the fact that a single Baby Jogger City Select would set me back a good $499 or a double $669!! You never find these strollers on sale and places like Babies R Us or some of the online baby website will not take a coupon for Baby Jogger products! So when I lucked up on a gently used single Baby Jogger City Select, I didn't think twice about purchasing it! Move over Chicco double Mama's got a new stroller and she is happy!!

Since I have two children - a 2 yr old and a 10 mo. old I wanted an additional seat to turn the Baby Jogger into a double. I finally broke down and purchased the second seat kit in Ruby from Amazon.

I love that this stroller, used as a double, seats little ones stadium style. Of course this stroller is very versatile and the seats can be positioned in a variety of ways within seconds. Many strollers similar to Baby Jogger seat babies/children tandem, but one rides beneath the other. Where's the fun in that when your child's only view is out the side of the stroller or at his/her sibling's seat back?

Moving on, since I'm only reviewing the second seat kit I won't go into detail about how fabulous this stroller is. If your looking for a review that spills all the bells and whistles then read some of the other customer reviews on here - they've done a might fine job too.

So the second seat kit arrived, packaged up good and secure. Within minutes I had the second seat installed - literally. No tools are required whatsoever! Baby Jogger City Select has a cover above the front wheels which pops out with the click of a button. You install or click into place the seat brackets which come with the second seat kit and then attach the seat by clicking it into the brackets. Presto! You are finished and ready to roll!!

Adding the second seat to the stroller didn't create much more weight. Over all I'd say the City Select as a double weights much less than my Chicco Double!

Again, while I think Baby Jogger is over-priced, it's a product that's well built and worth the money.

For our first baby born in July '07, we used (and loved) the original Polycarbonate Avent bottles the first few months.  Then the BPA paranoia overtook us, and we switched to Born Free bottles, which are made of honey-colored Polyether Sulphone (PES).  The Born Free bottles worked well enough, but we hated the 2 extra complicated parts per bottle that we had to clean.  For our second kid born in Sept '09, we wanted badly to switch back to Avent, but read poor reviews of the PES BPA-free Avent bottles (apparently they leaked for many users).  Fortunately, right around that time, Avent introduced a second line of BPA-free bottles made of the cloudy Polypropylene (PPE), and initial reviews indicated that Avent fixed the leaks (by adding a simple removable collar between the bottle and nipple).  After 1 month of using these new PPE Avent bottles, I can attest that they indeed don't leak, and I don't need to take special care or do any procedure to make them leak-free.  They just don't leak.  Yes, the newly added collar is an extra part to clean, but at least it's a simple part that's easy to clean.  So for all you Avent fans out there, take heart!  Avent fixed the leaks.  Tip: the leaky PES honey-colored bottles come in yellow-colored boxes.  The new leak-free PPE cloudy bottles come in blue-colored boxes.  Buy the blue-colored boxes.

[[VIDEOID:7ac493ee788183bb7c9ad3b10e36d560]] I received this bag as a baby gift from my registry. I wanted a easy to clean, backpack style that would stand up on its own, but wasn’t so big that it got in the way during the pregnancy/infant stage while I was getting the hang of things. This bag has been perfect. It is structured enough that it stands up on its own. The material seems to hold up great and just wipes off. The backpack straps actually fit me, I have narrow shoulders and most fall off even tightened down on the straps. It comfy enough for me to wear packed full but my husband can also wear it without issues. It has an easy access zipper on the back which is absolutely genius and has me spoiled. I am looking for a larger bag with even more pockets as we go into colder month and his clothes are getting larger, and I don’t know if I can stand not having the easy access. I may just have to keep some extra necessities in my car and repack it if we are out for a full day! It has a lot of little pockets inside, a zipper pocket on the front, and an insulated pocket on the front. I like the travel changing pad enough, I normally put a freebie pad in the bag and use the travel changer that came with it as an extra in the house. It has two pockets on each side of the bag that are big to hold whatever you want. I have a larger wipe package on one side and a mini wet bag, phone, wallet and keys on the other.

The only thing I would change on this bag is make the entire front pocket insulated with no bottle holder or just a piece of elastic, rather than individual bottle pockets. My nanobebe bottles will not fit in it and has to be in a small cooler inside. I wish the interior pockets were Velcro or a magnet or maybe just made a little differently. I have a hard time getting things out with the elastic and I have tiny fingers, but stuff doesn’t just fall out if the bag falls over. So, there are pros and cons to the interior pockets. If you aren’t carrying the changing pad or if you get a separate changing cloth that rolls up in the bag, the pocket is the perfect side to keep a folder for any documents through the pregnancy phase and 4th trimester. It makes it very convenient if the doctors ask about something we went over last time, I have everything in one spot.

It’s a great bag. I’ve been carrying it around for about 5 months (half during pregnancy and half after birth) and it’s very been very convenient and just what I needed.

I took a leap and bought the brand new Joovy Scooter after reading just a few cursory reviews on mom blogs and reviewing the product info on the Joovy web site. And I'm glad I did. It's a terrific stroller. It was easy to put together. Just basically attaching the wheels and sliding the cup holder into place. And it rolls like a dream. A real smooth ride for my 6-month-old. It maneuvers great, too. As well as the BOB, which costs more than twice as much. I had a hard time deciding between a really lightweight umbrella stroller and something more substantial. And weight was a real consideration since we live in a second floor apartment. This was a good compromise. I can carry it up and down one flight of stairs without much of a problem, and even carried it up with the baby in it, sleeping, after our walk this afternoon. I can't carry it folded down the stairs with one arm with the baby in my other arm, and then set it up with one hand while still holding my 21-pounder. But I'll live. More features and you end up with a heavier stroller. And I can't imagine doing without - a.) The huge sunshade. We live in Florida, and I walk the baby a lot during the day, so this is really essential; b.) The big basket. You can fit a lot under here; c.) The toy pockets for baby. I put a toy in each one today, and he took them out and played with them when he got bored; d.) The peek-a-boo window; and e.) The parent's pocket, for keys, cell phone, etc. Now for the criticism, and I only have one -- the color. This stroller comes in black, greenie and orange. I didn't want a black stroller or an orange stroller, so I went with greenie, hoping it wouldn't be as bright as it looked on the Joovy web site. It is. It's flourescent green/yellow. My only wish is that Joovy would make this stroller in apple green, like the Joovy Kooper, and maybe also in that same beautiful shade of blue as the Joovy jogging stroller. Aesthetically, I think the Scooter is the most pleasing. It's a very balanced design, whereas the Kooper has that 'pitching forward' look, and the jogging strollers look sort of 'hoisted up.' It's just...Sooooo bright.

Yes, I am ashamed to admit I was one of those FTM who would look down on Pampers, Huggies, etc, thinking they were inferior.

So then we found Pampers Sensitive and all of our problems were solved. Yes, these DO HAVE fragrance. But they are different from regular Swaddlers because they don't cause a rash on my very sensitive daugther. So I don't mind the frangrance at all..

More recently, we've tried Pampers Pure, which I believe are going to be replacing Pampers Swaddlers Sensitive, and while they are great and DO NOT HAVE fragrance, it does not warrant the ~40% price difference in my opinion. I do like the llamas on them A LOT, but not all of them have llamas.. lol.

I am currently looking for a replacement since I can't find these in a size 4 anywhere. I really hope Pampers continues to make them because if the only option for sensitive babies is paying at least 50 cents a diaper for Pampers Pure, I will reluctantly have to find a different brand.
