Our baby room was upstairs, and I wanted to make sure it would work in the basement, as well as outside if we were in the backyard. Setup of the monitor was simple and we mounted the camera to the ceiling easily. The monitor is simple to navigate and the menu options are easy to use. I like that there is an option for the screen to turn off after a certain amount of time if you would like to conserve battery life.
After set up and using the monitor for 2 years here are my thoughts:
Pros: The camera is clear, not HD but you can't expect that. It is easy to see baby clearly, and there isn't a lag or delay in the image like many of the wifi cameras out there which I really appreciate. With wifi cameras there can be a 2 second delay which is frustrating. No big lag with this camera. Sound is great, yes there is white noise, but I assume all cameras will have that. The brightness of the screen can be dimmed, the sound can also be dimmed or muted, and there is still a visual audio that will light up if baby is crying or making noise.
We took the camera to our basement (directly below the baby room), in the next door room, and across the house to the kitchen and it had great reception. I didn't have any interference. We even took the monitor outside to the backyard and it works outside.
I love the multiple lens/multiple camera function. You can have a zoom lens or a widescreen lens so you can see the whole room. You can choose to view one camera or have it scan and rotate between the multiple cameras you own. This will be so handy when we have multiple kids or want to use one in a baby room and one in a playroom, etc.
Battery life seems pretty good, I didn't have problems with it dying on me, but I would always charge it at night. As time went on, the battery wouldn't last quite as long.
Cons:
The camera had an annoying beep anytime the battery was low or the camera lost reception. It is really really loud. (Thankfully this feature has been updated and there is now the option to mute the alert which is great!!)
The connection to the charging cable was really loose and wiggly. There is no way to open up the monitor if it needs to be fixed. It's glued shut.

We used this monitor for 2 years, being extremely careful with it. Our baby never played with it, it was never dropped, we always took care of it. Around the 2 year mark the monitor stopped working. The power button wouldn't turn on the monitor. If we pressed the power button and wiggled it a little sometimes it would turn on, but it finally stopped working. Maybe it was a connection issue, but there was no way to open it up and fix it. I was really frustrated that we spent so much money on a monitor and were so careful with it and it died. We were about the have another baby and I didn't want to dish out another few hundred for a monitor that was rated worse than this one. As a last resort I decided to reach out to the company.
I cannot say enough good things about them. I talked with Renee and she was quick to respond and help me troubleshoot. Her responses were professional and timely. I knew I was out of the warranty time period so I didn't expect them to do anything. After discussing and troubleshooting, Renee said that our monitor and battery were faulty and she offered to replace the monitor and battery for free! I shipped back the monitor I had and received the new one within a few days of shipping mine out.
I connected it to the camera and it works perfectly! Better yet, the new monitor has the silent feature for the alarm which is great, and it looks like they replaced the charging cable and it is much more secure. I have only had the monitor for a few weeks but we have had no problems with it.
I am so impressed by this company and their customer service. They went above and beyond when they didn't have to. I think it is rare to find such customer service these days. I highly recommend this monitor for not only being a good quality monitor, but for their excellent customer service. I'm so happy we purchased this monitor and I will be able to use it through both my kids and hopefully beyond!

[[VIDEOID:bf594da15699d8503e52b57a500537ba]] Bit of background: I've nursed all my kids (4) ranging from 12 days to 2yrs. With my previous child I worked full time and used an Elvie as my main pump and nursed at home. This time around knowing what works for me I purchased another Elvie. But knowing I need a back up because mom brain has had me forget parts before, I began searching for a back up wearable pump that would be comparable without costing another 500+. I found this one which is currently already under 100 for a single, and with a half off coupon came out to under 45 so I decided to give it a try. The Haimmy pump comes with everything included (see pictures). My favorite things about are the auto shut off display, once you turn it on (hold on button for 2 seconds) it'll display battery, suction level and then after a few seconds shut off so you don't have the forever dreded iron man boobs like with the elvie. Also it comes with silicone inserts to make the flange smaller! I always need a 21mm, and this pump has the option of a 24/21/19mm insert, since the flange itself is a 28mm. For the elvie I had to purchase the inserts separately. What I dislike the most about the pump is that is isn't as quiet as the elvie, it makes about as much noise as a spectra (I've used the s1 and s9). Also if you're an "every single drop counts" mama like me, because I make just enough milk, no filling fridges over here, this pump is going to drive you nuts with the amount the stays behind in the bottle. I included pictures and video of this, I tried and tried and the flat top of the bottle just made it impossible to get that last sizable drop out so it was sacrifices to the dish water gods. Overall, I do not regret the purchase, I prefer wearable pumps to conventional because of my work, and my hatred for the bottles dangling in front of me. If I could not have afforded the elvie this is definitely the pump I would've purchased. Will I buy a second one to have the pair? Honestly, I'm considering it, maybe if it goes half off again lol. In the meantime this single will serve as my backup. As with any wearable pump, they're as "discreet" as you get, still comically large looking boobs, but not significantly more than with the elvie. See picture, right boob is Haimmy left is Elvie. I used it for like 5min and got about 1.5oz, the measurements were accurate, they're just barely visible on the front of the bottle, vs the elvie that has them printed along the back of the bottle.

Pros:
Auto shut off display, inserts included, easy assembly and disassembly (the peices stay together, elvies don't), no bottle release buttons where nipples are like with the elvie, C charger which is not more universal than the elvie micro USB, the manual includes a very useful guide and cut out to help you measure your nipples so you know you're using the right size (if you will be pumping regularly this is essential) , and of course the cost. Added: battery life better than the expensive pump as well.

Cons:
A little on the loud side, the bottle does hold on to a decent amount of milk, personally the suction was a little on the strong side, I would not be able to go past level 1 (there's 9) but this is not a deal breaker 1 was still comfortable for me. One concern I have is how would I go about getting replacement parts for this when the time comes.

If you're looking for a wearable pump, cannot spend 500+, and you don't like having the big control display sticking out of your bra, and want to avoid the hoses, get this pump!

I originally tried these diapers from a sample they were endorsing on facebook. I fell in love with the diaper since the first one was used. This is a premium brand hence the shortage of diapers for the price point.

Pros:
Thinner diaper so less bulk
Soft
Longer tabs with a belly button cut out
No fragrance
Has a reasonable volume absorbency

Cons:
Expensive for a lack of diapers

In comparison to other value diapers like Huggies snug & dry, these are far softer. They are less bulky. They also have no scents or fun prints. Lack of prints is fine by me in that such doesn't effect the performance of the diaper. To date since using BabyCozy, we have no experienced any blowouts unless the diaper was too small since it takes a week in shipping to receive a new box. This diaper also holds two-three pees ( over night ) quite well.

If I had to compare to another "luxury" diaper I would go with the Target exclusive of Millie Moon brand. Both function the same with a similar design however Millie has more bulk on them and some designs. They are my back-up brand when I need something today and not next week. Diaper count per box is the same which last 3-4 weeks max but closer to three and a half weeks.

My child is able to move around in these comfortably since she is crawling. She also hasn't experienced any rash from the diaper.

Overall for my family this is an excellent diaper. It's just quite expensive but it makes sense given all the research that went into the design and how comfortable it is on a baby.

I'm slightly sorry to add another 5 star log to the fire, but I really do love this pillow. Before I purchased it, I was having trouble getting a decent night's sleep with any number of other pillows, blankets, stuffed animals, etc. all packed around my body, between my arms and legs, and under my neck. I didn't want to like such an expensive pillow that looks so ridiculous on the bed, but it's been fantastic. I'm 5'6" and 32 weeks pregnant, and I can wrap the top end under my neck and cuddle it with my arms while still having the bottom end between my legs and under my stomach.

For the first time in my life, I am sleeping without covers or sheets over me because my stomach feels protected by the pillow. However, it may also be keeping me very warm at night - my husband gets all cuddled up under the covers because I have to have the AC on to keep cool enough to sleep. It never occurred to me that the pillow might be the culprit until I read some of the other reviews. Either way, it's well worth the temperature adjustment.

As one other reviewer mentioned, it can be a bit of a struggle to turn over at night. I've got a routine going for when I want to lie on my right side for a while, but it takes some effort to unlace the pillow from between my legs and then redo it. Also, getting out of the bed to go to the bathroom when the pillow is between you and the edge of the bed can be challenging. The loose end of the pillow once flopped out and knocked my glass of water onto the floor, thus making sleep difficult for a while as I cleaned up.

All told, I really do love this pillow, and it's going to be tough for me to give it up when pregnancy's over and I don't have an excuse to let it take up half the bed anymore. In the meantime, I'm going to keep snuggling for all it's worth and appreciating that I'm a rare pregnant woman without trouble sleeping.

These are excellent cups for little ones.  The lid of the cup snaps snugly onto the rim of the cup such that you can't push up on the lid to remove it from the cup (because when you push up, you're actually pushing up on the rim of the cup, not the lid).  This is excellent to stop curious little ones from spilling.  (To remove the lid I find it easiest to apply a little pressure to the cup's 'spout', then the lid separates from the edge of the cup.)  Also, the holes in the spout are small enough that even when tipped over (or held upside down) water doesn't leak out.  I feel safe enough with these cups to let the kids have them in bed - not one has accidentally popped open, or leaked in bed yet!  If I had to come up with a flaw, I'd say that the holes in the spout are so tiny that it takes a decent bit to drain the cup by drinking, but I'd rather have small holes than big leaky ones.  Overall, excellent cups.  Great purchase!

We started out as most new parents with an infant carrier and that worked great until around 3 months. By then she was getting to be too heavy for me to carry. So we moved on to an infant toddler car seat...the Triumph by Evenflo. The seat was great for a few month but then as you got taller we started having problems. She would scream when it was time to buckle and we would struggle to get enough strap to get her buckled. When she turned 1 and became a forward facer we headed back to the fire department to get the seat adjusted and they advised us to get her a new one.

The reasons were very clear...at 1 year old, 32 inches tall and 25 pounds she had already outgrown it and she was not safe in it. The straps either had to come out of the seat above her ears our below her shoulders and given the right accident they said she would be killed from the car seat alone. They told us that an infant to toddler seat just cannot work. They said sheer dynamics of an infant verses a toddler and rear verses forward facing makes designing a seat to do it all nearly impossible. They told us in the future we would be better off and safer with an infant seat and then spending the most money on a toddler to booster seat...something like this one.

But I had learned enough from the first two seats to know we needed to play and try them out in the store before we bought them. This was the first seat we tested and she loved it. The second I put her in it she sat up tall and proud. It was easy to adjust and buckle and for the first time she actually wanted to get buckled!

The shoulder straps and buckle can both be adjusted rather easily. And it is easily secured with either the LATCH system or with the regular seatbelt. The cup holder is a great feature and she loves having her cup at her finger tips. She also loves the arm rests! It is so cute to look back to see her little legs crossed and her arm propped on that arm rest as she looks out the window...it's one of those priceless kind of moments.

The only complaints I have is that the recline is pretty much useless. Once the fire department secured that thing it was NOT reclining. Once they get it tight enough to be safe then there is no real room left for it to slide and recline. So that is kind of disappointing because her poor little head falls forward when she falls asleep. Also we had a couple of sippy cup accidents and the cover needed washed...good luck getting it loose! The thing doesn't appear to come off she was have a couple of nice stains that I can't get to budge with just spot cleaning. But other than that it is a great seat and she loves it...so much so that we bought one for each grandma to have in her car!

I bought an earlier version of the InStep Safari Swivel Wheel Double Jogger when my second child was born in 2006, so I can speak to its longevity more than some other reviewers. I have used it very heavily for a full five years, and a total of four children (plus those I babysit). I've subjected it to some harsher conditions than usual.

It is my primary "vehicle", since I do not drive, and is used at least 2 miles a day. It is used outdoors 99% of the time. I live near the beach, and bring it on the sand. I fill the bottom basket with library books, jugs of water, bags of garden soil, you name it! When my 3yo gets tired, I let her sit on what we call the "front step" (i.e. the foot rest), so the stroller is carrying three children. My children are also tall and heavy for their age, and I've allowed them to ride in it up to 4 years old.

My children have always been comfortable in the stroller. It reclines nicely for when they're sleeping, and sits up for when they're awake so they can look around. I haven't tried jogging with it, so can't speak to that. While walking, it is extremely easy to push. I've been in a situation where I am wearing a baby in a sling, holding an umbrella with one hand, and pushing the double stroller with the other. It maneuvers wonderfully!

Despite all this wear and tear, the stroller has held up magnificently. We were in a car accident, with the stroller in the back of the van, and the frame got bent. That is the only reason I am replacing this stroller, and I am replacing it with its duplicate. I am happy to see some updates in the 2012 model, like the improved sun shades and addition of cup holders.

Now, if you're going to be folding up the stroller in the trunk of a small car, and using it primarily for shopping, this stroller is not for you. This stroller is for someone more active who spends a good deal of time outdoors, in a variety of terrains.

I hope those with an active lifestyle like me enjoy this stroller as much as I do!

I have loved this monitor - 3 people in my family have one now and we all love it. I have had mine for 3 years and it still works like brand new. I am extremely clumsy and have dropped the parent unit countless times. It has dings as a result but it's functions have never been negatively affected by the falls.

The parent unit will stay charged when unplugged for 6-8 hrs and it notifies you with a recurring beep when the charge is running out. I do wish the child unit could be unplugged and work on battery, but it must be plugged in to work. I like that the cords are interchangeable so they work for either the child or parent unit.

The range is excellent- I can go anywhere in my 6000sq foot house and not go out of range. I can even go outside in my front or back yard. Huge bonus! I love that it let's you know when you are out of range (using a beeping sequence) so I'm not constantly wondering if I'll be able to hear my child.

I love that you can change the sensitivity and volume, use it to talk to your child, and use the child unit as a night light. The light is a very dim yellow so don't expect it to give much light, but sometimes the small glow is just what I want. It picks up even the smallest sounds my kids makes if the sensitivity is high.

There are other fancy listening monitors but this one is amazing and affordable.
